title: Glossary
text:
This page collects all terms introduced in the Conceptual Model. Hover over any glossary-highlighted term elsewhere on this site to see its definition.
For the full context in which each term is introduced, follow the cross-references to the relevant section of the conceptual model.

title: Glossary
text:
A

Accolade

One line of a page of music (a system), read from left to right: one horizontal piece of the page’s Time path, and the Timeline along it. An accolade is as long as its piece, states the area of the image it stands for in meta["box"] and the image in meta["image"], and holds the Boxes of the areas lying on it. A page is the SegmentLine of its accolades, a volume the segment line of its pages; neither states an area. TimeAxisPath.from_boxes() finds the accolades among the areas of a page given in reading order: a box begins a new accolade when its left edge lies left of the previous box’s by more than half the span of all left edges (group_into_accolades). See How to Represent Areas of Page Images as Boxes.

AlignmentAnchor

A coordinate pair associating one coordinate on timeline A with one on timeline B; a neutral record with no claim semantics—provenance is carried by the enclosing MatchClaim. Only synchronous MatchClaims produce AlignmentAnchors. From a MatchClaim of TimeIntervalEvents, one derives a StartAnchor and an EndAnchor. See Alignment.

AlignmentBundle

A collection of TimelineGroups with inter-group MatchClaim connections; provides coordinate transfer via offset arithmetic, interpolation, and WarpMaps. See Alignment.

AlignmentMatrix

An audio-to-audio alignment in which several recordings of one work are each warped onto a single shared, equidistant reference grid. Per recording, a parallel onset-time array gives that recording’s clock-time at each grid column; because every array indexes the same grid they are equal length, so together they form a dense matrix of shape (recordings × grid columns). A single such file encodes an entire MatchGraph directly — every pair of recordings is related at every grid column — rather than only one score-to-performance correspondence. The complete pairwise claim set is held in a MatchClaimField. See Alignment.

Archive member

A file inside a ZIP archive, named by the standard library’s zipfile.Path (the archive and the member’s path inside it). Every loader reads an archive member wherever it reads a path, without extracting the archive; a loader whose parser needs a file on disk reads the copy materialize() makes once in a cache. A string is always a filesystem path, never a member. A loader’s metadata["sources"] records a member as the archive’s absolute path plus member, its path inside the archive. See How to Load Data.

Atomic section

A stretch of a Timeline’s axis that its flow control never divides: an interval between consecutive coordinates of its Jumps, JumpTargets, Breaks and SectionBreaks and the places their Destinations go on at, named by a letter (A, B, …, Z, AA, …) in the order of the axis. Every flow is a sequence of atomic sections. Timeline.create_flow_maps_from_flow_control() writes them as Regions stating the type tts:AtomicSection, and the computed FlowMaps list them. See How to Encode and Play Flow Control.

title: Glossary
text:
B

BeatGrid

An ordered set of BeatGridSegments and the beats they generate on a seconds axis. Each segment states one stretch of a recording — an anchor instant, a tempo, a BeatPolicy, and which beat of a bar the anchor is — and generates beats without end; the grid orders the segments, bounds each by its successor’s start and the last by its extent, and labels the resulting beats with measure and beat numbers. Each labelled beat is a GridBeat. A BeatGrid is not a Timeline and stores nothing per beat. See How to Build Beat Grids.

BeatPolicy

How one bar is counted in beats: a grouping cycle over one counted note value. A 4/4 bar is four beats of a quarter, a compound 6/8 bar two beats of three eighths, an uneven (3+2+3)/8 bar three beats of unequal length. Beat lengths are derived from the grouping and the division, never stored. One signature admits more than one counting: a BeatGrid’s lattice reads 6/8 as six beats of an eighth, because its beat-in-bar index counts the notated value rather than the felt pulse.

BoundingBox

An axis-aligned area of an image: x, y, width and height (the xywh of IIIF and Media Fragments), in image space (origin the image’s top-left corner, x right, y down), all four in one unit and one number type; width and height are never negative. A shape, as is Quadrilateral: built with from_xywh(), from_corners() (MEI’s ulx, uly, lrx, lry) or from_media_fragment(), and written with to_dict(), as_media_fragment(), as_svg_points() and as_mei_zone(). Its numbers are never rounded: a value the axis cannot hold exactly (385.5 on pixels) is refused. Every shape has a bounding box, the smallest BoundingBox holding it. See How to Represent Areas of Page Images as Boxes.

Box

An area of an image as an interval event of a graphical Timeline running along a horizontal piece of the image’s Time path, such as an Accolade of a page. A Box holds exactly one shape, a BoundingBox or a Quadrilateral, in the image’s space, and the interval of the shape’s x extent on its timeline: start is the shape’s x_min less the x at which the timeline stands in its image (the x of its meta["box"], 0 where it states none), duration is x_max − x_min. Box.from_shape(shape, origin=, id=) makes it; adding a Box whose interval contradicts its shape, or whose shape is on another unit or number type than the timeline, is refused on every path that adds events, a package read included. DmosLoader and MeiFacsimileLoader read Boxes onto the accolades of their pages and name them with box_ids; an AlignmentBundle’s to_file() writes every timeline’s Boxes beside the manifest in one table, boxes.parquet, named in its resources with the type Box (see Resource), and from_file() reads them back. See How to Represent Areas of Page Images as Boxes.

Barline

A Flow control element recording a barline the source prints (a double or a final barline). It changes nothing in the flow. See How to Encode and Play Flow Control.

Break

A Flow control element at which the flow does not go on: when the flow plays up to it, a Jump at the same coordinate with a Destination that holds is taken, otherwise the flow ends there and begins again at the next SectionBreak, if any. With ends (a condition: passes, after) it ends the flow only while that condition holds, as a Fine does after a D.C. or D.S. A Break lies between two brackets of alternative endings. See How to Encode and Play Flow Control.

title: Glossary
text:
C

Catalogue

Data shipped with the TimeToShare package that guides the writing of statements and that tools read to offer properties and values and to print pairs in words: the prefixes of the vocabularies its patterns use, from which a written manifest’s inline @context takes those its statements use; aliases, namespaces read as equal (https://schema.org/ as http://schema.org/); the identifier systems (Wikidata, MusicBrainz, the GND, VIAF, MeLODy with LRMoo, IMSLP and others, and the fallback vocabularies that state a relation where a system has no property of its own); the verbs, relations in words (is_a, performed_by, part_of, …) each with a pattern per system; and the types of thing a subject or value is. The validators never consult it. add_verb() states a verb in one system’s vocabulary, and get_rectangles() gathers the pairs it reads as one verb about one thing. See How to Describe What a Bundle and Its Timelines Stand For and TimeToShare’s description of a manifest, section 10.

ChainMap

A MultiMap that applies multiple ConversionMaps in sequence, creating a conversion path from a source unit to a target unit. See Conversion maps.

Child

A Timeline nested within a parent, sharing its measuring unit but defining its own origin. add_child() locks a child by default, which prevents side effects from modifications. An unlocked child’s length may change only within its parent’s known length: a parent never grows because a child grew. A child holds its parent’s positions from its start up to its end, and its end only where no sibling starts there; a nested timeline is reached only through parents that all hold the position. A child created with measures=True holds the slice of its parent’s measure map over its span; by default it holds none. See Nested timelines.

CHUNK

A sentinel value in a synchronous MatchClaim for a side whose coordinate the claim states without an event: the claim’s AlignmentAnchors hold the coordinate (its start, and its end for a span), and no event or Projection is added. A synchronous claim between two bare positions is CHUNK on both sides; MatchClaim.from_events() also takes a position on one side only. The MatchClaim table writes it as CHUNK_SENTINEL in the side’s event ID column; in code it is the constant CHUNK, and MatchClaim.chunk_sides lists the timelines of a claim’s CHUNK sides. Unrelated to the chunks of a FlowMap, the stretches it plays. See Alignment Bundles and MatchClaims.

ClaimType

The semantic kind of a MatchClaim, derived from its structure rather than stored — read from whether the claim is synchronous and whether both of its sides name an event or one names the NOMATCH sentinel. Each side of a MatchClaim names an event or a sentinel: a side without an event of its own is given a Projection, except on a synchronous claim between two bare positions, which is CHUNK on both sides. Three members: event_match (synchronous, an event or CHUNK on each side; the case that yields AlignmentAnchors), nomatch (non-synchronous, one event and the sentinel on the other side; see NOMATCH), and conceptual (non-synchronous, an event on each side — a structural correspondence with no temporal commitment). What a MatchGraph infers through groups is the graph’s own inferred edge and has no kind here. See Alignment.

CombinationMap

A MultiMap yielding outputs from multiple ConversionMaps simultaneously (e.g., (x, y) coordinate pairs). See Conversion maps.

Commensurability

Two timelines are commensurable if connected by a chain of ConversionMaps, membership in the same TimelineGroup, or cross-group MatchClaims, enabling coordinate translation between them. See Alignment.

Commensurable

See Commensurability.

Complete form

The form in which to_dict(minimal=False) writes a TimeToShare manifest: every key the format defines is written, those holding their default value included (null, {}, []). A key whose default is its absence, such as a manifest’s id or a root timeline’s offset, is written only when it has a value. The complete and the Minimal form of one object read back to equal objects, and each writes back to itself. See How to Save and Load Timelines, Groups and Bundles.

ConcatenationMap

A MultiMap combining bounded ConversionMaps such that each coordinate region is handled by a specific map. See Conversion maps.

Contiguity

A TimeInterval is contiguous if it monotonically spans all coordinates between its start and end. An Instant is contiguous with a TimeInterval if it is synchronous with its EndInstant. See Flow control.

ConversionMap

A typed function attached to a Timeline that maps each coordinate to exactly one value (coordinate, label, or filename); also permits inverse conversion back to the timeline’s own unit. Also called C-map. See Conversion maps.

Coordinate

A position on a Timeline, expressed as the distance from the origin in the timeline’s measuring unit. Combines a numeric value with a TimeUnit. The unit alone decides the number policy: quarters and beats are exact Fractions, discrete units (ticks, samples, frames, pixels) are locked to int, and the remaining continuous units (seconds, points, centimeters, …) are float. That declared number type is preserved at every boundary — authored, converted, offset-computed, interpolated, queried or retrieved — so a fraction-canonical axis always yields Fractions and a float-canonical axis always yields floats. An explicit number_type= overrides the default, and exact input is never degraded. See Foundations.

title: Glossary
text:
D

Destination

One place a Jump may go on at, and when: a JumpDestination. Its place is to (the element id of a JumpTarget, a Region, a child timeline or the timeline itself), by (a signed distance from the Jump; by: 0 is going on and is never taken) or neither (the start of its section). Its conditions all must hold: passes (the arrivals at the Jump that count), repeat_count (taken at most that often), after (another Jump’s destination must have been taken) and determined (false for a choice nobody can check, such as an ossia, which is never taken). reset says whether going back restores the Jumps and Breaks gone back over, as a repeat does; a D.C. or D.S. played without repeats states reset: false. See How to Encode and Play Flow Control.

DictStore

A generic EventStore subclass holding a dict[str, EventData] with arbitrary keys. Used internally by AlignmentLoaders to store one EventData table per timeline-to-be (e.g., "score:clt_…", "perf:Chopin_op10_no3_p01:cpt_…"). Maintains the uniform EventStore interface. See the API reference.

Discrete

A timeline is discrete when coordinates exist only at discrete points (e.g., pixels, samples, ticks). Contrast with Continuous timelines where coordinates can take any real value (e.g., seconds, quarters). See Foundations.

Domain

One of three temporal categories: Graphical (visual/spatial), Logical (symbolic/musical), or Physical (audio/sound). Each domain has both discrete and continuous timeline variants. See Foundations.

title: Glossary
text:
E

element id

The id that identifies an element of a manifest: the manifest’s own, a Timeline (root or descendant), TimelineGroup, MeasureMap, ConversionMap at any nesting depth, Region, Flow control element, FlowMap, Virtual timeline or Resource. It is unique across the whole manifest and every kind, so the id alone names the element. An id is free: whatever was given is kept verbatim, any non-empty string without a control character; spaces, colons, slashes and URIs are allowed, and no word is reserved. Only an element given no id gets a minted one, when it is constructed: a prefix, _ and 13 random base-36 characters (region_3kq9x0m2ztb7a). The characters are seeded, so a run repeats them: a loader seeds from the bytes it reads, an object built in code from its content, and a seed= argument makes them exact. The prefix names the kind: clt, dlt, cpt, dpt, cgt or dgt for a timeline (continuous or discrete, logical, physical or graphical), group for a group, measure_map for a MeasureMap, cmap for a conversion map, region for a Region, resource for a Resource, jump, jump_target, break, section_break or barline for a flow-control element and flow for a FlowMap; a virtual timeline is minted as a timeline of its unit; a loader role leads it (score:clt_…). An id is never renamed: when trees are joined into a group or bundle, an id held twice is refused, minted or given alike, for every kind of element, before anything changes. The id identifies, the name displays: a name may be absent or repeat, and an id is never derived from it.

EndInstant

An Instant marking the end of a TimeInterval. Its coordinate must be greater than or equal to the corresponding StartInstant’s coordinate. See Foundations.

Event

Anything associated with a Timeline via Instants. An InstantEvent has zero duration; a TimeIntervalEvent has duration defined by start and end coordinates. See Foundations.

title: Glossary
text:
F

Finding

What playing flow control found, without raising: a flow that never ends (endless_loop), a flow ending at a Break that states no condition before the end (flow_ends_at_break), two Destinations of one Jump holding at once (ambiguous_targets), a destination nobody can check (undetermined_target), and a stretch never played (never_played). The default and single flows have findings, the printed flow none; Timeline.get_flow(convention) returns them with the flow. A finding may name its cause (FlowFinding.cause, a FlowFindingCause): a stretch the single flow leaves out that the default flow plays has the cause single_playback (going through once takes the last volta ending). See How to Encode and Play Flow Control.

Flow control element

One of the elements a Timeline holds as its flow control (a manifest’s flow_control array): a Jump, a JumpTarget, a Break, a SectionBreak or a Barline. Each lies at one coordinate and has an element id; how it looks in the source is its manifestation, which decides nothing. An element is never changed or deleted to repair flow control: an actor’s belief "false" rejects it (flow_control.with_belief()), and the right one is added. Timeline.get_flow() plays the elements no actor rejects. See How to Encode and Play Flow Control.

FlowMap

One order in which stretches of one root Timeline are played: an ordered list of chunks, each the ID of a Region, a child timeline or a Virtual timeline of that timeline’s tree, or a Gap in which nothing of the timeline is played. A FlowMap holds no interval; resolved against its timeline (resolve()) it places each stretch where the one before it ends and converts positions both ways: unfold() takes a position of the timeline to every position it is played at, fold() a position of the flow to the position it plays, or None in a gap. Timeline.create_flow_map(chunks) creates and attaches one; Timeline.create_flow_maps_from_flow_control() writes the flows of the flow control (default, single, printed) as FlowMaps over the Atomic sections. See How to Encode and Play Flow Control.

title: Glossary
text: G

title: Glossary
text:
I

IdCoordinate

A Coordinate that also names the Timeline it belongs to. It is the default return of every coordinate getter in the library — stamps, timelines, groups, bundles, match lines, graphs and warp maps all hand back IdCoordinate(value, unit, timeline_id) unless an explicit format= asks for something else. Carrying identity is what lets a retrieved coordinate be handed straight back as a query without restating which axis it came from. An IdCoordinate never compares equal to a plain Coordinate in either direction; use format="coordinate" when timeline identity should be discarded. See Foundations.

Instant

Associates a Coordinate (a “time-point”) with a signification such as “start of event e”. Instants sharing a coordinate are synchronous. See Foundations.

InstantEvent

An Event defined by a single Instant, having zero duration. See Foundations.

Interval

A frozen scalar pairing two plain Coordinates as a half-open span [start, end): the start is inclusive, the end exclusive. Both endpoints must share one TimeUnit and one number type, which makes the interval’s own unit and number_type unambiguous; its duration is exactly end - start, returned as a Duration. Reversed intervals raise; zero-length ones are valid. It renders through the same formatter the scalars use, so an interval on a quarters axis prints [1/2, 3/2) quarters rather than [0.5, 1.5). Interval is the scalar leaf of interval retrieval: TimeIntervalStamp.get_interval() and TimelineGroup.get_interval_for() both return one. See Nested timelines.

IntervalField

The SemanticField paired with Interval. It stores a struct of start and end coordinate structs under one unit, domain, and number_type metadata triple, materialises Interval | None per row, and exposes vectorized start, end, and duration accessors returning CoordinateField, CoordinateField, and DurationField. See Nested timelines.

InverseMap

The reverse transformation of a bijective ConversionMap. See Conversion maps.

title: Glossary
text:
J

Jump

A Flow control element where the flow may leave the axis, holding one Destination for every place it may go on at: a repeat end, a D.C., a D.S., a To Coda and the brackets of alternative endings at one coordinate are destinations of one Jump. When the flow plays up to it, of the destinations that hold one is taken (one going back with reset first, then one going back without, then one ahead, the nearest first); when none holds, the flow goes on. See How to Encode and Play Flow Control.

JumpTarget

A Flow control element marking a place a Destination names by its element id: a repeat start, a segno, a coda, a bracket. Nothing happens when the flow plays up to it. See How to Encode and Play Flow Control.

title: Glossary
text:
L

Length

The distance between a Timeline’s origin and its last Instant, or None when it is not known (see Unknown length). See Foundations.

Locked

A timeline state that fixes its coordinate axis: no Instants may be added after the last time-point, so its length cannot change. Locking governs the coordinate axis only — non-structural annotations such as Regions may still be added to a locked timeline. A timeline is locked with locked=True, when add_child() embeds it as a Child with its default locked=True, or after construction with lock(); a child read from a manifest keeps the manifest’s locked. A lock cannot be lifted. A locked timeline’s length may still be unknown. On a locked timeline, setting length, append_child() and append_segment() raise RuntimeError, and content, a child or a MatchClaim position (AlignmentBundle.create_match_claims()) past its end is refused with a ValueError before anything is added, unless add_events() or add_child() is given allow_expansion=True; create_child_from_region() gives a child of any region within its length. A loader locks a timeline whose source states its length: AudioLoader a recording at the file’s length, a score loader a score whose measures all state their length, at the end of its last measure or of its last event, whichever is later. Containment does not depend on the lock: a child, locked or not, ends within its parent’s known length, and content or a child added into an unlocked timeline grows that timeline only. See Nested timelines.

title: Glossary
text:
M

Match

See MatchClaim.

MatchfileLoader

Loader for Vienna Match (.match) alignment files. Uses the standard two-step load() → create_*() pattern. A single instance processes all .match files that share the same score, building a shared score timeline on the first file and verifying subsequent files against it. Returns an AlignmentBundle directly via create_bundle(). Score goes into its own group; performances are standalone timelines; MatchClaims connect score to performances. See the API reference.

MatchClaim

A claim of equivalence between two events on different timelines, each coordinate on its own timeline’s axis, with its Provenance (how it was made and who believes it) and a certainty. A side without an event of its own is given a Projection, or is the sentinel CHUNK on a synchronous claim stated from positions. May be synchronous (producing AlignmentAnchors) or not: conceptual (structural equivalence without temporal commitment) or NOMATCH (an event on one side, the sentinel on the other). A MatchClaim is always stated: what a MatchGraph infers through groups is the graph’s own (its inferred edges), never a MatchClaim. A person stating claims is recorded as believing them "true" (create_match_claims(..., actor=)). A claim is never deleted: who disagrees records a belief "false" in it (AlignmentBundle.add_match_claim_belief()), and every reader of claims, the MatchStamp and coordinate getters included, takes the belief filter (believer=, beliefs=; see Provenance). Readers of claims take the same timeline filters: timeline_ids keeps a claim with any of the named timelines on either side, within a claim whose both timelines are in the set. Held individually, or in the bundle’s one MatchClaim table, a MatchClaimField. Its ID never changes: a claim given none is minted one when it is constructed (claim_ and 13 random characters, seeded from the claim’s content or by seed=), and joining an AlignmentBundle mints nothing. A MatchClaim is addressed by its ID alone: a bundle or field already holding an ID refuses a second claim under it, and merging bundles (from_bundles()) refuses, before anything is merged, two sources holding one ID. See Alignment.

MatchClaimField

The MatchClaim table: a columnar, PyArrow-backed store holding a set of MatchClaims of every kind as Arrow columns, one per property of a MatchClaim (the two timeline IDs, the start and end anchors, each holding coordinate_a and coordinate_b only, the row’s timelines being theirs, is_synchronous, the provenance and certainty, the event IDs, each an event’s ID or a sentinel’s string and never null, the event names, and id), rather than as one frozen MatchClaim object per claim; its columns are TimeToShare’s MatchClaim table. Each anchor coordinate is a cell naming its own unit and number_type beside its number. In memory (table) the number keeps both sides, value and the exact numerator / denominator; the package form (package_table, the table to_parquet() writes) writes it once, in the member its number type names (an int as numerator alone, a fraction as numerator and denominator, a float as value alone), the others null, and from_package_table() reads that form back, refusing a cell that does not stand as its number type says and a null coordinate. A fraction is read in any terms (2/4 is the value 1/2), and a claim gives an end on both sides or on neither. Either way a claim’s coordinate comes back in its axis’s declared number type instead of being flattened on the way through the column. Individual MatchClaims are materialised on demand when a row is indexed or iterated. Built vectorized via from_columns(), it is the scalable backing for dense AlignmentMatrix alignments, where the complete pairwise topology of a whole work runs to roughly a million claims, and an AlignmentBundle keeps all its claims in one, match_claim_table. Shared provenance is held once at field level; only claims whose provenance differs carry it per row. The table property gives the field as an Arrow table, the shared provenance in its schema metadata under the key timetoshare:provenance, and from_table() reads it back unchanged; to_parquet() and from_parquet() write and read match_claims.parquet in the package form. An AlignmentBundle’s to_file() writes its table there, beside the manifest, named in the manifest’s resources (see Resource), and from_file() reads it back; writing over an existing table keeps every claim it holds (the succession rule: same timelines, events and anchors, only the provenance may differ). to_dict() renders the same table as {"provenance": …, "rows": […]}, one mapping per claim keyed by the columns, and from_dict() reads it back. See Alignment and How to Keep MatchClaims, Projections and Beliefs in a Package.

MatchGraph

An auxiliary structure formed by extending MatchClaims through shared coordinates; may be viewed as a hyperedge connecting multiple coordinates from different timelines. Connected components yield MatchStamps. Its edges are the anchors of the synchronous MatchClaims it was given (stated) and those extend_to_groups() infers through TimelineGroup membership (inferred_edges, each naming its group and the claim it comes from); an inferred edge is the graph’s own, never a MatchClaim. filter() keeps the claims the unified filters choose (timeline_id and timeline_ids on either side, within both sides in the set, the belief filter, stated_only for no inferred edges) and rebuilds the graph from them, extended through the same groups. Each Match box M1–M15 in the Hendrix figure is a MatchGraph. See Alignment.

MatchLine

An ordered sequence of AlignmentAnchors derived from MatchClaims, sorted by coordinate on a source timeline; input for WarpMap generation. See Alignment.

MatchPath

A path traversal connecting matched events across multiple timelines (e.g., A -> B -> C), enabling indirect alignment. See Alignment.

MatchStamp

The union of TimeStamps from groups synchronously connected by a MatchGraph. Contains one coordinate per participating timeline. C-map conversion values are opt-in here: unlike TimeStamp, where C-Maps are visible by default, conversion_maps on a MatchStamp getter (bundle.get_matchstamp_at(), get_matchstamps_at(), get_matchstamp_table(), MatchClaim.get_matchstamp()) defaults to False — across a large bundle they would bury the alignment answer. This is a per-context default value for a shared parameter, not a structural difference: MatchStamp implements the same Stamp interface as every other stamp type — get_coordinate_for(timeline_id) returns an IdCoordinate by default and a plain number under format="float"/"int"/"fraction", get_unit() converts through a C-map, get_conversion_for() reads label and structured map values, present_timelines lists available timelines, and is_interpolated identifies interpolation fallback. A stamp from any source keeps the identical structure, methods, and behaviour the Stamp contract guarantees; only the caller-visible default for one keyword argument varies by producing context. within= on a MatchStamp getter (and on MatchStamp.filter_by_timelines()) always keeps the queried timeline and selects among the others; on get_matchstamp_table() and a group’s get_timestamp_table() it selects the table’s columns; the MatchClaims the stamp is read from are chosen by the belief filter (believer=, beliefs=), and a stamp counts apart the timeline pairs a MatchClaim’s anchor links and those an inferred edge links (n_stated_pairs, n_inferred_pairs). See Alignment.

MeasureConstituent

A measure of a measure map that is only part of its nominal measure: an anacrusis, or one constituent of a split measure. It carries offset_within_measure, the strictly positive quarter-note position at which it begins inside the nominal measure, and is the only measure class that does. A measure is classified as a constituent exactly when that offset is stated and non-zero: a shared measure number never marks a split measure, because alternative endings (“16a”, “16b”) share one too. A measure table states the offset in its mc_offset column; a Measure Map .mm.json file states none, so MeasureMapLoader applies the standard’s one convention, a first row numbered 0 that is shorter than nominal being an anacrusis at offset nominal minus actual length. In a compressed measure-map row the offset is the offset_within_measure extension, written only when non-zero.

MetricMap

A table-based ConversionMap from a quarter position to its measure count, built from explicit measure-boundary anchors rather than a uniform measure length. Correctly handles anacrusis (an incomplete first measure), irregular measures, varying time signatures, and repeat structure. Built directly from a Verovio timemap via MetricMap.from_verovio_timemap(). Not invertible — many quarters map to the same measure. See Conversion maps.

MetricalPositionMap

A CombinationMap pairing a MetricMap with a beat-in-measure map to return a metrical position {mc, beat} from a quarter coordinate. Adds a reverse lookup quarters_at(mc, beat) (metrical position to quarters) and mn_at(quarters) (quarters to measure-number label). A TimeToShare manifest writes it as a MeasureBeatMap over the measure map its meter map describes, each measure’s count standing as its number; reading the manifest returns that MeasureBeatMap. See Conversion maps.

Minimal form

The form in which every to_dict() writes a TimeToShare manifest by default (to_dict(minimal=False) writes the Complete form): every key holding its default value is left out, except a timeline’s length, which both forms write. Readers supply every default left out, so a minimal manifest can be written by hand; the smallest names the version and one timeline with its id, unit and length. to_file() writes a manifest file in the form it was read in, and in the minimal form and canonical YAML for an object not read from a file. See How to Save and Load Timelines, Groups and Bundles.

MpmLoader

Loader for an MPM-Toolbox project: a sibling .msm score, .mpm modelled performance, and .mpr project file (carrying an observed audio-to-score alignment) for one work. Uses the standard two-step load() → create_*() pattern. Builds a shared logical "score" group holding the notes in two units — a ticks Timeline (also carrying every MPM markup event: Tempo, Dynamics, Articulation, …) and a quarters Timeline — with a TicksToQuarters map and a modelled quarters→seconds TableMap integrated from the performance’s tempo markup; and a physical "perf" group of observed onsets in seconds and samples. Emits one synchronous cross-group MatchClaim per score note (the MSM xml:id ↔︎ MPR ref join is a bijection). Reads the modelled performance and the observed alignment; never runs an aligner. Returns an AlignmentBundle via create_bundle().

MultiMap

An umbrella term for composed ConversionMaps: ChainMap (sequential), CombinationMap (parallel outputs), and ConcatenationMap (regional). See Conversion maps.

title: Glossary
text:
N

NOMATCH

A sentinel value in a MatchClaim explicitly encoding the absence of a corresponding event on the other timeline. The MatchClaim records both timeline IDs and names the event of the timeline that has it, but has no AlignmentAnchors; is_synchronous is always False. Written NOMATCH_SENTINEL in the event ID column of the MatchClaim table; in code, the constant NOMATCH, which create_match_claims() takes as the side without an event. See Alignment.

title: Glossary
text:
O

Origin

The zero coordinate of a Timeline, from which all positions are measured. See Foundations.

title: Glossary
text:
P

Package

A TimeToShare manifest and the tables its resources name. A manifest alone with its files beside it is a package of one manifest, which an AlignmentBundle’s to_file() writes and from_file() reads. Several manifests share their tables in a folder whose package.yaml lists the manifests and the tables, each table a file or a folder of Parquet files holding the rows of one type of every manifest naming it. The Package class writes and opens such a folder: write_bundle(bundle, url) adds a bundle as the manifest at url (a new package stages it and to_file(path) writes every bundle staged, then package.yaml; a package on disk is written at once). The Registry is the folder registry/ and the Extraction table the file tables/extractions.parquet; each write adds one file per Pre-parsed table type and one of MatchClaims under tables/<Type>/, holding the rows of every bundle it writes, every event type included, and named from its content. from_file(path) opens a package, and bundle(url) reads one of its manifests with every table filtered to the timelines its resources list. In a package a timeline ID is held by one manifest, an event ID once among the events of every type, and a MatchClaim ID once among its MatchClaims; a collision is refused before anything is written. A manifest written again replaces the old one: its rows leave the files holding them, and its MatchClaims obey the succession rule. After each write the package is checked whole (timetoshare.tables.package_problems), and a problem is raised with every file restored. See the API reference (Package), How to Write the Registry and Share Tables in a Package and TimeToShare’s README, “Packages”.

Parent

A Timeline that contains one or more Child timelines. The parent and all its children must share the same measuring unit. See Nested timelines.

PerformancePrecisionLoader

Loader for audio-to-score alignment specimens: a directory bundling a .solo score, a Verovio timemap, and per-performer alignment files at the note, bar, and beat granularities. Uses the standard two-step load() → create_*() pattern. Resolves every "<measure>+<offset>" label to absolute quarters via a MetricMap, builds one logical score Timeline (quarters) and one physical performance Timeline per recording (seconds), and emits a MatchClaim per alignment row — synchronous for located onsets, NOMATCH for the dangling ones. Returns an AlignmentBundle via create_bundle(). See the API reference.

ParangonadaLoader

Loader for a parangonar parangonada export: per-performance CSV triples (score notes, performed notes, note-level correspondences) for one work. Uses the standard two-step load() → create_*() pattern. Parses the shared score once into two logical Timelines (quarters and division-grid ticks, linked by a divs→quarters LinearMap), builds one performance group per recording with two physical Timelines (seconds and samples, linked by a SamplesToSeconds map), and emits one cross-group MatchClaim per correspondence — synchronous for a matched note, NOMATCH for a score-only or performance-only note. Reads the existing alignment; never runs an aligner. Returns an AlignmentBundle via create_bundle().

Pre-parsed table

A Parquet table holding what is particular to the Events of one type, keyed by their IDs and without positions: a Note’s name, a Projection’s projection_of, a Box’s shape. An event’s ID, type, timeline and position are its Registry row, whose location names the table holding its content. Beside a lone manifest it is a file (Note.parquet; projections.parquet and boxes.parquet for Projections and Boxes); in a Package it is the folder tables/<Type>/, shared by every manifest. An event whose content can be read again from its source file is re-parsed instead and has no row there. An AlignmentBundle’s to_file() writes the tables of the Projections and Boxes its timelines hold, to_file(events=True) one for every other event type as well, and from_file() reads each event’s content when its timeline’s events are first read. See How to Write the Registry and Share Tables in a Package and TimeToShare’s README, “Resources and tables”.

Projection

An event standing on a timeline for an event that timeline does not hold, so that a MatchClaim can join two events: its ID (projection_ and 13 random characters when none is given), its position on the timeline’s own axis (start, and a duration for a span), and projection_of, the event it stands for ({timeline_id, event_id}), or none where no such event is known: the source names an event the package does not hold, a NOMATCH is stated from a position, or a conceptual claim relates two positions. A synchronous claim between two positions adds no Projection: both its sides are CHUNK. Timeline.add_projections() adds Projections, reusing one the timeline already holds for the same event and position; AlignmentBundle.create_match_claims(), the alignment loaders and match_notes_by_attributes() give a Projection to every side stated as a position, except the CHUNK sides. A package holds every timeline’s Projections as rows of the Registry, which hold their positions, and in the Projection table (projections.parquet), the Pre-parsed table of their IDs and projection_of; an AlignmentBundle’s to_file() writes both beside the manifest whenever one of its timelines holds Projections, and from_file() reads them back onto the timelines. In memory a Projection’s start and duration are coordinate cells, each naming its unit and number type; the registry writes them in the package form: the axis’s unit and number_type once per row, each number once, in the member its number type names (see MatchClaimField). A Projection’s ID is unique among all Projections of its manifest: a missing one is minted when the Projection is added, an ID another timeline’s Projection already holds is refused, and no ID is ever renamed, since a MatchClaim may name it. Timelines given Projections apart and joined later may hold one ID twice; writing their package refuses it, naming both timelines. See Alignment Bundles and MatchClaims and How to Keep MatchClaims, Projections and Beliefs in a Package.

Provenance

How an item was made and who believes it, one facility for statements and MatchClaims. Every key is optional, but an entry states at least one: who stated the item (stated_by), the day (date), how (method: manual, reconciled, imported, inferred or an IRI), the lookup service, the sources it rests on (basis), how closely a value matches (match), a note, and beliefs: at most one per actor, "true", "false" or "unlikely", with its date. A person stating an item is recorded as believing it "true"; a loader or a service records how it made the item and believes nothing. A belief never removes an item. The belief filter reads one actor’s beliefs: believer= names the actor, and beliefs= the states kept, any of four: "true", "undecided" (the believer holds no belief on the item), "unlikely" and "false"; the default keeps every state but "false", and without a believer nothing is filtered. Actors compare as the IRIs they stand for under the manifest’s @context, so one believer may be spelled twice in one entry; the entry is then read as the most critical of that believer’s beliefs ("false" before "unlikely" before "true"). For a statement, the entry sits in the provenance beside an element’s statements (or inside a value node, for its own pairs) and names the pair again by property and value; a subject has at most one entry per pair, and a pair without one is stated by the manifest’s publisher. A pair held only as its entry is a candidate: add_candidate() offers one, add_statement() states it, add_belief() records a belief, and get_candidates() and get_provenance() take the belief filter. For a MatchClaim, the entry is the claim’s provenance: create_match_claims(..., actor=) records the stating person’s belief "true", and AlignmentBundle.add_match_claim_belief() records a belief in a claim the bundle holds. See How to Describe What a Bundle and Its Timelines Stand For, Alignment Bundles and MatchClaims and TimeToShare’s description of a manifest, section 9.

title: Glossary
text:
Q

Quadrilateral

An area of an image bounded by four corners, each a Point (x, y), held in the order top_left, top_right, bottom_right, bottom_left (the order SVG polygons and IIIF selectors draw): it follows a measure of a scan whose sides are not upright. A shape, as is BoundingBox. from_points() takes the corners in any order a source writes them, order= naming each one’s role; from_svg_points() reads four SVG or MEI points starting at any corner and running either way. The corners held always run clockwise around a convex outline: from_points() refuses roles that do not, and points that bound no convex quadrilateral are refused, never reordered into one. See How to Represent Areas of Page Images as Boxes.

title: Glossary
text:
R

raw_quarters

The conventional name for the ConversionMap (specifically a ShiftMap) attached to a score timeline. The timeline stores normalised (non-negative) coordinates — shifted so the minimum onset is 0.0 — and this map converts them back to the raw quarter values of the source. Its offset equals min(raw_onsets). Added by MatchfileLoader and PartituraLoader so downstream code can detect and apply the same shift when comparing coordinates across loaders.

Reach

The farthest coordinate on a Timeline’s own axis that its content reaches: the ends of its children (a Child of Unknown length contributing its offset plus its own reach), Region ends, the coordinate of every Flow control element, the place of every Destination stating a distance (by), and the end of the measure map. Events are not part of it. A timeline without such content reaches 0. The reach is independent of the length; displays use it as the extent of a timeline of unknown length. Read it as Timeline.reach.

Region

A part of a Timeline defined by a TimeInterval, identified by its element id and displayed by its name (e.g., “Chorus”, “Verse”). Regions are not timelines and cannot hold events or maps directly. See Regions.

Registry

The Parquet table of every ID a TimeToShare manifest or a Package resolves. An event’s row states its ID, its type (kind), its timeline, its position on the axis of its timeline’s root (start and, for a span, duration, with the axis’s unit and number_type, each number once in the member its number type names), the extraction that made it with its locator in the source, and the location of the Pre-parsed table holding its content. A non-event row names every element of the manifest, every MatchClaim and every extraction, with its kind and location. The registry holds no names. Beside it, the Extraction table has one row per run of a parser over a source file, or of a tool that made events without one. A manifest names the registry among its resources with the type Registry: beside a lone manifest it is registry.parquet, in a package the folder registry/ of non_events.parquet and one part per extraction. resolve(target, id) answers what an ID names, through a manifest or a package root, always as a list. See the API reference (resolve, EventRegistry, Extraction) and How to Write the Registry and Share Tables in a Package.

Resource

An entry of a TimeToShare manifest’s resources, naming a file, or a folder of Parquet files read as one table, that holds data for its timelines: its id (any element id no other element of the manifest holds; an entry the library adds gets a minted resource_…, and an entry read keeps its own when written back), its type (what its rows are: MatchClaim for the MatchClaim table, a MatchClaimField, or Registry for the Registry, whose rows point to the Pre-parsed tables, which no resource names), the IDs of the timelines it holds data for, its url relative to the manifest (a folder when it ends in /, Resource.names_folder), and optionally its media_type, size in bytes and integrity (an Integrity: algorithm and digest; a file’s only). A manifest may name several resources of one type, each listing other timelines. Resource.is_table tells a Table resource from a resource carried with the manifest, such as a recording. A manifest and the files it names make a Package; the manifest reads and draws without them, and names no event. An AlignmentBundle keeps the entries as Resource objects in its resources; from_file() reads every table resource holding events or MatchClaims: a file whole, a folder keeping the rows of the timelines the resource lists (a MatchClaim’s either timeline), since the files of a folder may hold the rows of other manifests of a package; a table of other rows, and a folder holding no Parquet file, is carried as it stands. Its to_file() writes the MatchClaim table when it holds MatchClaims, and the registry, the Extraction table and a pre-parsed table per type for the Projections and Boxes its timelines hold, and with events=True for every other event type its timelines hold as well. It refuses, with a NotImplementedError, to write rows of a type whose resource names a folder: the files of a folder are shared by a package’s manifests, and Package.write_bundle() writes into them. A named file or folder that is absent is not read and its entry is kept. See the API reference (Resource, Integrity), How to Keep MatchClaims, Projections and Beliefs in a Package, How to Write the Registry and Share Tables in a Package and TimeToShare’s README, “Resources and tables”.

Root

The top-level Timeline in a hierarchy of nested timelines. No parent bounds its length; an unlocked descendant grows only within its parent’s known length, never pushing its parent. See Nested timelines.

RotationMap

A periodic ConversionMap that wraps coordinates cyclically (e.g., an ostinato part that repeats while the main timeline advances). See Conversion maps.

title: Glossary
text:
S

ScoreNote

A note or rest of a score: a Note written on a staff and in a voice. staff and voice are the source’s numbers (an MEI <staff> and <layer>, a MuseScore staff and voice); a performance states neither, so a Note has no staff and no voice. Every other member, the pitch among them, is the Note’s. The score loaders write their notes as rows of event type Note; get_field(ScoreNote) on such rows reads them back as ScoreNotes where the table states an integer staff and voice, and get_field(Note) reads the same rows as Notes. See Foundations.

SectionBreak

A Flow control element where a section ends (a movement, a section of a piece); the flow goes on across it. A Destination without place goes on at the nearest SectionBreak before its Jump, and a flow ended by a Break begins again at the next one. See How to Encode and Play Flow Control.

Segment

A Child timeline that is contiguous with its siblings. Segments enable concatenation of local coordinate systems. See Nested timelines.

SegmentLine

A runtime class parameterized by its segment class, such as SegmentLine[DiscreteGraphicalTimeline], whose contiguous Segments tile its full length. A line is also an instance of that segment class. Any timeline can check the structure with the property is_segment_line and adopt enforcement with as_segment_line(); a line returns to an unenforced timeline with to_timeline(); both return a copy. Use create_children_from_boundaries() for boundary-driven tiling. Appending extends an unlocked line, while appending to a locked line raises RuntimeError. The segments of a line of known length keep ending at its length: a segment with a successor ends at the successor’s offset, the last one at the line’s end, and changing a segment’s length never moves the line’s end. A segment of unknown length ends at its successor’s offset, or, the last one, at the line’s known length. See Nested timelines.

StartInstant

An Instant marking the start of a TimeInterval. See Foundations.

Statement

A property–value pair saying what an element of a manifest stands for or how that thing relates to others. Three kinds of element carry statements: the manifest (the AlignmentBundle), which names the work it is about by schema:about; every Timeline at any depth, for the manifestation it is the axis of; and every Region, for the stretch it marks. A group carries none, and works and expressions are values, never elements. The property is type (“is a”) or an IRI, compact (prefix:suffix, the prefix declared by the manifest’s inline @context) or absolute; the value is a literal, a value object, a node (a thing, {id: …}, with its own pairs) or an ordered list. A value naming an element is its reference, {id: "#cpt_1"}; the library renames it with the element and drops the pair when the element leaves the manifest. Statements never nest, order or align timelines. A timeline and a bundle change them in place (add_statement(), add_verb(), remove_statement()), a frozen region returns a copy (with_statement(), without_statement()); each pair may carry a provenance entry. MeiHeadLoader and MelodyLoader import them from an MEI header and from MeLODy’s Turtle. See How to Describe What a Bundle and Its Timelines Stand For and TimeToShare’s description of a manifest.

SupportPolicy

How a cross-timeline MatchStamp treats a timeline whose transferred coordinate falls outside alignment support — the entering coordinate lies beyond the transferring WarpMap’s anchor hull, or the produced coordinate would fall outside the target timeline’s [0, length] span. omit (the default) drops that timeline; clamp reports the nearest in-support boundary coordinate; extrapolate keeps the linear extrapolation clipped to [0, length]. No policy ever yields a negative coordinate, and the queried timeline’s own coordinate is never altered. Set per call on AlignmentBundle.get_matchstamp_at(..., support_policy=...) or persistently via AlignmentBundle.support_policy. See Alignment.

Synchrony

Strict synchrony: Instants sharing identical coordinates. Pragmatic synchrony: Instants binned together based on a threshold (e.g., for quantisation). See Foundations.

title: Glossary
text:
T

Table resource

A Resource of a TimeToShare manifest that names a table, by the format’s one rule (timetoshare.tables.is_table_resource, which Resource.is_table asks): its type is MatchClaim or Projection, its url names a folder (ends in /) or a Parquet file (ends in .parquet), or its media_type is application/vnd.apache.parquet. In a Package each names a table of package.yaml of its type; any other resource (a recording, an image, a score file) is carried with its manifest. An AlignmentBundle reads a table resource into its timelines where it holds events (the columns id, timeline_id, unit, number_type and start) or MatchClaims; a table of other rows is carried as it stands. See TimeToShare’s README, “Packages”.

Time path

The line a reader follows through an image (TimeAxisPath). No image has a time axis until its path is defined: a Timeline of an image runs along the path and is as long as it. A path converts between its coordinate and the image’s (x, y) with to_2d() and from_2d(). HorizontalLinePath, VerticalLinePath, DiagonalLinePath and ParametricPath are single lines; a PiecewisePath is made of consecutive pieces, such as the Accolades of a page, each starting where the ones before it end. TimeAxisPath.from_boxes() makes the path of a page from the areas drawn on it. DmosLoader and MeiFacsimileLoader make the paths of their pages (create_paths()); IIIFManifestLoader is given the path of each canvas. See How to Represent Areas of Page Images as Boxes and How to Work with Graphical Timelines.

TimeInterval

Defined by a StartInstant and EndInstant; left-inclusive and right-exclusive [s, e). The EndInstant’s coordinate must be >= the StartInstant’s. See Foundations.

TimeIntervalEvent

An Event with duration, defined by a TimeInterval. Contrast with InstantEvent. See Foundations.

TimeIntervalStamp

Combination of a start TimeStamp and an end TimeStamp, representing a cross-section of an interval through the timeline hierarchy. It stores one Interval per timeline ID; get_interval(timeline_id) returns that Interval, get_intervals() the whole mapping, get_duration_for() an IdDuration, and get_interval_in(unit) the span converted through a C-map. Interval retrieval takes no format argument — its scalar leaf is always an Interval. See Nested timelines.

Timeline

A positive coordinate axis defined by an origin and a measuring unit; continuous (real) or discrete (integer). Accommodates events and potentially Child timelines. See Foundations.

TimelineGroup

An array of member timelines that share the same graphical start and end: every member’s 0 coincides with every other member’s 0, and every member’s length with every other member’s length. Placing timelines in a group asserts Commensurability regardless of their units. A position in between converts linearly and exactly (p on member A is p · len_B / len_A on member B) and is written in the target member’s number type. When only part of a timeline takes part, the member is a Child of that timeline at its exact offset; a member is never placed partially. No member is an ancestor or a descendant of another member of the same group, since a child sits at its offset inside its parent. A group answers with the same TimeStamp class as a Timeline; to_dict() and from_dict() write and read it with every timeline it needs. See Alignment.

TimeStamp

A cross-section through a timeline or group at a given coordinate, capturing positions in all connected systems plus values converted by all attached ConversionMaps. It stores one Coordinate per timeline ID, so each entry carries its own unit and number type. TimeStamp implements the Stamp interface it shares with MatchStamp: a typed axis, get_coordinate_for() and get_coordinates_for() returning IdCoordinates by default, get_unit() for unit conversion, get_conversion_for() for label and structured map values, present_timelines, and is_interpolated. A bare number is an explicit format="float"/"int"/"fraction" request; there is no ambient float view. Which children answer follows the containment rule of Child. See Nested timelines.

TimeToShare manifest

The file format in which timelines, groups and bundles are exchanged, written in canonical YAML, or optionally in pretty JSON or RFC 8785 JSON, one shape for all: the version marker "timetoshare", an array of root timelines, and optionally the manifest’s id, name and meta, its groups, its measure_maps, its resources (the files beside it, such as the MatchClaim table; see Resource), its @context, statements and provenance (see statement) and its graphical (display order and styling). A single timeline is a manifest of one root, a group a manifest with one group; a manifest with an id or a name is named. Every manifest is an alignment bundle, also one holding one timeline or one group, and a manifest with neither an id nor a name is an anonymous bundle. A value on a timeline’s own axis (length, a child’s offset, region bounds, flow-control coordinates) is written bare, in the axis’s number type. Timeline, TimelineGroup and AlignmentBundle write one with to_dict() and read one with from_dict(), and write and read a manifest file with to_file() and from_file(). See How to Save and Load Timelines, Groups and Bundles.

title: Glossary
text:
U

Unknown key

A key of a TimeToShare manifest that the format does not define, written by another application for its own use. The library keeps every unknown key on the object read from the JSON object it was found in and writes it back in place.

Unknown length

A timeline length of None (null in a manifest), stating that the length is not known. It is a fact, never inferred from content, and any timeline may have it: root, Child, Locked, group member or Segment. Positions on such a timeline are not bounded above, unless its parent ends it, as a segment line ends a Segment; an operation that needs the end raises UnknownLengthError. Setting a length to or from None is an ordinary edit; Timeline.is_length_known tells which case holds, and displays use the Reach.

UnknownLengthError

The ValueError raised by an operation that needs the end of a timeline whose length is unknown, before it changes anything. Its message names the operation and the timeline; group conversion to or from such a member and appending a child at such a parent’s end are examples.

title: Glossary
text:
V

Virtual timeline

The statement that a map was applied to a Timeline, giving a timeline with an element id, a unit, a number type and a length of its own and nothing else: no events, no children, no flow control. Applied, a FlowMap gives its root’s played order as a virtual timeline, and positions convert through it in both directions (unfold(), fold()). Timeline.create_virtual_timeline() states one; a manifest lists them in virtual_timelines. See How to Encode and Play Flow Control.

title: Glossary
text:
W

WarpMap

An interpolation-based coordinate mapping derived from a MatchLine; enables non-linear coordinate transfer between TimelineGroups. It declares both axes — source and target unit and number type — and is queried through get_coordinate_at(position) for one position or get_coordinates_at([...]) for a batch; the object is not callable and exposes no raw arrays. inverse() returns a WarpMap with both units and both number types swapped. See Alignment.

title: ContinuousGraphicalTimeline
text:
ContinuousGraphicalTimeline
timelines.ContinuousGraphicalTimeline(
    length=0,
    unit=None,
    number_type=None,
    uid=None,
    name=None,
    locked=False,
    meta=None,
    *,
    seed=None,
)
A graphical timeline with continuous coordinates.
Used for visualization where real-valued positions are needed (e.g., a note head at x=12.75 centimeters).
Default unit: centimeters. Default number type: float. Allowed units: meters, centimeters, millimeters, inches, points, css_pixels, user_units.

title: EepNotesLoader
text:
loader.EepNotesLoader(unit=None, number_type=None, **kwargs)
Loader for EEP .notes alignment files.
Subclasses :class:CsvLoader with configuration for the whitespace-separated, headerless .notes format. Each line contains onset (seconds), offset (seconds), and pitch (note name, “rest”, or comma-separated chord).
The loader: - Assigns column names start, end, pitch - Infers the staff number from the filename (e.g., *_vln1.notes -> staff 1) - Respells every note name’s accidentals as ♯/♭ (Eb5 -> E♭5), the spelling of the library’s score loaders, so names compare equal across loaders - Preserves “rest” entries and comma-separated chords
Chord explosion (splitting G3,D4,B4,F5 into separate rows) is left to post-processing, typically during note matching.


>>> loader = EepNotesLoader.from_file("EEP_Normal_align_vln1.notes")
>>> len(loader)
1266
>>> loader.events.summary()
>>> # Load all 4 instruments for a recording
>>> loader = EepNotesLoader()
>>> loader.load(*sorted(eep_dir.glob("*_align_*.notes")))
>>> len(loader)
4026

title: MatchfileLoader
text:
loader.alignment.matchfile.MatchfileLoader(
    score_unit=TimeUnit.quarters,
    normalize_anacrusis=True,
    *,
    seed=None,
)
Load Vienna Match (.match) alignment files via partitura.
A single MatchfileLoader instance is intended to process all .match files that share the same score (e.g. 22 performances of one piece). It builds a shared score timeline on the first compatible file and verifies subsequent files against it. Incompatible files (snote ID present with different coordinates) are rejected with a warning.
Usage follows the standard loader two-phase pattern:

loader.load(*match_files) — parses all files, builds internal state.
loader.create_bundle() — assembles the result.
loader.create_timeline(uid) — retrieves individual timelines.

Produces:

A ContinuousLogicalTimeline for the score side (quarter-beat coordinates; MIDI divisions available via the attached quarters_to_divs ScalarMap C-Map).
One DiscreteLogicalTimeline per performance (MIDI tick coordinates; seconds available via the attached ticks_to_seconds ScalarMap).
One MatchClaim per alignment record per file:

Matched notes produce MatchClaim.from_events() (synchronous interval claim).
Deletion records produce MatchClaim.nomatch() (non-synchronous, NOMATCH).


All MatchClaims carry the provenance Provenance(method="imported", note="vienna_match v1.0.0") and certainty=1.0.
Coordinate system and normalisation: Score coordinates are stored as normalised TTA coordinates (shifted so the minimum onset is 0.0). A ShiftMap named "raw_quarters" is attached to the score timeline to convert normalised coordinates back to raw partitura values. The shift amount is computed from the file itself and never hardcoded.
External score timeline: Pass a score timeline previously built by PartituraLoader via the score_timeline= parameter of create_bundle(). The loader verifies compatibility (matching snote IDs and coordinates) and references the supplied timeline in all MatchClaims. MatchClaims are never rebound after creation.

title: MapsLoader
text:
loader.alignment.MapsLoader(seed=None)
Load a MAPS alignment file and state it as MatchClaims.
Usage follows the standard loader two-phase pattern:

loader.load(path) — read and validate the rows of one MAPS file.
loader.create_bundle(score, performance) — both timelines and the claims in one bundle; create_match_claims gives the claims alone.

Every row is kept as stated, one claim per listed id. The recording has no events of its own, so an onset enters the performance timeline as a :class:~timetoalign.core.Projection on its own axis:

a non-negative onset: a synchronous claim between the score note and its Projection at the onset;
a negative onset (trompa-align’s -1 for a note not performed): a NOMATCH claim from the score note;
an id beginning trompa-align_inserted_ (a performed note not in the score): a NOMATCH claim from a Projection at the onset that stands for no score note, the id kept.

An id listed in two rows (say, a repeat played against an unrepeated score) gives one claim per row, and load logs it. load logs the count of each kind, and refuses a file it cannot read as stated: a missing key, obs_num not consecutive from 1, an onset that is not a JSON number, an xml_id that is neither a non-empty string nor a non-empty list of them, and an inserted id at a negative onset, which states a note on neither side.
One loader reads one file: a MAPS file aligns one performance. Its payload is the rows, not an AlignmentStore, so store stays None.

    score,

Return one claim per listed id of every row, as the row states it.
Every claim names its events. The recording holds no event of its own, so each onset is a :class:~timetoalign.core.Projection on performance, its position the onset converted onto the performance timeline’s axis (through its C-Map where that is not in seconds: a samples timeline holds samples, never seconds); the claims are made by the library’s one projection operation (:meth:AlignmentBundle.create_match_claims <timetoalign.alignment.bundle.AlignmentBundle.create_match_claims> takes the same sides):

a note at a non-negative onset: a Projection of the score note (projection_of naming it on score) and a synchronous claim between the score note, at its start coordinate on score, and that Projection;
a note at a negative onset: a NOMATCH claim from the score note; nothing is added to performance;
an inserted id: a Projection standing for a note the score does not hold (projection_of null) and a NOMATCH claim from it. The Projection keeps the file’s id; where trompa-align gives two inserted notes one id (it spells the pitch only), each Projection is minted an id of its own and the claim keeps the file’s id as the event’s name.

performance keeps one Projection per score note and onset: a second call on the same timelines reuses every Projection the first added (an inserted note under its kept id is then the event the timeline holds), so it adds nothing to performance.

State the header’s description on a bundle and its timelines.
The work becomes a value node under the bundle’s schema:about, each manifestation a new graphical timeline in millimetres of unknown length, named by its first title; expressions and items are value nodes. A name without an IRI is offered as a candidate. A pair a subject already states or holds an entry of (a candidate, a pair someone believes) is passed over, and the pairs of a value node go into it only while the subject states it, so importing a header twice into one bundle adds nothing and every belief recorded stands. The import holds no belief. Every pair is checked before the bundle changes: a refused one leaves it as it was.

title: ListenHereLoader
text:
loader.alignment.listen_here.ListenHereLoader(seed=None)
Load a Listen Here! alignment JSON file as one AlignmentBundle.
The loader parses a single alignment JSON file describing many recordings of one work warped onto a shared equidistant reference grid, and assembles a bundle in which every recording is a seconds timeline in its own group, related to every other recording by a complete set of pairwise synchronous instant :class:MatchClaim rows held columnar in a :class:MatchClaimField. The file states grid positions, not events, so every claim is :data:~timetoalign.core.ids.CHUNK on both sides and the timelines hold no events.
Usage follows the standard loader two-phase pattern:

loader.load(alignment_json) — parse one alignment JSON file.
loader.create_bundle() — assemble the AlignmentBundle.
loader.create_timeline(uid) / create_timelines() — retrieve individual timelines.

The loader reads the existing alignment; it never runs an aligner.

Description

The recording stems, in sorted order.

The reference recording (header.ref) — the grid origin.

The field is handed to the bundle with :meth:~timetoalign.alignment.bundle.AlignmentBundle.add_match_claim_field, not exploded into a list of :class:MatchClaim objects. The bundle answers get_matchstamp_at by filtering the field’s claim columns vectorized and materialising only the handful of claims at the queried coordinate, so a whole-work file (on the order of a million claims) never builds a million Python claims.

title: Box
text:
Box()
An area of an image as an interval event of a timeline along its x.
A Box holds exactly one shape, a :class:BoundingBox or a :class:Quadrilateral, in the image’s space, and the interval of the shape’s x extent on its timeline: start is the shape’s x_min less the x at which the timeline stands in the image, duration the shape’s x extent (x_max - x_min). The shape is on the start’s axis (one unit, one number type).
Storage struct (derived): {id, start, duration, bounding_box, quadrilateral}, the shape not held null; every number on the axis :class:BoxField declares. In a timeline’s events, bounding_box and quadrilateral are two columns.


>>> box = BoundingBox.from_xywh(385, 46, 139, 20, unit="pixels")
>>> rect = Box.from_shape(box, origin=7, id="rect_h2")
>>> rect.start, rect.duration
(Coordinate(378, pixels), Duration(139, pixels))

title: Ms3Loader
text:
loader.score.Ms3Loader(*args, auto_discover=False, **kwargs)
Load symbolic scores from DCML-style TSV files.
Wraps ms3.load_tsv to load standard tabular data. Returns a ScoreStore with category-specific data.
Unlike single-file loaders (PartituraLoader, Music21Loader), TSV corpora store each facet (notes, measures, chords, harmonies) in a separate file. By default the loader loads exactly the files it is given. Pass auto_discover=True to have it locate companion facet files automatically.
Auto-discovery keeps the piece name and swaps the facet, looking in two places for each other facet:

Flat siblings (ms3 convention): for name.notes.tsv, look for name.measures.tsv, name.chords.tsv, name.harmonies.tsv in the same directory.
Facet directories (DCML corpus convention): if the file sits in a directory named after its facet (notes/name.notes.tsv), look in the sibling directories named after the other facets (measures/name.measures.tsv, chords/name.chords.tsv, harmonies/name.harmonies.tsv).

A facet the piece lacks is skipped; a file for which no companion is found at all raises a UserWarning and is loaded alone.
TSV columns (notes.tsv gold standard): - mc, mn: Measure count/number - quarterbeats: Continuous logical time (Fraction string) - duration_qb: Duration in quarter beats (float) - mc_onset, mn_onset: Measure-relative offsets (Fraction string) - timesig: Time signature context - staff, voice: Part context - duration, nominal_duration, scalar: Symbolic duration - tpc, midi, name, octave: Pitch info - tied, gracenote, chord_id: Note attributes

text:
loader.midi.score.ScoreMidiLoader(
    part_voice_assign_mode=0,
    quantization_unit=None,
    estimate_voice_info=False,
    estimate_key=False,
    assign_note_ids=True,
    parser='partitura',
    unit=None,
    number_type=None,
    **kwargs,
)
Load score MIDI files using partitura or a mido fast path.
This loader uses partitura’s sophisticated MIDI parsing to extract structural information like voices, parts, and specific pitches (optional). It is ideal for quantized MIDI files representing scores.
The default partitura parser emits :class:ScoreMidiEventData, the wider schema containing voice, staff, and part_id. parser="mido" parses only MIDI messages and emits the base :class:MidiEventData schema; it is appropriate when structural score information is not required. Both parsers write each note’s velocity as its note-on message states it; partitura’s score parse keeps none, so the default path reads the velocities from the same file and joins them to partitura’s notes by partitura’s note number, checking onset, pitch and duration. A note that cannot be joined that way (a partitura release numbering its notes otherwise) keeps an empty velocity, and one UserWarning per file names the first such note; parser="mido" reads every velocity.
A MIDI file states no note IDs, so every event ID is minted by the loader’s minter (note_…), whichever parser reads the file.

loader.alignment.tilia.TiliaJsonLoader(media_unit=TimeUnit.seconds, **kwargs)
Loader for TiLiA JSON annotation exports.
Parses a TiLiA .tla or .json file and produces one ContinuousPhysicalTimeline (seconds) per annotated timeline in the file. The primary output is a timetoalign.timelines.groups.TimelineGroup containing all timelines, accessible via create_group().
Internally, the "timelines" array is parsed so that each element (which has its own "kind" and "components") becomes a separate pa.Table keyed by its source identifier. The underlying JsonLoader machinery is used for normalising each timeline’s components into a flat table.
The .store property returns a TiliaDictStore with helper properties for each TiLiA timeline type::
loader.store.hierarchy  # all hierarchy tables concatenated
loader.store.marker     # all marker tables concatenated
loader.store.beat       # all beat tables concatenated
Two-phase usage:

loader.load("Bruckner5_Scherzo.json")
group = loader.create_group()

tl = loader.create_timeline("BEAT_TIMELINE_3")

bundle = loader.create_bundle()
