title: VerovioLoader
text:
loader.score.VerovioLoader(options=None, **kwargs)
Load an engraved score through the Verovio toolkit.
Any format Verovio reads (MEI, MusicXML, Humdrum, ABC, PAE, …) yields one score as Verovio renders it: its timemap is taken verbatim, and nothing is computed from the notated rhythm. A measure that holds only <mSpace> is timed by Verovio as a measure rest (see Known issues).

:meth:create_timeline gives the logical timeline: one ContinuousLogicalTimeline in quarters, positions the timemap’s exact qfrac (useFractions), with a quarters → seconds C-Map.
:meth:create_physical_timeline gives the same events on Verovio’s rendered time: one ContinuousPhysicalTimeline in seconds, positions the timemap’s integer milliseconds tstamp as Fraction(tstamp, 1000), with the inverse C-Map. It is time synthesised from the score’s tempo, not a performance.

The C-Map is one TableMap through every timemap entry (:meth:create_quarters_to_seconds_map). Verovio holds the tempo constant within a measure, so linear interpolation between the entries reproduces its own time.
Movements. Every named <mdiv> Verovio loads (one with a non-blank @label) is a child timeline, in document order, its id minted from the loader’s minter after the root’s (score:clt_…, rendered:cpt_…): placed at its first position, as long as its measures, named by its label, with meta holding count (its place among all <mdiv>s of the file, from 1), its xml:id, n and label verbatim, and element "mdiv". A named <mdiv> nests under the child of its nearest named ancestor <mdiv>, else under the root. An unnamed <mdiv> makes no timeline: what it holds belongs to the nearest named ancestor’s child, else to the root, so a score whose one <mdiv> has no label is the root alone. Events live in the innermost named movement holding them, at parent − offset; the root holds the measures, the flow control and the C-Map. All movements are loaded unless an mdivAll or mdivXPathQuery option chooses.
Repeats. The timemap is Verovio’s rendering: with repeats expanded (Verovio’s default, steered by the expand, expandAlways and expandNever options), a repeated passage appears once per pass. Event id is the rendered id (…-rend2 from the second pass on); field notated_id is the element’s id in the notated score (equal to id when nothing is expanded), read with getNotatedIdForElement for ids the notated tree does not hold. The store’s measure table is the printed one (one row per <measure> in document order, lengths as rendered, positions on the folded axis), carrying the repeat barlines, endings and <repeatMark>s (segno, coda, Fine, D.S., D.C.) and the barline @right states. Without an expansion the timeline carries that table as its MeasureMap and what it states as its flow control (a dbl and an end barline as barlines). With an expansion the timeline is already unfolded: its MeasureMap lists the rendered measures (row id = rendered id, name = @n) without flow control. The order in which the expansion plays the printed measures is a FlowMap of the printed score: :meth:create_stated_flow_map writes it onto the timeline that a loader of the same file with expandNever creates.
Ids. Every event keeps its element’s xml:id verbatim. Verovio generates ids only where the source has none, from a random seed unless told otherwise; the loader seeds them from the input’s checksum (xmlIdChecksum), so a generated id is stable for one Verovio version and one input. A user xmlIdSeed wins and is logged. After loading, every xml:id of getMEI() is checked for uniqueness, because Verovio’s generator does not test it: a duplicate held by an element the loader reads raises, any other is logged and listed in the store metadata under "duplicate_ids".
Sources of each value:

Positions come from the timemap with useFractions. The timemap’s float qstamp is a cross-check: the float nearest to each exact position must equal it, else the load raises.
Membership (movement, measure, staff, layer), <tie> elements and tempo text come from the MEI tree that getMEI() returns, read with the standard library’s XML parser.
MIDI pitch comes from getMIDIValuesForElement.

Events: one interval event per note (event_type "Note") and per rest ("Rest") from onset to offset, and one instant event per <tempo> and pass ("tempo indication", its text verbatim). mc, mn name the printed measure; mc_onset is the position in the rendered pass of it, in quarters, on the logical timeline only. voice is the <layer> number, chord_id the xml:id of the note’s <chord>. A tied note’s continuation is an event of its own; field tie (i, m, t, verbatim from @tie or from the <tie> elements naming the note) tells attacks from continuations. Field grace is the @grace of the note, its chord or its <graceGrp>, verbatim. <space> elements are not events. The note staff is the staff the note is drawn on: a cross-staff chord’s @staff, else its <staff>.


Grace notes and arpeggiated notes sit where Verovio performs them, not at their notated onsets. An unaccented grace note takes a short fixed span before its principal note (or delays the principal note at a measure start), an accented one takes a share of the principal note and delays it, and the notes of an arpeggio are rolled one after the other. The controls are MEI attributes (@grace, @grace.time, graceGrp/@attach, arpeg/@order); the loader does not undo them. A <tie> whose endid names no element of the file (a tie leaving an excerpt) is logged and listed in the store metadata under "dangling_ties"; its start note keeps tie = "i" and nothing is invented for the missing end. Verovio prints its own warning to the process’s standard error; getLog() stays empty. A measure without timed content has no length in Verovio’s timemap and no entry of its own: the next measure starts where the one before it ends. Where such a measure holds an <mSpace> (a measure-long space) and a meter is in force, the loader renders Verovio’s MEI output once more with each of its <mSpace>s read as an <mRest> of the same xml:id: Verovio then times the measure itself, at its meter’s length and the tempo in force there (a tempo written in it, else the one before it), in every pass of an expansion. The rests are no events. Any other measure without content raises, naming the measures. Verovio 6.4.1’s expansion leaves out the measures of <ending>s it cannot place (both endings, and no repeat of their passage, after another repeat). Their lengths are read from a second rendering with expandNever; their events are not in the rendered timelines. They are logged and listed in the store metadata under "omitted_measures". Verovio’s expansion does not follow D.S. and D.C. marks; the printed measure table states them. expandAlways writes the expansion into the MEI tree, which then no longer states the printed score; it raises. Verovio 6.4.1 crashes the process in renderToTimemap when it expands the repeats of some files; expandNever reads them. An MEI file whose <music> holds no <measure> and no <staff> (a header describing a work, <music/> empty) can give no timeline: the loader reads the file before Verovio does and raises, naming the element that is missing or empty. Verovio’s Python binding writes its reasons to standard error, not to getLog(); where Verovio declines another file, the message says that it gave no reason.



>>> loader = VerovioLoader.from_file("score.mei")
>>> timeline = loader.create_timeline()
>>> seconds = loader.create_physical_timeline()

An unaccented grace note takes a short fixed span before its principal note (or delays the principal note at a measure start), an accented one takes a share of the principal note and delays it, and the notes of an arpeggio are rolled one after the other. The controls are MEI attributes (@grace, @grace.time, graceGrp/@attach, arpeg/@order); the loader does not undo them. A <tie> whose endid names no element of the file (a tie leaving an excerpt) is logged and listed in the store metadata under "dangling_ties"; its start note keeps tie = "i" and nothing is invented for the missing end. Verovio prints its own warning to the process’s standard error; getLog() stays empty. A measure without timed content has no length in Verovio’s timemap and no entry of its own: the next measure starts where the one before it ends. Where such a measure holds an <mSpace> (a measure-long space) and a meter is in force, the loader renders Verovio’s MEI output once more with each of its <mSpace>s read as an <mRest> of the same xml:id: Verovio then times the measure itself, at its meter’s length and the tempo in force there (a tempo written in it, else the one before it), in every pass of an expansion. The rests are no events. Any other measure without content raises, naming the measures. Verovio 6.4.1’s expansion leaves out the measures of <ending>s it cannot place (both endings, and no repeat of their passage, after another repeat). Their lengths are read from a second rendering with expandNever; their events are not in the rendered timelines. They are logged and listed in the store metadata under "omitted_measures". Verovio’s expansion does not follow D.S. and D.C. marks; the printed measure table states them. expandAlways writes the expansion into the MEI tree, which then no longer states the printed score; it raises. Verovio 6.4.1 crashes the process in renderToTimemap when it expands the repeats of some files; expandNever reads them. An MEI file whose <music> holds no <measure> and no <staff> (a header describing a work, <music/> empty) can give no timeline: the loader reads the file before Verovio does and raises, naming the element that is missing or empty. Verovio’s Python binding writes its reasons to standard error, not to getLog(); where Verovio declines another file, the message says that it gave no reason.

title: SupportPolicy
text:
core.SupportPolicy()
How to treat a transferred coordinate that falls outside alignment support.
A coordinate transferred to another timeline is out-of-support when the entering coordinate lies outside the transferring WarpMap’s source-anchor hull, or when the produced coordinate would fall outside the target timeline’s [0, length] span. This policy decides what happens to such a timeline when a cross-timeline stamp is assembled.










Name
Type
Description




omit

Drop the out-of-support timeline from the stamp entirely. This is the default: a coordinate below the first alignment anchor or beyond the last one has no defined position, so the timeline simply does not appear.


clamp

Clamp the entering coordinate to the nearest hull boundary before warping (yielding that boundary anchor’s target), then clip the result to [0, length]. The timeline stays present.


extrapolate

Keep the linear extrapolation beyond the hull, then clip the result to [0, length]. The timeline stays present.



No policy ever emits a negative coordinate or one exceeding the target timeline’s length.

title: DmosLoader
text:
loader.graphical.DmosLoader(seed=None)
Load the pages, systems and measures of a DMOS JSON file.
A page’s time path is its systems read one after the other (:meth:create_paths), and the timelines mirror it, all in pixels (int):

a system is an accolade: a :class:~timetoalign.timelines.DiscreteGraphicalTimeline as long as its region is wide, named by its DMOS id, stating the region in meta["box"] and the page image in meta["image"];
a page is the segment line of its accolades in document order, named by its no_page, stating meta["image"] (its page_url) and no meta["box"]: its axis is a concatenation, not an area;
the volume (:meth:create_timeline) is the segment line of the pages.

Each measure is a :class:~timetoalign.core.Box event of its system’s accolade, holding the measure’s quadrilateral in the page image’s pixels: start is the measure’s least x minus the system’s least x and duration the measure’s x extent, so the accolade’s meta["box"] and the Box’s shape, both in image space, agree with the interval.
Known limits: measures have no id and no number in DMOS, so their Boxes are minted box_… unless box_ids names them; DMOS system ids repeat on some pages, so an accolade’s name (its DMOS id) need not be unique, while its timeline id is. A measure whose x extent leaves its system’s region, on the left or on the right, cannot be a Box of that system’s accolade and refuses the file (the accolade spans exactly its region’s x extent; neither is widened to hold the measure). A system whose region has no x extent (a vertical line) and which holds no measures, as DMOS output holds some, is no part of the time path: it is left out of :meth:create_paths, :meth:create_timelines and :meth:create_timeline alike, and :meth:load logs one warning per file naming each such system by its page and its position on it. A system without x extent that holds measures loads, but creating paths or timelines from the file is refused, naming the page and the system’s position. A page without systems, or all of whose systems are left out, has no time path and is left out.


The pages of a DMOS file as one timeline, its measures numbered through the score::
loader = DmosLoader.from_file("dmos.json")
volume = loader.create_timeline(uid="scan", box_ids="m{n}")
page = volume.get_child(volume.list_children()[0])
accolade = page.get_child(page.list_children()[0])
boxes = accolade.get_events().table.to_pylist()

Description

Forget the loaded file.

A page’s path is its systems in document order, each one horizontal piece: from its region’s least x to its greatest, at the middle of its y extent, with half that extent as tolerance, so the piece’s strip is the system’s y extent. Nothing is grouped or guessed: every stated system is one piece, also where it starts right of the one before. A system without x extent and without measures is no piece of the path and is left out; a page without systems, or all of whose systems are left out, has no path and no entry.

title: Timeline
text:
timelines.Timeline(
    length=0,
    unit=None,
    number_type=None,
    uid=None,
    name=None,
    locked=False,
    meta=None,
    *,
    seed=None,
)
A positive coordinate axis with events and nested child timelines.
A Timeline represents a temporal dimension in one of three domains (Logical, Physical, Graphical) with either continuous or discrete coordinates. It stores events in an EventData and can contain nested child timelines (segments) at specified offsets.
Intended usage: This base class provides the full Timeline API but does not enforce domain or modality constraints. For typical usage, prefer one of the six concrete subclasses or the create_timeline() factory function:

ContinuousLogicalTimeline – beats, quarters, measures (Fraction)
DiscreteLogicalTimeline – ticks (int)
ContinuousPhysicalTimeline – seconds, ms, minutes (float)
DiscretePhysicalTimeline – samples, frames (int)
ContinuousGraphicalTimeline – cm, inches, points (float)
DiscreteGraphicalTimeline – pixels (int)

These subclasses restrict allowed units and number types to prevent accidental cross-domain errors and provide sensible defaults.
Direct instantiation of Timeline is appropriate for internal use, generic algorithms that operate across domains, or advanced scenarios where domain constraints are intentionally relaxed.
If you have a Timeline instance and need the appropriate typed subclass, use :meth:to_typed.

>>> # Preferred: use concrete subclasses

>>> # Or use the factory to auto-select the right subclass

timelines.Timeline.add_child(
    child,
    offset,
    allow_expansion=False,
    use_conversion_map=None,
    *,
    locked=None,
    seed=None,
)
Embed a child timeline at the specified offset.
The child timeline is locked once added unless locked=False, which leaves its own state as it is. An unlocked child may change its length, but only within this timeline’s known end: this timeline never grows because a child grew. A segment of a segment line is never locked: the line’s lock governs it, and the segment’s own lock is lifted when it joins. A segment line is locked like any child, whether it becomes a child or a segment; unlocking it is not supported yet, so locked=False is refused for a segment line that is unlocked, and accepted (asking for nothing) for one already locked. Parent-child coordinate conversion uses exact offset arithmetic.
The child’s whole subtree joins this timeline’s manifest, in which every id is unique across all element kinds: an element of the subtree whose id, given or minted, is already held here makes the call raise without changing anything. Nothing is renamed.
A timeline can accommodate events and other timelines, called Children, as long as they use the same measuring unit.
When the child uses a different unit than the parent, set use_conversion_map to automatically convert the child to the parent’s unit via a C-Map. The parent must have a C-Map whose target_unit matches the child’s unit, so that inverting it yields the child_unit -> parent_unit conversion. The child’s events are copied with converted coordinates; the original child is NOT modified.
The converted child is named "{child.name} [{parent.unit}]" and receives a minted id: from IdMinter(seed) with seed, else from the content minter of the source’s id and the parent’s unit.

    believer=None,

    actor=None,
    date=None,
    seed=None,
)
Write this timeline’s atomic sections and its computed FlowMaps.
The flow control of the timeline and of its descendants of its unit (:attr:tree_flow_control <timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.tree_flow_control>) is played on the timeline’s axis with the three conventions (:func:~timetoalign.timelines.flow.engine.play): a root plays its whole tree, a child its own subtree. The atomic sections (:func:~timetoalign.timelines.flow.engine.atomic_sections) become Regions of the timeline, each named by its letter and stating the type tts:AtomicSection with the provenance method inferred. The default flow becomes a FlowMap listing those Regions in the order played; single and printed become FlowMaps only where their chunks differ from default’s. Each FlowMap names its convention and the provenance method inferred.
A FlowMap names a root timeline. On a root, the Regions are the root’s, also where its flow control lies only in descendants. On a child, the Regions are the child’s and the FlowMaps are stored on the root of its tree, listing the child’s Regions; a FlowMap written there anew is named after the child and its convention ("Allegro, default"). The computed FlowMaps of a timeline are those of its root that list its Regions only, so the flows of several children of one root stand side by side, and a virtual timeline applying one to the root takes its new length when it is written again.
Called again after the flow control changed, the call takes nothing away and never lets a Region’s ID name another stretch:

an atomic section whose stretch is still one keeps its Region; it is renamed where the new sectioning gives it another letter;
a stretch that is new gets a new Region, also one that was a section before and whose Region has been rejected since;
a Region whose stretch is an atomic section no longer stays, with its ID, its interval and its name, and actor’s belief "false" is recorded in its statement type: tts:AtomicSection (:meth:Region.with_belief <timetoalign.timelines.Region.with_belief>), so that it is no atomic section any more (:attr:Region.is_atomic_section <timetoalign.timelines.Region.is_atomic_section>). What names it (a FlowMap written by hand, a statement, a Jump going on at it) keeps naming the same stretch;
the computed FlowMaps keep their IDs, names and canonical flags and list the new sections; one written before for single or printed stays, also where its chunks have come to equal default’s; a virtual timeline applying one takes its new length.

timelines.Timeline.from_dict(data, *, timeline_id=None, name=None)
Read a timeline from a TimeToShare manifest.
Without timeline_id and name, a manifest holding one root timeline and no group is read as a whole: its root is returned, and the manifest’s own keys are kept so that :meth:to_dict writes the manifest back. An argument naming a timeline of the manifest, root or descendant, selects it; given both, they must name the same timeline. Only arguments naming no timeline override the root’s id and name, and only in a manifest of one root and no group; the new id must not be held by any element of the manifest, and the statements naming the root name it by its new id.
A timeline selected leaves the rest of the manifest behind: a value of a statement of its tree naming a timeline or region of the rest is dropped, with its provenance.
The class comes from the unit (each unit belongs to exactly one class) and is_segment_line. Every optional key may be left out and reads as its default; a number_type left out is the unit’s own (int for ticks, samples, frames and pixels, fraction for quarters and whole_notes, float otherwise). A value on the timeline’s own axis is read as its number type decides, whatever its lexical form (2.0 on an int axis is 2, [1, 8.0] on a fraction axis is 1/8); a length of null reads as None. A root’s offset is kept as :attr:root_offset. Keys the library does not know are kept on the object read from the JSON object they were found in, and written back.

Extract a portion of this timeline as a new, independent timeline.
Returns a new timeline containing all events within [start, end). The returned timeline has its coordinate origin at 0, with all coordinates shifted by -start.
Slicing creates a new timeline that is a structural copy of the specified interval of the source.
A timeline holding Boxes (itself or a descendant) stands for an area of an image (meta["box"]): the slice states the part of that area over its x extent (the area as written where the slice covers the whole timeline), and meta["image"] is carried over, so a Box keeps its shape, in the image’s space, and its start moves with the slice’s origin. meta is otherwise free-form: a timeline holding no Box gives the slice none of it.

The area of a proper slice of a quadrilateral area is the slice of its bounding box. A timeline holding Boxes that states no area moves a Box of its own only into a slice starting at 0; its children are sliced by this rule in turn, so a page made of accolades is sliced accolade by accolade, each slice stating its own area.

timelines.Timeline.to_dict(
    minimal=True,
    events=False,
    external_references=False,
)
Write a TimeToShare manifest holding this timeline as its one root.
The timeline object is the timeline’s structure: its axis, children, conversion maps, regions and flow control, and its statements and provenance (see :mod:~timetoalign.timelines.statements). Its measure map is a MeasureRecordMap among the conversion maps (chained after a LinearMap to quarters on an axis in whole notes or ticks) naming an entry of the manifest’s measure_maps, which also holds every measure map a measure view names; equal measure maps share one entry. The metric hierarchy has no manifest form and is not written. Every conversion map is written as one of the format’s map types (see :meth:ConversionMap.to_dict <timetoalign.maps.ConversionMap.to_dict>). The library’s class is not written: the unit decides it. A value on the timeline’s own axis — length, a child’s offset, region start/end, a flow-control element’s coordinate — is written bare, represented as the axis’s number type selects (8, 8.0, [8, 1]); a length of None is written null. "events" and "external_references" are written only on request. The FlowMaps naming the timeline and the virtual timelines that come from its tree are written at the manifest’s top level (flow_maps, virtual_timelines), each list sorted by id and left out when empty.
By default every key at its default value is left out, except length (the minimal form); with minimal=False every optional key is written, its default value included (the complete form). Keys the library does not know, kept when the timeline was read, are written back. A timeline read from a manifest as a whole writes that manifest’s id, name, meta, statements, graphical and unknown keys back around it. :meth:to_file writes the manifest as a file. Every manifest carries its inline JSON-LD @context: the format’s terms and the prefixes its statements use.
The manifest is written whole and valid wherever the timeline belongs: a value naming a timeline or region this manifest leaves out (another timeline of the bundle) is left out with its provenance.
Collections are written in one canonical order, independent of the order in which their content was added, so equal timelines give equal text: children by offset, then id; conversion_maps by id; regions by start, then end, then id; flow_control (every element in one array, see :meth:FlowControlRegistry.to_dict <timetoalign.timelines.flowcontrol.FlowControlRegistry.to_dict>) by coordinate, then id; measure_maps by id. Values compare exactly and ids by Unicode code point. The timeline’s own storage is not reordered, and :meth:from_dict accepts any order.

Each argument left None takes the value the file the object was read from had (see :meth:from_file); for an object not read from a file, the minimal form, the styling included, in canonical YAML, without event rows or external references. An :class:~timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle holding MatchClaims or Projections writes its tables beside the manifest and names them in its resources: its manifest is written (validated and serialized) once before any table, and once more naming the tables written. The manifest validated is the one the file holds: without its styling where styling=False leaves the styling out, so a manifest whose styling the format refuses (a named timestamp beyond the length its timeline was given since) is written without it.

Return this timeline re-instantiated as the appropriate typed subclass.

timelines.Timeline.add_child(
    child,
    offset,
    allow_expansion=False,
    use_conversion_map=None,
    *,
    locked=None,
    seed=None,
)
Embed a child timeline at the specified offset.
The child timeline is locked once added unless locked=False, which leaves its own state as it is. An unlocked child may change its length, but only within this timeline’s known end: this timeline never grows because a child grew. A segment of a segment line is never locked: the line’s lock governs it, and the segment’s own lock is lifted when it joins. A segment line is locked like any child, whether it becomes a child or a segment; unlocking it is not supported yet, so locked=False is refused for a segment line that is unlocked, and accepted (asking for nothing) for one already locked. Parent-child coordinate conversion uses exact offset arithmetic.
The child’s whole subtree joins this timeline’s manifest, in which every id is unique across all element kinds: an element of the subtree whose id, given or minted, is already held here makes the call raise without changing anything. Nothing is renamed.
A timeline can accommodate events and other timelines, called Children, as long as they use the same measuring unit.
When the child uses a different unit than the parent, set use_conversion_map to automatically convert the child to the parent’s unit via a C-Map. The parent must have a C-Map whose target_unit matches the child’s unit, so that inverting it yields the child_unit -> parent_unit conversion. The child’s events are copied with converted coordinates; the original child is NOT modified.
The converted child is named "{child.name} [{parent.unit}]" and receives a minted id: from IdMinter(seed) with seed, else from the content minter of the source’s id and the parent’s unit.

timelines.Timeline.add_events(rows, allow_expansion=False, *, seed=None)
Add events to the timeline.
Only event_type and a coordinate are strictly required per dict. Missing fields are filled in automatically:

id: minted (:func:~timetoalign.storage.events.mint_event_ids), its prefix the event type in lower case: note_…, beat_…, projection_…; from IdMinter(seed) when seed is given, else from the content minter of the timeline’s ID, the number of events it holds and the event types of the rows without an ID.
temporal_type: inferred from keys – "interval" when both start and end (or duration) are present, "instant" otherwise.

Positions are stored on this timeline’s axis. A start, end or instant given as a :class:~timetoalign.core.Coordinate in another unit is converted through the timeline’s C-Map; a duration given as a :class:~timetoalign.core.Duration (or Coordinate) in another unit is the span from the start it is added to, converted as the two ends of that span are, so its start must be given in the same unit. Each converted value is written in the timeline’s number type. Bare numbers and struct dicts are taken as on this timeline’s axis.
A Projection (event_type "Projection") holds id, its position and projection_of, the event of another timeline it stands for, as a dict {"timeline_id": ..., "event_id": ...} or an :class:~timetoalign.core.EventReference (None where none is known); it repeats nothing else of that event.
A Box (event_type "Box") is an area of the image the timeline runs along: its shape, in the image’s space, and the interval of its x extent on the timeline. Its shape must be on the timeline’s axis (its unit and number type; a shape is never converted), and its start must be the shape’s x_min less the x at which the timeline stands in its image: the x_min of the shape meta["box"] states, 0 where it states none. A shape given as the memory cell of its column is read through the shape’s constructor, as every shape’s numbers are (never rounded). A Box row may state unit, number_type and timeline_id, as a package’s Box table does: they must name this timeline and its axis, and are not stored.
An :class:~timetoalign.core.Event object (a :class:~timetoalign.core.Projection, a :class:~timetoalign.core.Box) may be given in place of its row, alone or in the list.

Write this timeline’s atomic sections and its computed FlowMaps.
The flow control of the timeline and of its descendants of its unit (:attr:tree_flow_control <timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.tree_flow_control>) is played on the timeline’s axis with the three conventions (:func:~timetoalign.timelines.flow.engine.play): a root plays its whole tree, a child its own subtree. The atomic sections (:func:~timetoalign.timelines.flow.engine.atomic_sections) become Regions of the timeline, each named by its letter and stating the type tts:AtomicSection with the provenance method inferred. The default flow becomes a FlowMap listing those Regions in the order played; single and printed become FlowMaps only where their chunks differ from default’s. Each FlowMap names its convention and the provenance method inferred.
A FlowMap names a root timeline. On a root, the Regions are the root’s, also where its flow control lies only in descendants. On a child, the Regions are the child’s and the FlowMaps are stored on the root of its tree, listing the child’s Regions; a FlowMap written there anew is named after the child and its convention ("Allegro, default"). The computed FlowMaps of a timeline are those of its root that list its Regions only, so the flows of several children of one root stand side by side, and a virtual timeline applying one to the root takes its new length when it is written again.
Called again after the flow control changed, the call takes nothing away and never lets a Region’s ID name another stretch:

an atomic section whose stretch is still one keeps its Region; it is renamed where the new sectioning gives it another letter;
a stretch that is new gets a new Region, also one that was a section before and whose Region has been rejected since;
a Region whose stretch is an atomic section no longer stays, with its ID, its interval and its name, and actor’s belief "false" is recorded in its statement type: tts:AtomicSection (:meth:Region.with_belief <timetoalign.timelines.Region.with_belief>), so that it is no atomic section any more (:attr:Region.is_atomic_section <timetoalign.timelines.Region.is_atomic_section>). What names it (a FlowMap written by hand, a statement, a Jump going on at it) keeps naming the same stretch;
the computed FlowMaps keep their IDs, names and canonical flags and list the new sections; one written before for single or printed stays, also where its chunks have come to equal default’s; a virtual timeline applying one takes its new length.

timelines.Timeline.from_dict(data, *, timeline_id=None, name=None)
Read a timeline from a TimeToShare manifest.
Without timeline_id and name, a manifest holding one root timeline and no group is read as a whole: its root is returned, and the manifest’s own keys are kept so that :meth:to_dict writes the manifest back. An argument naming a timeline of the manifest, root or descendant, selects it; given both, they must name the same timeline. Only arguments naming no timeline override the root’s id and name, and only in a manifest of one root and no group; the new id must not be held by any element of the manifest, and the statements naming the root name it by its new id.
A timeline selected leaves the rest of the manifest behind: a value of a statement of its tree naming a timeline or region of the rest is dropped, with its provenance.
The class comes from the unit (each unit belongs to exactly one class) and is_segment_line. Every optional key may be left out and reads as its default; a number_type left out is the unit’s own (int for ticks, samples, frames and pixels, fraction for quarters and whole_notes, float otherwise). A value on the timeline’s own axis is read as its number type decides, whatever its lexical form (2.0 on an int axis is 2, [1, 8.0] on a fraction axis is 1/8); a length of null reads as None. A root’s offset is kept as :attr:root_offset. Keys the library does not know are kept on the object read from the JSON object they were found in, and written back.

    start,
    end,
    *,
    truncate_events=True,
    include_children=True,
    copy_cmaps=True,
    seed=None,
)
Extract a portion of this timeline as a new, independent timeline.
Returns a new timeline containing all events within [start, end). The returned timeline has its coordinate origin at 0, with all coordinates shifted by -start.
Slicing creates a new timeline that is a structural copy of the specified interval of the source.
A timeline holding Boxes (itself or a descendant) stands for an area of an image (meta["box"]): the slice states the part of that area over its x extent (the area as written where the slice covers the whole timeline), and meta["image"] is carried over, so a Box keeps its shape, in the image’s space, and its start moves with the slice’s origin. meta is otherwise free-form: a timeline holding no Box gives the slice none of it.
Known issues: a Box crossing a slice boundary cannot be clipped (its interval would contradict its shape), so with truncate_events the slice is refused; slice with truncate_events=False to leave such a Box out (the flag holds for the slices of the children too). The area of a proper slice of a quadrilateral area is the slice of its bounding box. A timeline holding Boxes that states no area moves a Box of its own only into a slice starting at 0; its children are sliced by this rule in turn, so a page made of accolades is sliced accolade by accolade, each slice stating its own area.

timelines.Timeline.to_dict(
    minimal=True,
    events=False,
    external_references=False,
)
Write a TimeToShare manifest holding this timeline as its one root.
The timeline object is the timeline’s structure: its axis, children, conversion maps, regions and flow control, and its statements and provenance (see :mod:~timetoalign.timelines.statements). Its measure map is a MeasureRecordMap among the conversion maps (chained after a LinearMap to quarters on an axis in whole notes or ticks) naming an entry of the manifest’s measure_maps, which also holds every measure map a measure view names; equal measure maps share one entry. The metric hierarchy has no manifest form and is not written. Every conversion map is written as one of the format’s map types (see :meth:ConversionMap.to_dict <timetoalign.maps.ConversionMap.to_dict>). The library’s class is not written: the unit decides it. A value on the timeline’s own axis — length, a child’s offset, region start/end, a flow-control element’s coordinate — is written bare, represented as the axis’s number type selects (8, 8.0, [8, 1]); a length of None is written null. "events" and "external_references" are written only on request. The FlowMaps naming the timeline and the virtual timelines that come from its tree are written at the manifest’s top level (flow_maps, virtual_timelines), each list sorted by id and left out when empty.
By default every key at its default value is left out, except length (the minimal form); with minimal=False every optional key is written, its default value included (the complete form). Keys the library does not know, kept when the timeline was read, are written back. A timeline read from a manifest as a whole writes that manifest’s id, name, meta, statements, graphical and unknown keys back around it. :meth:to_file writes the manifest as a file. Every manifest carries its inline JSON-LD @context: the format’s terms and the prefixes its statements use.
The manifest is written whole and valid wherever the timeline belongs: a value naming a timeline or region this manifest leaves out (another timeline of the bundle) is left out with its provenance.
Collections are written in one canonical order, independent of the order in which their content was added, so equal timelines give equal text: children by offset, then id; conversion_maps by id; regions by start, then end, then id; flow_control (every element in one array, see :meth:FlowControlRegistry.to_dict <timetoalign.timelines.flowcontrol.FlowControlRegistry.to_dict>) by coordinate, then id; measure_maps by id. Values compare exactly and ids by Unicode code point. The timeline’s own storage is not reordered, and :meth:from_dict accepts any order.

Build the line through the first and the last pair by position.
The positions are read from origin (position - origin). Every inner pair is checked against the line through the end pairs, evaluated exactly on the positions as given, before origin is subtracted: the position at which the line reaches the pair’s value must be its position, exactly for an exact calibration and within the error of a position computed in doubles otherwise (see :meth:ConversionMap.from_pairs). The line is never fitted.

title: MatchClaim
text:
alignment.MatchClaim()
A claim that two events on different timelines correspond.
A MatchClaim always knows which two timelines it connects via top-level timeline_a_id and timeline_b_id fields, and it names on each side an event or a sentinel, a reserved string no element takes as its ID:

a synchronous claim names an event or :data:CHUNK on each side. A CHUNK side is a position the anchor states on a timeline holding no event for it: not an event and not a Projection, its coordinate the anchor’s on that side;
a claim that is not synchronous names two events (conceptual), or one event and :data:NOMATCH on the other side (the event has no counterpart there).

A CHUNK side may carry a name, naming the stated position; a NOMATCH side has none. Anchors are only present for synchronous claims, and each of their coordinates is on its timeline’s own axis (:meth:check_on_timelines).



from_events: Two sides on different timelines correspond (synchronous, with anchors, each side an event or CHUNK; or conceptual, between two events, without).
nomatch: An event has no equivalent on the other timeline.

A MatchClaim is always stated: the correspondences a :class:~timetoalign.alignment.graph.MatchGraph infers through groups are the graph’s own inferred edges, never MatchClaims.

(True, 'nomatch', 'NOMATCH_SENTINEL')
Two positions where neither timeline holds an event, CHUNK on both sides:

>>> claim.chunk_sides, claim.claim_type.name
(('score', 'recording'), 'event_match')
>>> claim
MatchClaim(instant: score@4 quarters [CHUNK] <-> recording@30 seconds [CHUNK])

>>> from timetoalign.timelines.types import (

>>> score = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=16, uid="score")

3

title: ClaimType
text:
core.ClaimType()
The semantic kind of a MatchClaim, derived from its structure.
A claim’s kind is never stored; it is read from whether the claim is synchronous and whether a side is the NOMATCH sentinel. A MatchClaim names an event or a sentinel on each side: a synchronous one an event or the CHUNK sentinel (a position on a timeline holding no event for it, held by the anchor), one that is not synchronous two events, or one event and the NOMATCH sentinel. What a MatchGraph infers through groups is the graph’s own and has no kind here.


event_match: Synchronous: two sides correspond, temporally anchored, each side an event or CHUNK. nomatch: An event has no counterpart on the other timeline. conceptual: Two events correspond structurally, with no temporal commitment (no anchors).

title: QuartersToFloatingMeasures
text:
QuartersToFloatingMeasures(
    x_values,
    y_values,
    source_unit=TimeUnit.quarters,
    target_unit=TimeUnit.floating_measures,
    uid=None,
    name=None,
    seed=None,
)
Map quarters to floating measures.
A floating measure (fm) writes a position as <ordinal>.<how far into that bar> — the convention behind annotation tables that read 12.5 for the middle of the twelfth bar. Two properties make it exact rather than approximate:

The fractional part is anchored on the NOMINAL bar. An incomplete bar’s content sits where it is notated, so a 1/8 pickup in 9/8 onsets at 0.888 — eight ninths of the way through the bar it belongs to — not at 0.000.
Emission truncates to three decimals. Three decimals is the convention’s resolution, and truncating (rather than rounding) is what makes 8/9 read 0.888; it is also the rule behind the .999 an interval end shows when a bar is read from the right.

An fm value is a float by definition: the fractional part measures an uneven discretisation of logical time — bars vary in length — so it is not a ratio of anything, and its resolution is capped at a thousandth of a bar. Converting fm back to quarters is therefore exact only to that resolution; the inverse interpolates linearly over the same knots and never tries to reconstruct what truncation dropped.


>>> cmap = QuartersToFloatingMeasures(
...     x_values=[0, 4, 8, 12],
...     y_values=[1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0],
... )
>>> cmap(0.0)    # Start of M1
1.0
>>> cmap(2.0)    # Halfway through M1 (4 quarters/measure)
1.5
>>> cmap(4.0)    # Start of M2
2.0

Description

to_measure_number_map
Convert to non-interpolating measure number map.





QuartersToFloatingMeasures.from_measure_map(measure_map, *, seed=None)
Build the floating-measure lattice of a measure map.
A floating measure is a compound measure: a maximal run of consecutive measure records that share one number, each continuing the one before it. A record continues the compound so far when the last record’s next names it — across a metre change too, since one measure number is one notated bar — or when it has the last record’s nominal_length and its offset_within_measure is exactly where the compound so far ends inside the notated bar (the first record’s offset plus the records’ actual lengths) — the second part of a bar split at a repeat sign whose first part jumps back. Two records stating different volta brackets never join, nor does a record without a number. A record on its own is a compound of one. The records of a split bar, whose parts the source represents separately, thus read as the one bar they are notated as.
One knot per compound measure, placed at its first record’s virtual nominal downbeat — its sounding start minus the offset at which its content sits inside the notated bar — and carrying the compound’s ordinal. A final knot closes the lattice at the end of the last record. Between two knots the map is linear, so the slope inside a bar is 1 / nominal_length when the bar fills its nominal length, and inside a compound the reading spreads over the compound’s whole extent.
Ordinals count compound measures, never the printed labels: the first is 0 when it is an anacrusis (its first record’s content is offset and its records are shorter together than its nominal bar) and 1 otherwise, and every following compound adds one. Counting runs monotonically through voltas — a first ending 15a that jumps back and the second ending 15b are two bars and get two consecutive ordinals — and never resets.

loader.graphical.ScoreWarpLoader(seed=None)
Load the time axis drawn into a ScoreWarp SVG.
The drawing becomes a :class:ContinuousGraphicalTimeline in css_pixels, the unit of the SVG’s outer viewport, and its time axis a child over the drawn segment, carrying the C-Map from css_pixels to the unit of the axis title, built through the labelled ticks (see :meth:~timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.create_calibrated_child).
The drawing’s length is its content extent, because a child lies within its parent: the viewport width, or the end of the axis’s farthest line where the axis runs past the viewport (ScoreWarp sets overflow="visible").
Known limits: the extent of text is not counted, since no font metrics are read, and nothing but the axis is read; the score’s own elements and the transforms that place them are left alone.


>>> loader = ScoreWarpLoader.from_file("warped.svg")
>>> drawing = loader.create_timeline()
>>> axis = drawing.get_child(drawing.list_children()[0])
>>> cmap = axis.get_conversion_map("seconds")

title: RepoVizzLoader
text:
loader.RepoVizzLoader(seed=None)
Load RepoVizz XML manifests or single CSV files for creating physical timelines.
RepoVizzLoader supports two modes:
XML Manifest Mode (when loading a .xml file): Parses the RepoVizz XML manifest and builds a catalogue of all data files in the recording directory. Provides lazy access to: - Audio recordings (ambient + pickup) - Essentia audio descriptors - Bowing gesture descriptors - MoCap position data - Score alignment files (.notes)
Legacy CSV Mode (when loading a .csv file): Reads the 2-line RepoVizz CSV format for a single sensor signal. This preserves backwards compatibility with existing code.
Both modes create :class:DiscretePhysicalTimeline instances with the samples unit and an attached SamplesToSeconds conversion map.


XML manifest mode::
>>> loader = RepoVizzLoader.from_file("StringQuartetEEP_I_Normal.xml")
>>> loader.groups
['audio', 'descriptors', 'mocap', 'score']
>>> loader.timeline_ids[:5]
['ROOT0_Audi1_Audi0_Ambi0', 'ROOT0_Audi1_Audi0_Ambi1', ...]

>>> tl = loader.create_timeline("ROOT0_Audi1_Audi0_Ambi0")
>>> tl.length
Coordinate(11753638, samples)
Legacy CSV mode::
>>> loader = RepoVizzLoader.from_file("vln1_bb_angle.csv")
>>> loader.n_samples
63965
>>> loader.frame_rate
240

Abstract base class for coordinate conversion maps.
A ConversionMap transforms coordinates from one representation to another. Maps are callable and support both scalar and array inputs.
The key methods are: - call(value): Convert a single value or array - inverse(): Get the inverse map (if invertible)

>>> # Create a map that doubles values
>>> linear = LinearMap(scalar=2.0)
>>> linear(5.0)
10.0
>>> # Maps are callable
>>> linear(np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]))
array([2., 4., 6.])
>>> # Get the inverse
>>> inv = linear.inverse()
>>> inv(10.0)

This is the public API for array conversion, used by the timestamp system and other batch operations. It delegates to _convert_array().

ConversionMap.from_pairs(
    pairs,
    *,
    source_unit,
    value_unit=None,
    origin=0,
    seed=None,
)
Build the map a law reads from calibration pairs.
Each pair holds a position and the value it reads on the target axis. Positions are given in coordinates where the map’s source axis starts at origin: the map reads position - origin, while the pairs are checked against the law on the positions as given, where their rounding happened. Values are coordinates carrying the one unit they share, or numbers in value_unit. A map class that is a law of calibration implements this; the pairs it receives are checked against the law, never fitted to it.
Exactness is a property of the whole calibration. When every position and value is exact (an int or a Fraction), the pairs must lie on the law exactly. Otherwise, exact and float numbers may mix, and a position may miss the one at which the law reads its value by the error a position computed in doubles may carry, a bound derived by forward error analysis in ulps of the positions and of the span.

Build the map a law reads from calibration pairs.
Each pair holds a position and the value it reads on the target axis. Positions are given in coordinates where the map’s source axis starts at origin: the map reads position - origin, while the pairs are checked against the law on the positions as given, where their rounding happened. Values are coordinates carrying the one unit they share, or numbers in value_unit. A map class that is a law of calibration implements this; the pairs it receives are checked against the law, never fitted to it.
Exactness is a property of the whole calibration. When every position and value is exact (an int or a Fraction), the pairs must lie on the law exactly. EventRegistry(timeline_id, data, *, host=None)
The registry rows of the events of one or more families, as a view.
A view is a filter over the families it reads, read when asked: it follows the rows as they change. :attr:table holds one row per event in the columns of :data:REGISTRY_SCHEMA, positions on each family’s root axis; :meth:content the content of the events of one kind. The rows recording where a child lies (:data:SEGMENT_KIND) are no events and no view shows them.
Rows come in through the doors of package readers and loaders, on a view too: :meth:add_rows (rows read from a package), :meth:update (a parser’s new run, :meth:update_target the timeline it updates); writers read through :meth:written. A timeline adds its own rows through :meth:Timeline.add_events <timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.add_events>.

EventRegistry.add_rows(rows, contents=None, extractions=(), *, registered=True)
Hold registry rows already on the root’s axis, as read from a package.
Each row joins the family of the timeline it names, among the families this registry (a view too: a timeline’s, a group’s, a bundle’s) reads. loader.graphical.PiecewisePath(pieces)
A time axis made of consecutive pieces, read one after the other.
The path of a score page is piecewise: each accolade is one horizontal line, and the page’s time runs along the first, then along the second, and so on. Each piece starts on the path where the pieces before it end (:attr:offsets); the path’s length is the sum of its pieces’ lengths. All numbers are the pieces’ own: pieces of integers give an integer path.

title: ATONLoader
text:
loader.graphical.aton.ATONLoader(seed=None)
Load ATON format files (piano roll analysis data).
ATON (Artistic Text-based Object Notation) is a structured text format used by the Stanford SUPRA project for storing piano roll analysis data including hole punch positions and metadata.
The loader parses ROLLINFO metadata and HOLE blocks, providing access to both individual hole data and aggregate statistics.


>>> from timetoalign.testdata import ensure_data
>>> roll = ensure_data("supra") / "image" / "fd660zf8362_analysis.txt"
>>> loader = ATONLoader().load(roll)
>>> loader.rollinfo['MUSICAL_HOLES']
30092
>>> len(loader.holes)
30092
Hole positions are pixel coordinates on the scanned roll:
>>> loader.first_hole
Coordinate(15343, pixels)
>>> loader.last_hole
Coordinate(293119, pixels)

loader.graphical.aton.ATONLoader.create_timeline(uid=None, name=None)
Create a timeline populated with hole events.
Creates a graphical timeline (in pixels) spanning the full image height, with all parsed holes as InstantEvents at their absolute pixel coordinates.
This is the primary timeline for the piano roll image. To get a relative coordinate view (first hole = 0), create an inherited DiscreteGraphicalTimeline child at first_hole.
Each event is named by its hole’s @ID, which is also its ID. The SUPRA analysis software gives every hole that is no note the key 0 and counts per tracker-bar hole, so holes on different tracker holes can share one @ID (K0_N1). Such an @ID names no one hole: each hole holding it keeps it as its name and is given an ID minted from the loader’s minter (hole_…). Two holes of one @ID on one tracker hole are refused: the loader does not decide that a repeated block is one hole.

title: FlowControlView
text:
timelines.FlowControlView(elements=(), *, unit=None, number_type=None)
Flow-control elements on one axis, read only, in canonical order.
A view holds :class:FlowControlElement objects, ordered by coordinate and then by ID, and reads them as flow control: the views by class (jumps, jump_targets, breaks, section_breaks, barlines), the Jump at a coordinate, the place a destination goes on at, the elements a reading keeps. Nothing changes what a view holds. :class:FlowControlRegistry, the flow control a timeline states, is the view that elements are added to; :attr:Timeline.tree_flow_control <timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.tree_flow_control> is the view of a timeline’s flow control together with that of its descendants, which is what playing the timeline reads.
A view refuses, as a registry does, what cannot be played among the elements not rejected: a second Jump at a coordinate, a to naming neither a :class:JumpTarget held nor a place the view knows, an after that does not name exactly one destination of another Jump held, an element or a place before 0. Two elements under one ID are refused too.

Return where destination of jump goes on.

title: AudioLoader
text:
loader.AudioLoader(seed=None)
Load audio file metadata for creating physical timelines.
AudioLoader extracts metadata from audio files without loading the actual sample data. This is efficient for creating physical timelines that represent audio files in the TimeToAlign! framework.
The loader automatically: - Tries its backends in order, exact counts first: soundfile, then for WAV files the built-in wave module and a RIFF header parser, then mutagen - Extracts sample count, sample rate, channels, and format info - Creates a samples timeline with a SamplesToSeconds C-map (create_timeline) or a seconds timeline with a SecondsToSamples C-map (create_continuous_timeline)
Supported formats depend on installed backends: - soundfile: WAV, FLAC, OGG, AIFF, MP3 (libsndfile >= 1.1), and many more - wave (builtin) and the RIFF header parser: WAV only - mutagen: MP3, M4A, FLAC, OGG, and more


mutagen states only a duration, so its sample count is the estimate round(duration * sample_rate). For an MP3 the duration counts whole MPEG frames, encoder delay and padding included, or, without a VBR header, is guessed from the file size and bitrate, so the estimate can miss the decoded count in either direction. It is used only when soundfile is not installed or cannot read the file; audio_info.backend names the backend that answered, and the timeline’s metadata carries it.
An MP4 (M4A) file states its count: the loader reads the first sound track’s boxes. The media duration (mdhd) counts every coded sample, the encoder’s priming and padding included; a single edit of the media (elst) states the audio as played, and so does an iTunSMPB tag where there is no edit list. audio_info.extra["sample_count_from"] names the statement used. Where the file states neither, the media count stands: nothing is subtracted by rule, so a track whose priming is stated nowhere is counted with it. An edit list of several edits (an empty edit, more than one segment) is not interpreted and keeps the media count.
The RIFF header parser derives the block size from the bit depth and channel count rather than reading the header’s block align, so without a fact chunk it miscounts samples not packed in whole bytes.
Where mutagen’s stream info has no channels attribute the loader assumes 2; a stated 0, mutagen’s default for several formats, is refused.
A WAV truncated below the size its data chunk states gets a backend-dependent count: soundfile counts the frames present, the other backends answer the header’s count.



>>> loader = AudioLoader()
>>> loader.load("recording.wav")
>>> loader.n_samples
7938000
>>> loader.sample_rate
44100
>>> loader.duration_seconds
180.0
>>> # Create a timeline
>>> timeline = loader.create_timeline(uid="my_audio")
>>> timeline.unit
<TimeUnit.samples: 'samples'>
>>> timeline.length
Coordinate(7938000, samples)

title: FlowManifestation
text:
core.FlowManifestation()
What a flow-control element looks like in the score.
A manifestation names the sign a source prints for an element or for a destination of a Jump. It is optional everywhere and nothing computes with it: the flow follows from the elements’ classes, places and conditions alone. A word outside this vocabulary is kept as given.
Which words each class of :mod:timetoalign.timelines.flowcontrol admits:

a destination of a Jump: repeat_end, da_capo, da_capo_al_fine, da_capo_al_coda, dal_segno, dal_segno_al_fine, dal_segno_al_coda, to_coda, volta, ossia;

a Break: fine, volta;
a Barline: double_barline, final_barline;
a SectionBreak: none.

title: TimelineGroup
text:
timelines.TimelineGroup(
    id=None,
    name=None,
    timelines=None,
    meta=None,
    styling=None,
    *,
    seed=None,
)
An array of timelines sharing one graphical start and end point.
By definition every member’s 0 coincides with every other member’s 0 and every member’s length with every other member’s length; a position in between converts linearly. Position p on member A is p · len_B / len_A on member B, computed exactly — a float enters as its exact dyadic Fraction — and written in B’s declared number type.
When only part of a timeline participates, the participant is a child of that timeline: the child carries its exact offset, and the child is the member. A member is never placed partially.
A member may be of unknown length: membership states that it shares the group’s start and end, wherever that end lies. Carrying a position between two members needs both lengths, so such a conversion raises UnknownLengthError; one member’s length is never carried to another.
Members keep the order in which they were added.

Type
Description

str

timelines.TimelineGroup.add_timeline(timeline)
Add a member; its whole extent [0, length] spans the group.
A member’s 0 coincides with every other member’s 0 and its length with every other member’s length. To let only part of a timeline participate, add the child of that timeline covering the part.
Every id in the newcomer’s manifest tree (its root and all that root’s descendants, with their maps, regions and flow-control elements) must be free in the group’s trees: the group’s members share one manifest, in which every id is unique. While the group lives, an element added to a member’s tree takes its id in that manifest too. A bundle holding the group holds every member, so the newcomer joins each bundle holding the group as well, its ids free in the bundle’s manifest too.
A newcomer that is an ancestor or a descendant of a member is refused: a child sits at its offset inside its parent, so the two cannot share one start and end. Every check runs before anything changes, so a refused newcomer is left as it was.
A segment line is locked when it joins, as when it becomes a child.

Type

Default

required

>>> from timetoalign.timelines import TimelineGroup
>>> from timetoalign.timelines.types import (
...     ContinuousPhysicalTimeline,
...     DiscreteGraphicalTimeline,

>>> image = DiscreteGraphicalTimeline(length=5000, uid="roll")
>>> holes = DiscreteGraphicalTimeline(length=2000, uid="holes")

timelines.TimelineGroup.from_dict(data, *, group_id=None, name=None)
Read a group from a TimeToShare manifest.

A manifest of one root timeline and no group makes a group of that timeline; group_id or name (or both) must be given.
An anonymous bundle with one group reads that group. Arguments naming it select it; arguments naming nothing override its id and name; given both, they must agree, both naming the group or neither.

In these two cases the manifest is read as a whole: its meta, statements, graphical and unknown keys are kept so that :meth:to_dict writes them back, around the anonymous bundle a group writes; a statement naming the group by an id it overrides names it by the new one. - From a manifest with several groups, or a named one, group_id or name (or both) must be given and select the one group whose id and name match them. The rest of the manifest is left behind: a value of a statement of the group’s trees naming a timeline or region outside them is dropped, with its provenance.
A group is read with the timelines its members need: each member id is resolved among the manifest’s roots and all their descendants, and the members are added in the group’s graphical.order entry (in members order without one). When the manifest is read as a whole, graphical’s other keys are kept as :attr:styling, and the entries of graphical.order keyed by a timeline, its band orders, are kept too, both unread. Keys the library does not know are kept on the object read from the JSON object they were found in, and written back.

timelines.TimelineGroup.add_timeline(timeline)
Add a member; its whole extent [0, length] spans the group.
A member’s 0 coincides with every other member’s 0 and its length with every other member’s length. To let only part of a timeline participate, add the child of that timeline covering the part.
Every id in the newcomer’s manifest tree (its root and all that root’s descendants, with their maps, regions and flow-control elements) must be free in the group’s trees: the group’s members share one manifest, in which every id is unique. While the group lives, an element added to a member’s tree takes its id in that manifest too. A bundle holding the group holds every member, so the newcomer joins each bundle holding the group as well, its ids free in the bundle’s manifest too.
A newcomer that is an ancestor or a descendant of a member is refused: a child sits at its offset inside its parent, so the two cannot share one start and end. Every check runs before anything changes, so a refused newcomer is left as it was.
A segment line is locked when it joins, as when it becomes a child.

timelines.TimelineGroup.from_dict(data, *, group_id=None, name=None)
Read a group from a TimeToShare manifest.

A manifest of one root timeline and no group makes a group of that timeline; group_id or name (or both) must be given.
An anonymous bundle with one group reads that group. Arguments naming it select it; arguments naming nothing override its id and name; given both, they must agree, both naming the group or neither.

In these two cases the manifest is read as a whole: its meta, statements, graphical and unknown keys are kept so that :meth:to_dict writes them back, around the anonymous bundle a group writes; a statement naming the group by an id it overrides names it by the new one. - From a manifest with several groups, or a named one, group_id or name (or both) must be given and select the one group whose id and name match them. The rest of the manifest is left behind: a value of a statement of the group’s trees naming a timeline or region outside them is dropped, with its provenance.
A group is read with the timelines its members need: each member id is resolved among the manifest’s roots and all their descendants, and the members are added in the group’s graphical.order entry (in members order without one). When the manifest is read as a whole, graphical’s other keys are kept as :attr:styling, and the entries of graphical.order keyed by a timeline, its band orders, are kept too, both unread. Keys the library does not know are kept on the object read from the JSON object they were found in, and written back.

The group is written with every timeline it needs: "timelines" holds the root of each member’s tree — a member that is a child contributes its root, which holds it — each a timeline object as :meth:Timeline.to_dict <timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.to_dict> writes it, sorted by id. The group itself holds no statements: the format keeps them off groups. Write the object’s manifest to a file.
The manifest is to_dict’s complete form, written with timetoshare.dumps_file in the form, styling and serialization chosen: every object’s keys sorted, its arrays in canonical order, so that equal manifests give equal text and a change shows in a diff as the lines it touches. Each argument left None takes the value the file the object was read from had (see :meth:from_file); for an object not read from a file, the minimal form, the styling included, in canonical YAML, without event rows or external references. An :class:~timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle holding MatchClaims or Projections writes its tables beside the manifest and names them in its resources: its manifest is written (validated and serialized) once before any table, and once more naming the tables written. EventData(table, unit, number_type=None)
PyArrow-based storage for timeline events.
EventData wraps a PyArrow table containing events. Events are rows in the table, not Python wrapper objects. The primary API is bulk operations:

from_dicts(): Create from list of row dictionaries
from_arrays(): Create from field-oriented arrays
from_dataframe(): Create from pandas DataFrame

The schema is fixed at class definition time but can be extended by subclasses to add domain-specific fields (e.g., pitch, velocity for notes).
NOTE: This class was renamed from EventStore to EventData in the 2026-01 API refactoring. EventStore now refers to the container class (formerly EventBundle) that holds one or more EventData tables.

...      "start": 0.0, "end": 1.0},
... ], unit=TimeUnit.seconds)

text:
loader.format.JsonLoader(
    principal_keys=None,
    *,
    sep='.',
    resolve_lookups=True,
    **kwargs,
)
Configurable JSON normaliser producing flat pa.Table objects.
JsonLoader parses one or more JSON files and normalises their nested structures into flat PyArrow tables stored in a timetoalign.storage.store.DictStore.
Principal keys determine which top-level arrays become tables:

If principal_keys is given (a list of strings, possibly dotted for nested paths like "cueData.hotCuePoints"), only those keys are normalised.
If principal_keys is None (the default), every top-level key whose value is a list of dicts is auto-detected and normalised.

Non-principal top-level keys whose values are lists of dicts are kept as lookup tables and used to resolve foreign-key fields (fields ending in _id) automatically. For example, if annotations rows contain image_id and there is a top-level images array, the loader appends image.file_name, image.width, etc. to the annotations table.
Scalar top-level keys (like "width": 604) are stored as table- level metadata on every resulting pa.Table.
A row’s locator is the JSON Pointer of the object it was read from (/audio/0; /audio/1/cueData/hotCuePoints/0 for a nested key), followed by key:<id> where the object states an id member of its own (/audio/0 key:a1); a row read from a file names that file’s extraction (:attr:extractions), one read from a dict none.
Follows the standard two-phase pattern:

loader.load(*sources) – parse JSON files.
loader.get_table(key) – retrieve a normalised table.












Name
Type
Description
Default




principal_keys
list[str] | None
List of keys to normalise. None for auto-detect.
None


sep
str
Separator for flattened nested key names. Default ".".
'.'


resolve_lookups
bool
Whether to resolve *_id foreign keys. Default True.
True






Auto-detect all array keys::
loader = JsonLoader()
loader.load("Wagner_WWV086B_140.json")
for name in loader.store.keys():
    print(name, loader.get_table(name).num_rows)
Specify principal key::
loader = JsonLoader(principal_keys=["audio"])
loader.load("dj_studio_data.json")
assert loader.get_table("audio").num_rows == 3
Nested principal key::
loader = JsonLoader(principal_keys=["hotCuePoints"])
loader.load("dj_studio_data.json")
# Collects hotCuePoints from audio[*].cueData.hotCuePoints

loader.format.JsonLoader.load(*sources)
Load and accept one or more sources through the shared template.
Each source is a filesystem path (Path or str) or a member of a ZIP archive (zipfile.Path), which is read without extracting the archive. Its entry in metadata["sources"] records path (for a member: the archive’s absolute path, and member, the member’s path inside it) and loaded_at.
Every ID the loader mints (events, timelines, maps, MatchClaims, Projections) comes from its :class:~timetoalign.core.ids.IdMinter, in the order the loader builds them. Every load call seeds a new one: the first call after the loader is made or cleared from the loader’s seed when one was given, else from :func:~timetoalign.core.ids.seed_from of the loader’s class name, its configuration (the constructor arguments that shape the events) and the SHA-256 digests of the call’s sources, in order; every later call from seed_from of the previous call’s seed and its own sources’ digests, so later sources count too. A fresh loader loading unchanged sources in the same calls mints the same IDs, in any process; IDs the source states are kept as they are.

title: AlignmentBundle
text:
alignment.AlignmentBundle(
    id='',
    name=None,
    timelines=dict(),
    groups=dict(),
    meta=dict(),
    support_policy=SupportPolicy.omit,
    styling=dict(),
    resources=list(),
    _warp_map_cache=dict(),
    _matchline_cache=dict(),
    _matchgraph_cache=dict(),
    _in_force_cache=dict(),
    _naming_cache=dict(),
    *,
    seed=None,
)
The primary entry point for all alignment workflows.
An AlignmentBundle manages timelines and their alignment relationships. Within a group, coordinate transfer uses linear interpolation (TimelineGroup.get_coordinate_at()). Across groups, transfer is mediated by the MatchClaim → MatchLine → WarpMap pipeline.
The bundle provides:

Timeline registration and lookup
Group management (collections of perfectly aligned timelines)
Coordinate transfer between any two timelines (same-group or cross-group via MatchClaim/WarpMap)

The alignment relationships and coordinates do not depend on the order in which timelines are added; the order of table rows and columns and of a stamp’s coordinates follows registration.





Name
Type
Description




id
str
Unique identifier for this bundle, minted with the prefix bundle unless given.


name
str | None
Optional human-readable name.


timelines
dict[str, 'Timeline']
Dictionary mapping timeline IDs to Timeline objects: every timeline added, and the root of every one that is a child. The other descendants of these roots are not listed, yet every getter answers for them as for the listed ones.


groups
dict[str, TimelineGroup]
Dictionary mapping group IDs to TimelineGroup objects. The groups are the one statement of membership; a timeline may be a member of several (see :attr:timeline_to_groups).


match_claim_table
MatchClaimField
The bundle’s MatchClaims, every kind, in one :class:~timetoalign.alignment.claims.MatchClaimField (the MatchClaim table), queried vectorized; a claim is materialised only where a reader needs the object. A MatchClaim is addressed by its id alone.


styling
dict[str, Any]
The members of the manifest’s graphical other than order (styles, rules, timestamps and any other), kept as given and never interpreted.


statements
dict[str, list[Any]]
What the manifest stands for, as property–value pairs, with their :attr:provenance (see :mod:~timetoalign.timelines.statements).


resources
list[Resource]
The files the manifest names (its resources), each a :class:~timetoalign.timelines.manifest.Resource: the MatchClaim table and the Projections table that :meth:to_file writes beside the manifest, and any other kept as read.






Every reader of the MatchClaims (queries, the matchstamp getters, the table getter :meth:get_matchstamp_table, the MatchLines and WarpMaps behind transfer) reads the one table, through the belief filter (believer, beliefs) where the reader takes it. Two bundles are equal when their claims are too: the tables are compared row by row, provenance included (:class:MatchClaimField equality).



>>> from timetoalign.alignment import AlignmentBundle
>>> from timetoalign.timelines.types import (
...     ContinuousLogicalTimeline,
...     ContinuousPhysicalTimeline,
... )
>>> bundle = AlignmentBundle()
>>> _ = bundle.add_timeline(ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=200, uid="score"))
>>> _ = bundle.add_timeline(
...     ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=91.0, uid="audio"), grouped_with="score"
... )
>>> stamp = bundle.get_matchstamp_at(100, "score")
>>> stamp.get_coordinate_for("audio", format="float")

alignment.AlignmentBundle.create_match_claims(
    event_pairs,
    *,
    synchronous=True,
    certainty=1.0,
    provenance=None,
    actor=None,
    date=None,
)
Create MatchClaims between events, projecting a side that has none.
A MatchClaim connects two sides. Each tuple (event_a, timeline_a_id, event_b, timeline_b_id) names one side per timeline, each side one of:

the id of an event its timeline (or a descendant of it) holds: the timeline’s own event answers for its ID; an ID the timeline does not hold and two of its descendants do names no one event and is refused (name the descendant holding the event instead);
an event dict whose id its timeline holds: that event;
an event dict stating a position: start, and end for a span, each a number on the timeline’s axis or a :class:~timetoalign.core.Coordinate in any unit one of the timeline’s C-Maps converts, and optionally name. On a timeline counting samples a position is an int or a Coordinate, never a bare float. A span runs forward (end at or after start). A Projection stands for the side there, on the timeline’s axis (:meth:Timeline.add_projections): under the dict’s id (an event the bundle does not hold, projection_of null), or, without one, naming the other side’s event in projection_of when the other side is an event its timeline holds (null when the other side is NOMATCH or both sides are positions of a conceptual pair). The timeline keeps one Projection per event and position: a second call with the same pairs reuses every Projection the first added. An id the timeline already holds names that event; given with start/end, they must be the event’s own span. The name is the claim’s name of the Projection: the name the first claim on a Projection recorded is the one every later claim on it shows. Where both sides of a synchronous pair are dicts without id, no Projection stands for either: both sides are :data:~timetoalign.core.ids.CHUNK, the claim’s anchor holding the two positions (an interval where both state an end; a name names the stated position and is kept as that side’s event_X_name);
:data:~timetoalign.core.ids.NOMATCH, the NOMATCH sentinel, on one side at most.

The MatchClaim is then made between the two sides, on the two timelines’ own axes (:meth:MatchClaim.from_events); an end on both sides makes an interval claim. A pair with NOMATCH makes a NOMATCH claim for the other side’s event (:meth:MatchClaim.nomatch), its id minted at its construction. The claims join the bundle (:meth:add_match_claims).
Every pair is checked before any Projection is added, so a refusal leaves the bundle and its timelines unchanged: the timelines are the bundle’s, an id names an event of its timeline, at most one side is NOMATCH, every position is placed on its timeline’s axis. A position, a Projection’s or a CHUNK side’s, never lengthens a locked timeline (a loader locks a timeline whose source states its length, such as a recording’s): a position past its end is refused. An unlocked timeline grows to hold it where its parent contains the new end (a parent never grows with its child); a position past an end the parent cannot contain is refused, as is one past where the parent ends a child of unknown length.

Coordinate input is the primary interface for cross-domain coordinate transfer and returns coordinates on every connected timeline. Interval input resolves its endpoints through that same coordinate lane and combines the two results.
A coordinate stamp is the transitive cross-group union reachable from the query. Exact-anchor coordinates from the coordinate’s MatchGraph are overlaid first (exact wins over interpolated), then the assembly walks outward across groups to closure: every reached timeline expands into its own group (by interpolation) and warps into not-yet-reached groups (by WarpMap). is_interpolated is False exactly when the query node itself carries an anchor a claim states.
A timeline whose transferred coordinate falls outside alignment support — the entering coordinate lies outside the transferring WarpMap’s source-anchor hull, or the produced coordinate would fall outside [0, length] — is handled by support_policy. Get a table of MatchStamps for alignment queries.
Analogous to get_timestamp_table() but for cross-group alignment. Fields are timeline IDs holding their coordinate values; what a row is depends on from_graph:

from_graph=False (default) — one row per alignment anchor: an instant claim gives one, an interval claim two (its start anchor, then its end anchor). A row fills exactly two cells and leaves the rest null, so a dense pairwise alignment produces sparse rows.
from_graph=True — one row per connected component of the (timeline_id, coordinate) graph the anchors induce, end anchors included. The pairwise rows above collapse into the cross-section they describe: one row per aligned instant, every participating timeline filled.

When claims is None the claims are the bundle’s :attr:match_claim_table, read column by column — no MatchClaim is materialised. Every coordinate is written as the claim holds it, on its timeline’s axis (a claim is checked against its timelines when it is added), so no cell is converted here. The belief filter (believer, beliefs) selects the claims either way.
When at is given instead of claims, each position or event ID is resolved through :meth:get_matchstamp_at and becomes exactly one row — a full transitive cross-section, every reached timeline filled — in input order. from_graph does not apply on this path (the stamps are already collapsed cross-sections) and is ignored.
