alignment.AlignmentBundle.create_match_claims(
    event_pairs,
    *,
    synchronous=True,
    certainty=1.0,
    provenance=None,
    actor=None,
    date=None,
)
Create MatchClaims between events, projecting a side that has none.
A MatchClaim connects two sides. Each tuple (event_a, timeline_a_id, event_b, timeline_b_id) names one side per timeline, each side one of:

the id of an event its timeline (or a descendant of it) holds: the timeline’s own event answers for its ID; an ID the timeline does not hold and two of its descendants do names no one event and is refused (name the descendant holding the event instead);
an event dict whose id its timeline holds: that event;
an event dict stating a position: start, and end for a span, each a number on the timeline’s axis or a :class:~timetoalign.core.Coordinate in any unit one of the timeline’s C-Maps converts, and optionally name. On a timeline counting samples a position is an int or a Coordinate, never a bare float. A span runs forward (end at or after start). A Projection stands for the side there, on the timeline’s axis (:meth:Timeline.add_projections): under the dict’s id (an event the bundle does not hold, projection_of null), or, without one, naming the other side’s event in projection_of when the other side is an event its timeline holds (null when the other side is NOMATCH or both sides are positions of a conceptual pair). The timeline keeps one Projection per event and position: a second call with the same pairs reuses every Projection the first added. An id the timeline already holds names that event; given with start/end, they must be the event’s own span. The name is the claim’s name of the Projection: the name the first claim on a Projection recorded is the one every later claim on it shows. Where both sides of a synchronous pair are dicts without id, no Projection stands for either: both sides are :data:~timetoalign.core.ids.CHUNK, the claim’s anchor holding the two positions (an interval where both state an end; a name names the stated position and is kept as that side’s event_X_name);
:data:~timetoalign.core.ids.NOMATCH, the NOMATCH sentinel, on one side at most.

The MatchClaim is then made between the two sides, on the two timelines’ own axes (:meth:MatchClaim.from_events); an end on both sides makes an interval claim. A pair with NOMATCH makes a NOMATCH claim for the other side’s event (:meth:MatchClaim.nomatch), its id minted at its construction. The claims join the bundle (:meth:add_match_claims).
Every pair is checked before any Projection is added, so a refusal leaves the bundle and its timelines unchanged: the timelines are the bundle’s, an id names an event of its timeline, at most one side is NOMATCH, every position is placed on its timeline’s axis. A position, a Projection’s or a CHUNK side’s, never lengthens a locked timeline (a loader locks a timeline whose source states its length, such as a recording’s): a position past its end is refused. An unlocked timeline grows to hold it where its parent contains the new end (a parent never grows with its child); a position past an end the parent cannot contain is refused, as is one past where the parent ends a child of unknown length.

Read a bundle from any TimeToShare manifest.
The manifest’s id becomes the bundle’s (a manifest without id, named or anonymous, gives a bundle whose minted id :meth:to_dict never writes), its name and meta the bundle’s. Get a cross-group match stamp for a position on a timeline.
Coordinate input is the primary interface for cross-domain coordinate transfer and returns coordinates on every connected timeline. Interval input resolves its endpoints through that same coordinate lane and combines the two results.
A coordinate stamp is the transitive cross-group union reachable from the query. Exact-anchor coordinates from the coordinate’s MatchGraph are overlaid first (exact wins over interpolated), then the assembly walks outward across groups to closure: every reached timeline expands into its own group (by interpolation) and warps into not-yet-reached groups (by WarpMap). is_interpolated is False exactly when the query node itself carries an anchor a claim states.
A timeline whose transferred coordinate falls outside alignment support — the entering coordinate lies outside the transferring WarpMap’s source-anchor hull, or the produced coordinate would fall outside [0, length] — is handled by support_policy. Get a table of MatchStamps for alignment queries.
Analogous to get_timestamp_table() but for cross-group alignment. Fields are timeline IDs holding their coordinate values; what a row is depends on from_graph:

from_graph=False (default) — one row per alignment anchor: an instant claim gives one, an interval claim two (its start anchor, then its end anchor). A row fills exactly two cells and leaves the rest null, so a dense pairwise alignment produces sparse rows.
from_graph=True — one row per connected component of the (timeline_id, coordinate) graph the anchors induce, end anchors included. The pairwise rows above collapse into the cross-section they describe: one row per aligned instant, every participating timeline filled.

When claims is None the claims are the bundle’s :attr:match_claim_table, read column by column — no MatchClaim is materialised. Every coordinate is written as the claim holds it, on its timeline’s axis (a claim is checked against its timelines when it is added), so no cell is converted here. The belief filter (believer, beliefs) selects the claims either way.
When at is given instead of claims, each position or event ID is resolved through :meth:get_matchstamp_at and becomes exactly one row — a full transitive cross-section, every reached timeline filled — in input order. from_graph does not apply on this path (the stamps are already collapsed cross-sections) and is ignored.

title: Package

alignment.Package(id=None, name=None)
A TimeToShare package: a folder of manifests sharing their tables.
package.yaml at the folder’s root lists the package’s manifests and its tables: the registry (registry/, as this class writes it: an part of the non-event rows non_events.parquet, one per manifest element, MatchClaim and extraction, and one part per extraction of its event rows, each position on the axis of its timeline’s root), the Extraction table (tables/extractions.parquet), one pre-parsed table per kind of event (tables/<Kind>/, each event’s content keyed by its ID, without positions) and the MatchClaim table (tables/MatchClaim/). A manifest names the registry and the MatchClaim table in its resources, with the timelines whose rows it keeps; nothing in a file names a manifest. An event ID is held once among all events of the package, every kind; a MatchClaim ID once among its MatchClaims; a timeline ID, as this class writes a package, by one manifest.
:meth:from_file opens a package; :meth:bundle reads one of its manifests as an :class:~timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle, every table filtered by the timelines its resources list and the events’ content read when first asked for. :meth:write_bundle writes a bundle into the package as one of its manifests, and :meth:to_file writes a new package where it is told.

alignment.Package.write_bundle(bundle, url)
Write bundle into the package as its manifest at url.
The manifest lies at url under the package’s root, its resources naming the registry (registry/, relative to it, without size or digest, since other manifests’ rows share it) with the timelines holding its events, and the MatchClaim table (tables/MatchClaim/) with the timelines its MatchClaims name; a resource that is no table (a recording) is kept. A table the bundle carries (a table resource of a type it does not read, or a MatchClaim table it holds no rows of) is copied into the package with its bytes, at tables/<Type>/ under its own name (a name holding other content: one seeded from the table’s content), listed in package.yaml, and its resource names the copy; one lying in the package already stays where it lies, and equal content lying at its name is that copy. The format reads such a table as the pre-parsed table of its type, keyed by id: a Parquet table without an id column of strings is the package check’s foreign_table, so writing the package raises it and restores the package, while a folder holding no Parquet file (scans, recordings) is carried. A table resource of a type the bundle holds no rows of and does not carry is refused: the writer has no file to copy.
Its events of every kind (:func:~timetoalign.timelines.manifest.event_tables) go into the registry: one part per extraction, registry/<extraction ID>.parquet (an ID that is no plain file name: part_ and 13 base-36 characters minted from it), holding that extraction’s rows of every manifest, sorted by timeline_id, exact start and id; a part holding the extraction already takes the new rows in, rewritten whole. Their extractions go into the Extraction table (tables/extractions.parquet, each extraction once, its source written as a path from the package’s root where the file lies under it, else as its file: URI, so that the package names no path of the machine that wrote it; read back, the source is the file’s path again), their content into the pre-parsed table of their kind and their MatchClaims (each row with its own provenance) into the MatchClaim table: each write adds one new file per kind and one of MatchClaims, tables/<Type>/part_<13 base-36 characters>.parquet, holding the rows of every bundle it writes (:meth:to_file writes every bundle staged at once), named from its content through the library’s ID minter, so that a rebuild names its files again; a column two bundles hold in two types is held in the one type holding both exactly (an int8 and an int64 column as int64), never in a type that may change a value. Last, the registry’s non-event rows are written from the manifests and tables (timetoshare.tables.write_non_event_rows). A manifest the package holds at url already is replaced: the rows of its timelines and of the bundle’s leave the files holding them (a pre-parsed row by the ID of its event), each such file rewritten whole (one left without a row removed), the other manifests’ rows kept; its MatchClaims must be kept by the bundle, as :meth:MatchClaimField.to_parquet <timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaimField.to_parquet> requires, so a bundle holding none while the package holds MatchClaims of that manifest is refused, and an extraction once written stays in the Extraction table.
Before anything is written, every ID is checked in memory: each event ID among every event of the package, every kind; each MatchClaim ID among its MatchClaims; each timeline ID among the timelines of its other manifests. A collision is refused, naming the ID and both holders; nothing is renamed. A new package (not written yet) stages the bundle, which :meth:to_file writes: the bundle’s own IDs are checked against an index of the IDs staged, so staging N bundles costs in the number of their rows. A package lying on disk (:meth:from_file, or written by :meth:to_file) is written at once, package.yaml with it, and each call reads the id and timeline columns of every file of the package, rewrites every file holding a row of the manifest replaced, and checks the package whole (:func:timetoshare.tables.package_problems): its cost grows with the package, so a package of many manifests is built new, staging every bundle and writing them with one :meth:to_file. Once written, the bundle’s :attr:resources <timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.resources> are the manifest’s, and the tables it carries the package’s copies.
A refusal leaves the package as it was, on disk and in memory: what can be checked in memory is checked before any file is written (the IDs, the bundle’s resources, an opened package’s format version); the new files are written under names readers skip and renamed into place once the old rows are removed; and where the write or the package check after it fails, every file rewritten gets its bytes back, every new file is removed. This holds for an exception, not for a process killed between the removal of the old rows and the renaming of the new files: the package then lacks the rows of the manifests written, until they are written again (:meth:from_file removes the new files left hidden).

required

title: PartituraLoader
text:
loader.score.PartituraLoader(**kwargs)
Load symbolic scores using partitura.
Supports MusicXML (fully typed) and MIDI (quantized). Returns ScoreStore with category-specific data.
A note keeps the ID its file states (MusicXML id, MEI xml:id, a match file’s score-note ID); a note without one, and every note of a format that states none (kern, MIDI), gets an ID minted by the loader’s minter. Partitura’s own numbering (n0, P1-s1-v1-el3) is never an ID.
All TTA timelines start at coordinate 0. When partitura reports negative quarter-beat onsets (anacrusis notes that precede the first full measure), this loader shifts every event coordinate so that the earliest onset maps to 0.0. The magnitude of that shift is available as :attr:anacrusis_offset and is also stored in ScoreStore.metadata["anacrusis_offset"] so that downstream consumers (e.g. MatchfileLoader) can apply the same correction when comparing raw partitura coordinates against this loader’s stored values.
The shift is equivalent to the offset of a ShiftMap whose forward direction is raw_partitura_coord → TTA_coord (i.e. adding the offset). Its InverseMap (subtracting the offset) converts TTA coordinates back to raw partitura space when needed.





Name
Description




anacrusis_offset
Quarter-beat shift applied to normalise anacrusis coordinates.

A ConversionMap that returns a constant value for any input.
Used to associate a fixed label (e.g., a filename) with every coordinate on a timeline. Typically used inside a timetoalign.CombinationMap to pair a numeric conversion (pixels to seconds) with a string label (source image filename).

IntervalToConstantMap(
    boundaries,
    values,
    end=None,
    source_unit=None,
    target_unit=None,
    uid=None,
    name=None,
    seed=None,
)
Interval-to-constant map: each interval [x_i, x_{i+1}) maps to value_i.
Unlike TableMap, IntervalToConstantMap does not interpolate. A coordinate x returns the value associated with the interval that contains x.
Values can be any type (string, int, float, etc.). This is NOT a coordinate conversion map when values are non-numeric (e.g., string labels).
Without an end the map is total: a position before the first boundary takes the first value, and the last interval has no end. With an end the map is defined on [boundaries[0], end) only, the form a manifest can hold for labels: a PiecewiseMap of ConstantMaps. Without an end, a map of numbers is written as a TableMap of kind previous (a ConstantMap for a single boundary), and a map of labels with more than one boundary cannot be written.
This is useful for: - Measure number lookup (quarters -> MN label) - Region/section lookup (coordinate -> section name) - Any step-function relationship

A synchronized timestamp across multiple timelines.
A MatchStamp represents a single coordinate (or instant) that has been synchronized across multiple timelines by the anchors MatchClaims state and/or by edges the MatchGraph inferred through group membership.
Contains one coordinate per participating timeline, each pair of timelines linked by a stated or an inferred edge.

title: AlignmentAnchor
text:
alignment.AlignmentAnchor()
A coordinate pair associating one coordinate on timeline A with one coordinate on timeline B.
A neutral record with no claim semantics. AlignmentAnchors are value objects: two anchors with the same coordinates and timeline IDs are equivalent regardless of how they were created.
Each coordinate is kept as given. An anchor knows its timelines only by id; the claim holding it checks both coordinates against the two timelines (:meth:MatchClaim.check_on_timelines), since only the timeline knows its declared number type.
Only synchronous MatchClaim instances produce AlignmentAnchors. Non-synchronous claims (conceptual matches, NOMATCH) have no anchors.

title: XmlLoader
text:
loader.format.XmlLoader(
    principal_tags=None,
    *,
    sep='.',
    include_text=True,
    propagate_ancestors=True,
    seed=None,
)
Configurable XML normaliser producing flat pa.Table objects.
XmlLoader parses one or more XML files and normalises their nested element structures into flat PyArrow tables stored in a timetoalign.storage.store.DictStore.
Principal tags determine which element types become tables:

If principal_tags is given (a list of tag names), only elements with those tags are collected and normalised.
If principal_tags is None (the default), tags appearing at least twice in the document are auto-detected as principal.

Each element’s attributes become fields. Nested child elements are flattened with dot-separated field names. Ancestor attributes are propagated downward with parent_<tag>_<attr> prefixes. A row’s locator is its element’s path in the document (/root/item[2]: local names, a position among same-named siblings where there are several), followed by key:<key> where the element states a key of its own, its xml:id, else its id (/root/item[2] key:i2); a row read from a file names that file’s extraction (:attr:extractions), one read from a string or an element none.
Follows the standard two-phase pattern:

loader.load(*sources) – parse XML files.
loader.get_table(tag) – retrieve a normalised table.












Name
Type
Description
Default




principal_tags
list[str] | None
List of element tags to normalise. None for auto-detect.
None


sep
str
Separator for flattened nested key names. Default ".".
'.'


include_text
bool
Whether to include element text as _text field. Default True.
True


propagate_ancestors
bool
Whether to propagate ancestor attributes. Default True.
True


seed
int | None
The seed of the loader’s ID minter (see Loader.load).
None






Auto-detect all repeated tags::
loader = XmlLoader()
loader.load("data.xml")
for tag in loader.store.keys():
    print(tag, loader.get_table(tag).num_rows)
Specify principal tags::
loader = XmlLoader(principal_tags=["Signal", "Audio"])
loader.load("manifest.xml")
assert loader.get_table("Signal").num_rows > 0

loader.format.XmlLoader.load(*sources)
Load and accept one or more sources through the shared template.
Each source is a filesystem path (Path or str) or a member of a ZIP archive (zipfile.Path), which is read without extracting the archive. Its entry in metadata["sources"] records path (for a member: the archive’s absolute path, and member, the member’s path inside it) and loaded_at.
Every ID the loader mints (events, timelines, maps, MatchClaims, Projections) comes from its :class:~timetoalign.core.ids.IdMinter, in the order the loader builds them. Every load call seeds a new one: the first call after the loader is made or cleared from the loader’s seed when one was given, else from :func:~timetoalign.core.ids.seed_from of the loader’s class name, its configuration (the constructor arguments that shape the events) and the SHA-256 digests of the call’s sources, in order; every later call from seed_from of the previous call’s seed and its own sources’ digests, so later sources count too. A fresh loader loading unchanged sources in the same calls mints the same IDs, in any process; IDs the source states are kept as they are.

loader.format.XmlLoader.update(registry)
Re-read the loader’s sources and update registry with what they hold now.
The loader is cleared and its load calls are run again (those :meth:from_registry set up, or the loader’s own); each timeline :meth:create_timelines builds from them (and each descendant) then updates the registry’s timeline that holds the rows its locators name (else the one of its ID), one extraction at a time (:meth:EventRegistry.update <timetoalign.storage.EventRegistry.update>): a row found again by its locator keeps its ID and takes the new content, position and extraction; a new row is added with the ID it was given (minted from the content, as at every load); a row of the source no longer found is kept and marked vanished in the new extraction. Nothing is deleted. Rows that name no locator (a child’s place, events made in code) are left as they are.

Vectorized base class for loading tabular data with column/field specs.
TabularLoader provides a ZERO ROW ITERATION framework for loading CSV, TSV, and other delimited formats into EventData. All operations use vectorized numpy / pandas / pyarrow operations.


delimiter: Field delimiter character (default: ,). header_row: Row index containing column headers (default: 0). id_column: Source column name for event IDs, kept as stated; without one, IDs are minted from the loader’s minter. name_column: Source column name for event names (optional). start_column: Source column name for start coordinate (required). end_column: Source column name for end coordinate (None for instant events). duration_column: Source column name for duration (alternative to end_column). event_type_column: Source column name for event type (optional). default_event_type: Default event type if no column provides one. column_specs: Mapping or sequence describing the per-column translation from source to :class:DataField. title: Projection
text:
core.Projection()
An event standing on a timeline for an event not held there.
A Projection is an event type of its own (event_type "Projection" in a timeline’s events). It holds its own ID, its position on the timeline’s axis and, when the event it stands for is known, the reference to it; it repeats nothing else of that event (its pitch, its name, its other properties stay where the event lives). A Projection without projection_of stands for a position a source states without an event of its own.
start and duration are on one axis: the duration has the start’s unit and number type. An instant has no duration. A Projection made without an ID has id None until the timeline it is added to mints one (:meth:Timeline.add_events).
Storage struct (derived): {id, start, duration, projection_of}, the two positions as coordinate cells (:data:~timetoalign.core.time.COORDINATE_CELL_TYPE), each naming its unit and number type, both sides of the number filled. A package’s Projections table writes them otherwise: the timeline’s unit and number type once per row, each number once, as its number type says (:func:~timetoalign.timelines.manifest.projection_table).


>>> from timetoalign.core import Coordinate, TimeUnit
>>> Projection(
...     start=Coordinate(850176, TimeUnit.samples),
...     projection_of=EventReference(timeline_id="clt_6", event_id="x1azmn68"),
... ).end is None
True

Description

title: MeasureMapLoader
text:
loader.score.MeasureMapLoader(**kwargs)
Load MeasureMap JSON files into ScoreStore.
MeasureMapLoader parses the MeasureMap JSON format (as specified in the MeasureMap paper) and returns a ScoreStore with populated MeasureData.
The loader handles: - Compressed MeasureMap (minimal entries, defaults inferred) - Expanded MeasureMap (all fields explicit) - Validation of structure (MC unique, qstamp monotonic, next valid) - The standard’s anacrusis convention: a first row numbered 0 that is shorter than its nominal length is the closing part of nominal bar 0, at offset nominal_length - actual_length within it (see :meth:_apply_anacrusis_convention) - -1 in next, the measure-table spelling of the end of the piece: the rows are read without it (it names no row) and the measure map leaves it out, while expanded_data and the measure table keep it where the file states it
Known limitation: a .mm.json file states no offset for the parts of an inner split bar, so they load as IrregularMeasures, whereas an Ms3Loader measure table stating mc_offset yields MeasureConstituents for the same bar.










Name
Type
Description




unit
TimeUnit
Always TimeUnit.quarters (MeasureMap uses quarter beats).


expanded_data
list[dict[str, Any]]
The fully expanded measure list after loading.






>>> from timetoalign.testdata import ensure_data
>>> path = (
...     ensure_data("score")
...     / "couperin_concerts"
...     / "c05n05_musete.measures.mm.json"
... )
>>> loader = MeasureMapLoader().load(path)
>>> len(loader.store.measures)
58
The measure data also summarises the flow control it carries:
>>> summary = loader.store.measures.get_flow_control_summary()
>>> summary['repeat_starts'], summary['repeat_ends']
(2, 3)

title: Note
text:
core.Note()
A single note or rest event.
A note holds what every note has, whether a score writes it or a performance plays it. The staff and the voice a score writes a note on and in belong to :class:ScoreNote; a keyword this model does not declare is refused rather than dropped.
Note.pitch is annotated EnharmonicPitch | SpecificPitch | None for materialised scalars — both are legitimate pitch representations on a note. This union MUST NOT translate to Arrow dense_union; instead, the field is dropped from the pa.Schema and pitch is represented exactly once on the EventData. NoteEventData (a spelled score source) stores specific_pitch as the sole default semantic pitch field and keeps the source MIDI pitch as a non-default raw midi int that affords an EnharmonicPitch view on request. Number-only sources store the bare number instead (as a raw pitch int or an EnharmonicPitch {midi_number} struct). See Contributing → §2.4 Architectural decision log (union-of-BaseModels rejected; columnar separation).

The pitch is read from the column representing it (specific_pitch, else midi, else pitch). title: MelodyLoader
text:
loader.MelodyLoader(seed=None)
Read MeLODy’s Turtle and carry its triples as statements.
load(*sources) takes Turtle files and MeLODy data repositories: a directory is read as one, every *.ttl at any depth except under indexes/, configuration/ and datasets/. Each file is parsed into its own graph. :meth:create_bundle then writes one work, its manifestations and their items as statements on a bundle, as the module describes.


>>> import tempfile
>>> from pathlib import Path
>>> from timetoalign.loader.metadata.melody import MelodyLoader
>>> folder = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
>>> _ = (folder / "work.ttl").write_text(
...     "@prefix melod: <https://lod.academy/melod/vocab/ontology#> .\n"
...     "@prefix schema: <https://schema.org/> .\n"
...     "<urn:uuid:works/1> a melod:Work ; schema:creativeWorkStatus 'authentic' .\n",
...     encoding="utf-8",
... )
>>> bundle = MelodyLoader.from_file(folder / "work.ttl").create_bundle(
...     id="clair_de_lune", date="2026-11-19"
... )
>>> list(bundle.statements)
['schema:about']
>>> work = bundle.statements["schema:about"][0]
>>> work["id"], work["type"], work["schema:creativeWorkStatus"]
('urn:uuid:works/1', ['melod:Work'], ['authentic'])
>>> bundle.provenance[0]["basis"]
['work.ttl']






Name
Description




records
The sources read, each with its files and graphs, in loading order.









Name
Description




clear
Forget every source read.


create_bundle
State one work, its manifestations and their items on a bundle.





loader.MelodyLoader.clear()
Forget every source read.



loader.MelodyLoader.create_bundle(
    work=None,
    into=None,
    subjects=None,
    id=None,
    base='',
    stated_by=LIBRARY_AGENT,
    date=None,
)
State one work, its manifestations and their items on a bundle.
The bundle states schema:about the work, a value node carrying the work’s triples. Each expression of the work is a value node under lrmoo:R4_embodies of every manifestation embodying it, or under the work node’s lrmoo:R3_is_realised_in when none does. Each manifestation embodying an expression of the work is a new :class:~timetoalign.timelines.ContinuousGraphicalTimeline in millimetres, of unknown length, named by its rdfs:label or else by the label of its first title; the timelines join the bundle ungrouped before any statement is added. Each item exemplifying such a manifestation is a value node under the manifestation’s lrmoo:R7i_is_exemplified_by.
A subject (the manifestation’s timeline, a mapped element) states its type, its own IRI as owl:sameAs, then its other triples as they are: in the code-point order of the compact property, values sorted by their canonical JSON. An IRI naming an entity with an element is {"id": "#<element>"}; another IRI {"id": ...} with the label and owl:sameAs the graph states of it; a blank node a node of its own triples, an rdf:List {"list": [...]}. Each pair stated carries an entry holding no belief: method imported, basis the subject’s file (and the file of the entity whose node the value is, where it differs). A pair the subject already states or holds an entry of (a candidate, a pair someone believes) is skipped, so importing twice into one bundle adds nothing and every belief recorded stands. Every pair is checked before the bundle changes: a refused one leaves it as it was.

Type
Description
Default

str | None
The IRI of the melod:Work the bundle is about; the only work of the graph when None.
None


into

A bundle to import into instead of a new one; it is returned.
None


subjects
Mapping[str, str] | None
Maps the IRI of a manifestation or an item of the work to the ID of a timeline (at any depth) or region of into, which then receives that entity’s statements instead of a new timeline or value node.
None


id
str | None
The ID of a new bundle; minted (and never written) when None. Pass one so that the bundle has an IRI of its own.
None


base
str
Written before each file’s relative path in a basis.
''


stated_by
str | Sequence[str]
Who the entries name as having stated the pairs.
LIBRARY_AGENT

str | datetime.date | None
The day of the entries; today when None.
None

Type

title: GraphicalLoader
text:
loader.graphical.GraphicalLoader(metadata=None, *, seed=None)
Factory for building GraphicalStore objects.
The loader accumulates sources and segments, then builds a store. This provides a fluent interface for constructing graphical timelines.
Every addition is a door into the loader, like a load call: it seeds the loader’s ID minter afresh from the previous seed and what it adds (an image file’s bytes, an image’s pixels, a segment’s source, offset, name and geometry), so :meth:create_timeline mints an ID that follows the content (see Loader.load).


>>> loader = GraphicalLoader()
>>> idx = loader.add_image("score.png")
>>> loader.add_horizontal_segment(idx, x0=10, x1=500, y=100, name="system_1")
>>> loader.add_horizontal_segment(idx, x0=10, x1=500, y=200, name="system_2")
>>> store = loader.store
>>> # From PDF
>>> import pymupdf
>>> doc = pymupdf.open("score.pdf")
>>> loader = GraphicalLoader()
>>> idx = loader.add_pdf_page(doc, 0)
>>> loader.add_horizontal_segment(idx, x0=50, x1=550, y=100, name="page1")

loader.alignment.performance_precision.PerformancePrecisionLoader(
    score_unit=TimeUnit.quarters,
    media_unit=TimeUnit.seconds,
    seed=None,
)
Load a Performance Precision specimen directory as an AlignmentBundle.
The loader composes :class:SoloLoader internally for the .solo score and :meth:MetricMap.from_verovio_timemap for the measure structure, then resolves every "<measure>+<offset>" label — both the score notes and the per-performer alignment rows — into absolute quarter-note positions.
Usage follows the standard loader two-phase pattern:

loader.load(specimen_dir) — ingests the whole directory: the score and performance timelines with their notes, and every alignment row resolved to its two sides.
loader.create_bundle() — assembles the AlignmentBundle and states every row as a MatchClaim in it, adding the Projections the note and dangling rows’ claims stand on.
loader.create_timeline(uid) / create_timelines() — retrieve individual timelines (the score holding its Projections once create_bundle has stated the claims).

loader.alignment.performance_precision.PerformancePrecisionLoader.create_bundle(
)
Assemble an AlignmentBundle from the loaded specimen.
The timelines join the bundle first; then every row is stated as a MatchClaim between events (:meth:AlignmentBundle.create_match_claims <timetoalign.alignment.bundle.AlignmentBundle.create_match_claims>), one call per performer and granularity, in file order:

an aligned note-level row: a Projection on the score at its LABEL’s position stands for the performed Note event (projection_of naming it), and the claim joins the two;
an aligned bar- or beat-level row: both sides are positions where neither timeline holds an event, so the claim is CHUNK on both sides (:data:~timetoalign.core.ids.CHUNK), its anchor holding the two positions, and no Projection is added;
a dangling row: a NOMATCH claim from a score Projection standing for no event.

A timeline keeps one Projection per position and event it stands for, so the dangling positions every performer shares stand once on the score timeline, and a second call adds no Projection. Every Projection is added while its timeline is in the bundle, so its ID is minted unique among all Projections of the bundle and the bundle’s package can be written.

Return the stretches of the axis that flow control never divides.
The intervals between consecutive boundaries: 0, the length, the coordinates of Jumps, JumpTargets, Breaks and SectionBreaks, and the places of every destination other than by: 0. They are lettered in the order of the axis; a run of a flow is the atomic sections it covers.

title: BeatPolicy
text:
core.BeatPolicy()
How a bar is counted in beats: a grouping cycle over one division.
A time signature says two things at once — which note value is counted, and how those values group into beats. division is the counted value in quarters (Fraction(1, 2) for an eighth), and grouping says how many of them each successive beat spans. A compound 6/8 bar is grouping=(3, 3) over eighths; a simple 4/4 bar is grouping=(1, 1, 1, 1) over quarters; an uneven (3+2+3)/8 bar is grouping=(3, 2, 3) over eighths.
The beat lengths (:attr:rods) are derived from that pair, never stored: the source encoding is what a policy holds, and every rod, offset and index question is answered from it.

Type
Description

How many divisions each beat spans, in order.


division
Fraction | None
The counted note value, in quarters. Given either directly or through beat_size, which completes it.

Duration | None
The counted value as a typed duration in whole notes or quarters. Completed from division when omitted.

Optional tempo indication, in counted beats per minute.

core.BeatPolicy.from_time_signature(signature)
Derive the default counting of a bar from its time signature.
A signature "n/d" is read as compound when n is a multiple of three greater than three and the denominator is an eighth or shorter — 6/8, 9/8, 12/16 count in dotted beats of three divisions. Everything else counts one division per beat. A composite signature "a/d+b/d+c/d" spells its own grouping. "C" is 4/4 and "C|" (also spelled "cut") is 2/2.

title: resolve
text:
alignment.resolve(target, id)
Everything an ID names, through a manifest or a package root.
An ID combined with a manifest’s persistent location names an element, an event, a MatchClaim or an extraction of its package. target is a manifest file or a package root (the folder of package.yaml), as a path or a file: URL; id is bare, or written #id. The resolutions are TimeToShare’s (timetoshare.tables.resolve): through a manifest, its element of that ID first, then the registry rows of that ID that belong to it; through a package root, every registry row of that ID, an element ID repeated across manifests once per manifest. Each is answered as a library object:

a manifest element: the :class:AlignmentBundle for the manifest itself, the :class:~timetoalign.timelines.Timeline, the :class:~timetoalign.timelines.TimelineGroup, the :class:~timetoalign.timelines.manifest.Resource or the :class:~timetoalign.timelines.Region of the manifest read (its events read as :meth:from_file reads them); any other element as its object in the manifest, IDs bare;
a MatchClaim: the :class:~timetoalign.alignment.MatchClaim, read from its table by ID;
an event: its scalar (a :class:~timetoalign.core.Projection, a :class:~timetoalign.core.Box, else an :class:~timetoalign.core.Event), its position on the axis of its timeline’s root as the registry states it, its content read from its pre-parsed table by ID (none for an event only re-parsable);
an extraction: the :class:~timetoalign.storage.Extraction, its source as the library holds a source (the path of a file the package names relative to its root, or by a file: URI).

title: Quadrilateral
text:
Quadrilateral()
A four-cornered area of an image, its corners in the canonical order.
top_left, top_right, bottom_right, bottom_left: the cyclic order SVG polygon and IIIF SvgSelector draw a box in (:data:CORNER_ORDER). Its sides may be skewed (a measure of a scanned page). All eight numbers are on one axis.
The corners run clockwise (with y down) around a convex outline, starting at the top-left one: an outline whose sides cross is refused, so a polygon drawn from the corners is the area they bound. The top-left corner is the corner of least x + y; of two such corners, the one of least y (the upper). On an axis-aligned box it is the corner the name says; on a skewed one it is the corner nearest the image’s origin along the diagonal. A list that runs clockwise but starts at another corner is refused by the constructor, saying which corner it starts at; :meth:from_svg_points reads a list in either direction from any corner and turns it into this order.
For example, the diamond 0,5 5,10 10,5 5,0 (left, bottom, right, top: counter-clockwise with y down) has two corners of least x + y = 5, (0, 5) and (5, 0); the upper, (5, 0), is the top-left corner, so :meth:from_svg_points reverses the list and starts it there: 5,0 10,5 5,10 0,5.
Storage struct (derived): {top_left, top_right, bottom_right, bottom_left}, each {x, y} of number structs; the axis is the field’s (:class:QuadrilateralField).


>>> measure = Quadrilateral.from_points(
...     [(1221, 1589), (2151, 1589), (1221, 2266), (2161, 2266)],
...     order=("top_left", "top_right", "bottom_left", "bottom_right"),

title: flow_control_from_measures
text:
timelines.flow.flow_control_from_measures(measures, *, seed=None)
Return the flow control a measure map states.
Coordinates are the measures’ qstamp values: quarters, exact.

A row with start_repeat gives a :class:JumpTarget (repeat_start) at its start.
A row with end_repeat gives a destination (repeat_end, repeat_count: 1) of the Jump at its end, to the nearest repeat start before it that no earlier repeat end has closed, and without place where there is none: nothing is added that the rows do not state, a repeat start least of all.
Rows with volta are brackets of alternative endings; adjacent rows stating the same passes are one bracket, and adjacent brackets naming different passes are one run. A run gives ONE Jump at the start of its first bracket with a destination per bracket (volta, passes the row’s value): the first by: 0, every other to a :class:JumpTarget (volta) at that bracket’s first row, where a :class:Break (volta) lies as well.
The repeat ends closing the brackets of one run go back to one place, the one the first of them closes. One closing another bracket than the first is written reset: false: it must not start the Jump before the brackets again, whose passes it counts.

Signs falling on one coordinate are destinations of one Jump. No row key says where a bracket ends, so no element does.





Name
Type
Description
Default




measures
MeasureMap | Iterable[Any]
A :class:~timetoalign.timelines.MeasureMap, or full rows as :meth:MeasureMap.expand_rows <timetoalign.timelines.MeasureMap.expand_rows> returns them. In either, volta is a pass number or several of them.
required


seed
int | None
The seed of the minter of the elements’ IDs; None mints them from the content minter of the measures’ rows.
None









Name
Type
Description





list[FlowControlElement]
The elements by coordinate and then by ID, each with an ID of its



list[FlowControlElement]
own, its role the prefix, minted in the order written.














Name
Type
Description





ValueError
If a measure states no qstamp or no actual_length, or a volta that is neither a pass number nor a list of them.






>>> from timetoalign.timelines import MeasureMap
>>> bars = MeasureMap.from_rows(
...     [
...         {"count": 1, "time_signature": "4/4"},
...         {"count": 2, "start_repeat": True},
...         {"count": 3, "end_repeat": True},
...         {"count": 4},
...     ]
... )
>>> start, repeat = flow_control_from_measures(bars, seed=7)
>>> start
JumpTarget('jump_target_1hvif5xc2r1fv', repeat_start @ 4 quarters)
>>> repeat
Jump('jump_0g2wfq87pa7jx' @ 12 quarters, 1 destination)
>>> repeat.targets[0].to_dict()
{'to': 'jump_target_1hvif5xc2r1fv', 'repeat_count': 1, 'manifestation': 'repeat_end'}

title: BeatGrid
text:
timelines.BeatGrid(segments, *, extent=None)
A sequence of tempo segments and the beats they generate.
Segments are given as they are stated — typically without an end, each one generating beats forever. The grid puts them in time order and bounds each by the next one’s start; the last segment is bounded by extent, or generates without end when no extent is given.


>>> from fractions import Fraction
>>> grid = BeatGrid.from_tempo(120, extent=8)
>>> [str(beat.seconds) for beat in grid.iter_beats()][:5]
['0', '1/2', '1', '3/2', '2']
>>> grid.seconds_at(2)
Coordinate(2.0, seconds)
>>> grid.position_at(2.75).instant
Coordinate(2.5, seconds)
>>> grid.position_at(2.75).instant == grid.seconds_at(2, 2)
True

timelines.MeasureMap(measures, *, id=None, name=None, meta=None, seed=None)
An immutable sequence of measures in printed order.
A measure’s id is its Measure Map row ID: str(count) unless a source states another, and next names successors by these IDs. A map states every successor explicitly: a measure built without next is followed by the next measure in printed order, and the last one by none.
In a manifest a measure map is an entry of measure_maps: an id, an optional name and meta, and its compressed rows. A map built without an id mints one with the prefix measure_map when it is built, which every manifest it is written in names. Identity takes no part in equality, nor do the keys of each row that the row form does not define, which a map read from a manifest keeps by measure and writes back in that measure’s row: two maps are equal when their measures are.

CoordinateField(raw=None, unit=None, number_type=None, *, source_fields=None)
Semantic field for coordinate fields.
Wraps a StructField containing the coordinate struct {value: float64, numerator: int64, denominator: int64} and adds semantic identity: unit, domain, number_type.

>>> import pyarrow as pa
>>> from timetoalign.core.enums import TimeUnit, NumberType
>>> from timetoalign.core.time import CoordinateField
>>> arr = pa.array(
...     [{"value": 1.5, "numerator": 3, "denominator": 2}],
...     type=pa.struct([
...         pa.field("value", pa.float64()),
...         pa.field("numerator", pa.int64()),
...         pa.field("denominator", pa.int64()),
...     ]),
... )
>>> cf = CoordinateField.from_field(arr, unit=TimeUnit.seconds, number_type=NumberType.float)
>>> cf[0]
Coordinate(1.5, seconds)

Used for MIDI-based representations where time is measured in quantized ticks. Essential for MIDI file parsing and generation.
Default unit: ticks. Default number type: int. Allowed units: ticks only.

alignment.WarpMap.materialise(source_timeline, *, seed=None)
Produce a new Timeline with all contents warped to target coordinates.
Creates a complete copy of the source timeline where every coordinate (events, children, regions) is converted by calling this map. The resulting timeline:

Contains warped copies of all regions
Carries an inverse WarpMap as a ConversionMap for traceability

Every timeline and region of the copy holds an id of its own, so the copy may join a group or bundle holding its source. A region’s id is minted from the source region’s id and the id of the timeline holding the copy; events keep theirs.

title: IIIFManifestLoader
text:
loader.graphical.IIIFManifestLoader(seed=None)
Load image metadata from IIIF Presentation API manifests.
IIIF manifests contain canvas dimensions that represent image sizes. This loader extracts width/height for use with graphical timelines without needing to download or load the actual image files. A timeline runs along the time path the caller gives for a canvas: :meth:create_timelines answers one timeline per canvas, :meth:create_timeline the whole volume, its pages laid end to end.
Supports both IIIF Presentation API 2.x and 3.x formats. Time-based Presentation 3 canvases (duration without width/height) are read and expose their duration; they have no pixels, so no time path runs through them and the single-image accessors refuse a manifest whose first canvas is one.


>>> from timetoalign.testdata import ensure_data
>>> manifest = ensure_data("supra") / "image" / "ifff_manifest.json"
>>> loader = IIIFManifestLoader().load(manifest)
>>> loader.dimensions
{'width': 4096, 'height': 299400}
Individual canvases carry their own label and dimensions:
>>> for canvas in loader.manifest_info.canvases:
...     print(f"{canvas.label}: {canvas.width}x{canvas.height}")
display image: 4096x299400
A piano roll is read from top to bottom, so its time path is a vertical line down the middle of the image:
>>> from timetoalign.loader.graphical.paths import VerticalLinePath
>>> path = VerticalLinePath(x=2048, y0=0, y1=299400, tolerance=2048)
>>> (roll,) = loader.create_timelines(path)
>>> roll.length.value
299400

    accolade_ids=None,
)
Create the volume: the selected canvases laid end to end, in pixels.
Each selected canvas becomes one page along its time path, in manifest order, and the volume is the segment line of the pages, as long as all of them together. A page whose path is a :class:~timetoalign.loader.graphical.paths.PiecewisePath is itself a segment line of accolades, one per piece; any other path gives one plain timeline of the path’s length. See :meth:create_timelines for what a page and an accolade state.
The volume states the manifest it was read from as the property dcterms:source ({"id": <manifest id>}; a manifest without an id states nothing). This property is provisional: it may change.

Two pages of a printed score, each with two systems::
from timetoalign.loader.graphical.paths import (
    HorizontalLinePath, PiecewisePath,
)

def systems(*lines):
    return PiecewisePath(tuple(
        HorizontalLinePath(x0=x0, x1=x1, y=y, tolerance=300)
        for x0, x1, y in lines
    ))

loader = IIIFManifestLoader().load("manifest.json")
volume = loader.create_timeline(
    {
        1: systems((1221, 4101, 1900), (971, 4112, 3300)),
        2: systems((519, 3661, 900), (522, 3659, 2300)),
    },
    canvases=[1, 2],
    uid="scan",
)
for _, offset, page in volume.iter_segments():
    print(page.name, offset.value, page.length.value,
          page.statements["dcterms:source"])




loader.graphical.IIIFManifestLoader.create_timelines(
    paths,
    *,
    canvases=None,
    page_ids=None,
    accolade_ids=None,
)
Create one timeline in pixels per selected canvas, along its time path.
A canvas whose path is a :class:~timetoalign.loader.graphical.paths.PiecewisePath becomes a segment line of accolades, one per piece in path order: an accolade along a horizontal piece is as long as the piece (x1 - x0) and states the strip it stands for in meta["box"]. Any other path gives one plain timeline of the path’s length, which must be a whole number of pixels: a piano roll is read along a VerticalLinePath.
Each page is named with its canvas’s label and states the canvas it measures: its id in meta["image"] (the accolades too) and as the property dcterms:source ({"id": <canvas id>}; Presentation 2 @id, Presentation 3 id). A canvas without an id states nothing. This property is provisional: it may change.
A horizontal or vertical line must lie on its canvas: 0 <= x0, x1 <= width and 0 <= y <= height (for a vertical line 0 <= x <= width, 0 <= y0 and y1 <= height).

Two pages of a printed score, each with two systems::
from timetoalign.loader.graphical.paths import (
    HorizontalLinePath, PiecewisePath,
)

def systems(*lines):
    return PiecewisePath(tuple(
        HorizontalLinePath(x0=x0, x1=x1, y=y, tolerance=300)
        for x0, x1, y in lines
    ))

loader = IIIFManifestLoader().load("manifest.json")
volume = loader.create_timeline(
    {
        1: systems((1221, 4101, 1900), (971, 4112, 3300)),
        2: systems((519, 3661, 900), (522, 3659, 2300)),
    },
    canvases=[1, 2],
    uid="scan",
)
for _, offset, page in volume.iter_segments():
    print(page.name, offset.value, page.length.value,
          page.statements["dcterms:source"])

title: SoloLoader
text:
SoloLoader
loader.tabular.SoloLoader(unit=None, number_type=None, **kwargs)
Loader for .solo performance-precision specimen files.
The loader operates header-less on a tab-separated source and routes the canonical start coordinate through the synthesised measure_number + mn_onset pair produced by Step 1; the canonical duration column is also produced by Step 1 (as a :class:DenominateNumberField bound to TimeUnit.quarters).
The loader does NOT reconcile the measure-number label into a flat-quarter coordinate — measures are second-order time units and resolving them needs a measure map this loader does not have. The canonical start coordinate therefore carries the raw within-measure offset (mn_onset) and nothing else: it is a position inside its measure, not a position in the piece, and the quarters label on it names the axis the offset will land on once a measure map places the bar. Callers that need flat-quarter onsets must read measure_number and mn_onset together and resolve the pair against their measure map — which is what :class:~timetoalign.loader.alignment.performance_precision.PerformancePrecisionLoader does, converting the whole-note offset to quarters on the way.

title: measure_order_from_successors
text:
timelines.flow.measure_order_from_successors(successors, first)
Walk the successors a source states into the order of measures they give.
A measure table may list, for each measure count, the counts of the measures that can follow it, in the order of the times the measure is reached (the next of a Measure Map row or of an ms3 measures table). The walk begins at first; on its n-th arrival at a measure it goes on to that measure’s n-th successor, and to the last one once they are used up. It ends at a measure without successors and where the successor is no measure of successors (-1 is the customary spelling of the end of the piece).
Nothing is derived here: the order is what the source’s successors say, read as their format defines them.

    timeline,
    length,
    *,
    id=None,

    _unknown_keys=dict[str, Any](),
    through=None,

The statement that a map was applied to a timeline, giving a timeline.
A virtual timeline exists only by applying the map: it has an ID, a unit, a number type and a length of its own, and nothing else of it is written. It holds no events, no children and no flow control. Its positions and those of the timeline it comes from convert through the map, in both directions (:meth:unfold, :meth:fold). It may be a member of a group (:meth:as_member).

title: MatchGraph
text:
alignment.MatchGraph(
    claims=None,
    *,
    units=None,
    axis=None,
    source=None,
    source_id=None,
    believer=None,
    beliefs=DEFAULT_BELIEFS,
)
A graph of MatchClaims connecting events across timelines/groups.
The MatchGraph builds a networkx graph where: - Nodes: (timeline_id, coordinate) tuples - Edges: synchronous AlignmentAnchors, stated by a MatchClaim or inferred through a group (:class:InferredEdge)
Only synchronous claims produce graph edges. Non-synchronous claims (conceptual matches, NOMATCH) are stored in _claims but do not create nodes or edges. The graph’s MatchClaims are those it was given; what it infers is held apart, in :attr:inferred_edges.
Each Hendrix M-box (M1–M15) is a separate MatchGraph. The system is NOT a global graph; MatchGraphs are created on demand.





Name
Type
Description




claims
list[MatchClaim]
The MatchClaims of this graph (synchronous and non-synchronous).


inferred_edges
list[InferredEdge]
The edges the graph inferred through groups.






Build a graph from two claims between notes of a score and onsets of a recording:
>>> from timetoalign.timelines import Timeline, TimelineGroup
>>> def claim(quarters, seconds):
...     return MatchClaim(
...         timeline_a_id="score",
...         timeline_b_id="audio",
...         event_a_id=f"note_{quarters}",
...         event_b_id=f"onset_{quarters}",
...         start_anchor=AlignmentAnchor(
...             timeline_a_id="score",
...             coordinate_a=Coordinate(quarters, TimeUnit.quarters),
...             timeline_b_id="audio",
...             coordinate_b=Coordinate(seconds, TimeUnit.seconds),
...         ),
...         is_synchronous=True,
...     )
>>> graph = MatchGraph(claims=[claim(0, 0.0), claim(4, 2.0)])
>>> graph.n_nodes, graph.n_edges, graph.n_components
(4, 2, 2)
Extend it through the group the score shares with its parts:
>>> score = Timeline(length=8, unit=TimeUnit.quarters, uid="score")
>>> parts = Timeline(length=8, unit=TimeUnit.quarters, uid="parts")
>>> group = TimelineGroup(name="edition", timelines=[score, parts])
>>> extended = graph.extend_to_groups({group.id: group})
>>> extended.n_nodes, extended.n_edges, extended.n_claims
(6, 4, 2)
>>> extended.inferred_edges[0].group_id == group.id
True
>>> extended.inferred_edges[0].source_claim.event_a_id
'note_0'
One stamp per synchronized position:
>>> stamps = extended.get_stamps()
>>> print(stamps[1])
MatchStamp (3 timelines, 2 edges)
  audio   2 seconds  stated
  parts  4 quarters  inferred
  score  4 quarters  stated

alignment.MatchGraph.extend_to_groups(
    groups,
    *,
    include_inferred=True,
    within=None,
    id_pattern=None,
    include_domains=None,
    include_units=None,
)
Extend anchors to full group timestamps via inferred edges.
For each coordinate in the graph, computes the equivalent coordinate for every other member of every group its timeline belongs to and adds an edge between the two, recorded as an :class:InferredEdge (the anchor, the group, and the MatchClaim the coordinate traces back to) in the extended graph’s :attr:inferred_edges. The extended graph holds the same MatchClaims as this one: an inferred edge is the graph’s own, never a MatchClaim. Membership is read from groups alone, and a timeline may belong to several. A coordinate reached this way is extended in turn through the other groups of its timeline, so a timeline shared by two groups carries a coordinate from the members of one to the members of the other. Filters control which timelines receive inferred edges; a timeline they exclude receives no coordinate, so no extension passes through it.

alignment.MatchGraph.filter(
    timeline_id=None,
    timeline_ids=None,
    id_pattern=None,
    within=None,
    synchronous_only=False,
    nomatch_only=False,
    stated_only=False,
    include_domains=None,
    include_units=None,
    believer=None,
    beliefs=DEFAULT_BELIEFS,
)
Return the graph of the MatchClaims the filters keep.
The filters choose claims, with the meaning they have on every MatchClaim query (:meth:~timetoalign.alignment.AlignmentBundle.get_match_claims), decided by :meth:~timetoalign.alignment.filters.ClaimFilter.select. The result is the graph of the kept claims: a graph extended through groups (:meth:extend_to_groups) is extended again through the same groups, under the same filters, and reaches only the timelines within, include_domains and include_units admit. So it holds exactly what a graph built from the kept claims and extended the same way holds.
Domains and units are read from the source bundle’s timelines when the graph has a source, else from the units of the graph’s anchors and of the graph it was filtered from (a filtered graph keeps the units its own source graph knew, so filters compose in any order): without a source, a claim on a timeline no anchor names (a NOMATCH or conceptual claim, say) passes no domain or unit filter.
The groups are read as they stand when filtering: a member added to a group after the extension is reached by the filtered graph.

alignment.ClaimFilter(
    timeline_id=None,
    timeline_ids=None,
    id_pattern=None,
    between=None,
    within=None,
    synchronous_only=False,
    nomatch_only=False,
    include_domains=None,
    include_units=None,
    believer=None,
    beliefs=DEFAULT_BELIEFS,
)
Reusable filter for querying MatchClaims and related objects.
All fields are optional. When multiple fields are set, they are combined with AND logic: a claim must satisfy every non-None criterion.
The matches_claim() method tests a single MatchClaim against all criteria; select() is its list form, asking the belief filter once for the whole list. The matches_timeline() method tests a single timeline ID (used to narrow the timelines of a stamp).


Filter for claims involving a specific performer::
f = ClaimFilter(id_pattern=r"^perf:")
filtered = [c for c in claims if f.matches_claim(c)]
Filter for synchronous claims between score and one performer::
f = ClaimFilter(
    between=("score:clt_1", "perf:dlt_1"),
    synchronous_only=True,
)

title: MatchClaimField
text:
alignment.MatchClaimField(
    raw=None,
    *,
    source_fields=None,
    name=None,
    provenance=None,
)
The MatchClaim table: a SemanticField[MatchClaim] columnar store.
MatchClaimField is the Field paired with the :class:MatchClaim scalar. It holds a large set of MatchClaims (millions of rows) as Arrow columns instead of one frozen :class:MatchClaim per claim; individual claims are materialised lazily, only when a row is indexed or iterated. Every kind of MatchClaim is a row like any other: synchronous claims with their anchors, NOMATCH and conceptual claims without. The event ID columns are never null: a side without an event holds its sentinel, :data:NOMATCH or :data:CHUNK; a NOMATCH side’s name is null, a CHUNK side’s names the stated position where one is given.
Like every paired Field, its struct schema is derived from the scalar by :func:~timetoalign.core.fields.derive_arrow_struct — so a row’s type is exactly MatchClaimField.pa_schema. Its :attr:table (and the Parquet file :meth:to_parquet writes, match_claims.parquet) has one column per top-level property of :class:MatchClaim, each nested as the property is. A provenance shared by every row is held once at field level (or None) and injected on read: the provenance column is left null, and :meth:__getitem__ gives each materialised claim the field’s provenance. Claims whose provenance differs, given to :meth:from_claims, carry it per row.
A MatchClaim is addressed by its id alone: an id held twice is refused, and an id never changes. A field never holds a row without an id: every constructor mints the missing ones (claim_…), from IdMinter(seed) when given seed=, from the minter given as minter= (a loader’s), else from the content minter of the rows (every column but id). Joining a :class:~timetoalign.alignment.bundle.AlignmentBundle mints nothing.

Type
Description

pa.Table

alignment.MatchClaimField.at(timeline_id, coordinate)
Return claims relevant at (timeline_id, coordinate).
The selection is a vectorized PyArrow boolean mask over the struct column. Instant rows compare their start coordinate exactly. Interval rows use closed containment between their start and end coordinates. Rows without anchors (NOMATCH, conceptual) are never relevant. No claim is materialised and the rest of the field is never touched; the shared provenance carries over.
Coordinate matching is exact in the query coordinate’s declared number representation. There is no tolerance or nearest-value fallback.

Return a filtered view following the unified filter API.
Every criterion is a vectorized boolean mask over the claim columns; no claim is materialised and the shared provenance carries over. All non-default criteria are combined with logical AND.

title: MeiFacsimileLoader
text:
loader.graphical.MeiFacsimileLoader(seed=None)
Load the surfaces and zones of an MEI file’s facsimile.
Each surface holding zones becomes a page: a segment line of its accolades, in pixels (int). An accolade is one horizontal piece of the page’s time path, a :class:DiscreteGraphicalTimeline as long as the piece, stating the area it stands for in meta["box"] and its image in meta["image"]. Each zone taking part is a :class:~timetoalign.core.Box event of the accolade it lies on, holding the zone’s shape in the image’s pixels. :attr:facs keeps which zones each element of the encoding points to.
For a Box on an accolade, start is the zone’s least x minus the x of the accolade’s meta["box"] and duration is the zone’s x extent, so the box, the shape and the interval agree.
:meth:create_timeline gives the whole facsimile as one volume (a segment line of the pages), :meth:create_timelines one root per page, :meth:create_paths the time paths made from the zones.
Known limits: only the first graphic of a surface is read, and zone coordinates are taken as its pixels (the surface’s own @ulx .. @lry are not read, so a surface whose corners measure another space than the graphic’s pixels has its zones placed as if they were the graphic’s pixels); a graphic size in a unit other than pixels (cm, in, …) states no pixel size and is not read; MEI states no accolades, so they are found from the zones’ left edges unless paths are given, and a page whose zones are not listed accolade by accolade needs a path; a zone without xml:id is minted box_… from the loader’s minter and cannot be pointed to; an element without xml:id is left out of :attr:facs, and a zone stating no coordinates out of the timelines (:attr:zones_without_coordinates lists those with an id). A zone whose @points are not four points bounding a convex area (five points, a concave or crossed outline) cannot be a :class:~timetoalign.core.Quadrilateral and refuses the file, the message naming the zone and the reason. The volume takes no name from the file’s title.


The pages of an MEI file as timelines, the measures of the first accolade, and the zones a measure points to::
loader = MeiFacsimileLoader.from_file("chorale_facsimile.mei")
(page,) = loader.create_timelines(zone_types="measure")
accolade = page.get_child(page.list_children()[0])
boxes = accolade.get_events().table.to_pylist()
zones = loader.facs["m-43"]

    paths=None,
    zone_types=None,
    page_ids=None,
    accolade_ids=None,
    box_ids=None,
)
Create one root timeline per surface, in document order.
A surface’s page is a locked segment line of its accolades, in pixels (int): its id the surface’s xml:id (minted dgt_… where it has none), its name the surface’s @n (page_N by its position in the call, from 1, where it has none), its length the sum of its accolades’, meta["image"] the graphic’s @target. It states no meta["box"]: its axis is a concatenation of accolades, not an area, and the graphic’s size is on no timeline.
The accolades are the pieces of the surface’s time path, made from the zones taking part (:meth:create_paths) unless paths gives one. Each is a :class:DiscreteGraphicalTimeline named accolade_K (K from 1 on its page) whose length is its piece’s x1 - x0, with meta["box"] the piece’s strip (x0, y - tolerance, x1 - x0, 2 * tolerance) and meta["image"].
Each zone taking part is a Box event of its accolade: the one it was grouped into or, on a given path, the piece it lies on (the piece whose x extent holds the zone’s and whose strip holds the zone’s vertical centre; of several the nearest). Its id is the zone’s xml:id (minted box_… where it has none); its shape is the zone’s coordinates as written; its start is the shape’s least x less the accolade’s x0.
A surface without a zone taking part and without a given path is left out.

title: FlowControlDraft
text:
timelines.flow.FlowControlDraft(minter=None)
Flow control being written from a score, before it joins a registry.
The signs at one coordinate are collected as the destinations of the one Jump there, and every element gets an ID of its own, minted in the order written by the draft’s minter (a loader’s; without one, the content minter of "flow_control"), so that the elements can name one another before a registry admits them together. Coordinates are quarters, exact. :func:flow_control_from_measures and the score loaders write through it.


>>> from fractions import Fraction
>>> from timetoalign.timelines.flowcontrol import JumpDestination, JumpTarget
>>> draft = FlowControlDraft(IdMinter(7))
>>> segno = draft.add(JumpTarget, Fraction(4), manifestation="segno")
>>> draft.add_destination(Fraction(16), JumpDestination(to=segno.id, repeat_count=1))
'jump_0g2wfq87pa7jx'
>>> draft.add_destination(Fraction(16), JumpDestination(repeat_count=1))
'jump_0g2wfq87pa7jx'
>>> draft.elements()
[JumpTarget('jump_target_1hvif5xc2r1fv', segno @ 4 quarters), Jump('jump_0g2wfq87pa7jx' @ 16 quarters, 2 destinations)]

A loader set up from registry’s extractions, to refresh it with :meth:update.
The loader runs with the parameters (and the seed) the registry’s extractions of this loader’s class recorded, and reads their source files, unless sources names what to read (a loader reading a folder, an archive or a project is given that). Nothing is read until :meth:update.

required

()

**kwargs
Any

{}














Name
Type
Description





Self

Name
Type
Description





ValueError
If the extractions of this class record two sets of parameters or seeds, the loader set up runs with other parameters than they record, or neither sources nor an extraction names a source file.







loader.Loader.load(*sources)
Load and accept one or more sources through the shared template.
Each source is a filesystem path (Path or str) or a member of a ZIP archive (zipfile.Path), which is read without extracting the archive. Its entry in metadata["sources"] records path (for a member: the archive’s absolute path, and member, the member’s path inside it) and loaded_at.
Every ID the loader mints (events, timelines, maps, MatchClaims, Projections) comes from its :class:~timetoalign.core.ids.IdMinter, in the order the loader builds them. Every load call seeds a new one: the first call after the loader is made or cleared from the loader’s seed when one was given, else from :func:~timetoalign.core.ids.seed_from of the loader’s class name, its configuration (the constructor arguments that shape the events) and the SHA-256 digests of the call’s sources, in order; every later call from seed_from of the previous call’s seed and its own sources’ digests, so later sources count too. A fresh loader loading unchanged sources in the same calls mints the same IDs, in any process; IDs the source states are kept as they are.










Name
Type
Description





FileNotFoundError
If a zipfile.Path names a member its archive does not hold.



ValueError
If the loader reads one source and is given none or more than one, or any while it holds one (after clear() it reads one again). Nothing is parsed then.







loader.Loader.update(registry)
Re-read the loader’s sources and update registry with what they hold now.
The loader is cleared and its load calls are run again (those :meth:from_registry set up, or the loader’s own); each timeline :meth:create_timelines builds from them (and each descendant) then updates the registry’s timeline that holds the rows its locators name (else the one of its ID), one extraction at a time (:meth:EventRegistry.update <timetoalign.storage.EventRegistry.update>): a row found again by its locator keeps its ID and takes the new content, position and extraction; a new row is added with the ID it was given (minted from the content, as at every load); a row of the source no longer found is kept and marked vanished in the new extraction. Nothing is deleted. Rows that name no locator (a child’s place, events made in code) are left as they are.











Name
Type
Description
Default




registry
EventRegistry
The registry to update: a timeline’s, a group’s or a bundle’s (:attr:Timeline.registry <timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.registry>).
required














Name
Type
Description





list[str]
The IDs of the registry’s timelines updated, in order.














Name
Type
Description





RuntimeError
If the loader has no load call to run again (it read nothing, or in-memory content only).



ValueError
If a timeline built holds rows that match no timeline of registry, by locator or by ID; nothing is updated then.

    unit=None,

    interval_policy=IntervalPolicy.warn,
    *,
    seed=None,
)
Abstract base class for event-producing loaders.
Loader provides a unified interface for loading one or more source files and aggregating their events into an EventData. Metadata about the sources is stored in the PyArrow table’s schema metadata for determinism.
Subclasses must implement: - _load_source(): Parse a single source file into event rows - _default_unit: The default time unit for this loader type

Type
Description

EventData
The EventData containing all loaded events.


sources
list[Source]
List of loaded source file paths.

TimeUnit

>>> # Subclass implementation
>>> class MidiLoader(Loader):
...     _default_unit = TimeUnit.ticks
...     _event_data_class = EventData
...
...     def _load_source(self, path):
...         # Parse MIDI file, return (metadata_dict, event_rows)
...         return {"format": "midi"}, [{"id": "n1", ...}]
>>>
>>> loader = MidiLoader()
>>> loader.load("piece.mid")
>>> print(loader.event_summary())

Bidirectional coordinate mapping using numpy.interp.
Provides O(log n) coordinate conversion without table lookup. Used for: - Timeline <-> Group relationships - WarpMap alignment warping
The map is bidirectional: calling the map converts source -> target, and inverse() returns a new map that converts target -> source.

Timeline/C-Map ID for source.

Timeline/C-Map ID for target.






>>> # Simple offset relationship: child at offset 10 in parent
>>> imap = InterpolationMap(
...     source_coords=np.array([0.0, 100.0]),  # child coords
...     target_coords=np.array([10.0, 110.0]),  # parent coords
...     source_id="child:1",
...     target_id="parent:1",
... )
>>> imap(50.0)  # child 50 -> parent 60
60.0
>>> imap.inverse()(60.0)  # parent 60 -> child 50

>>> # Tempo map: ticks to seconds
>>> imap = InterpolationMap(
...     source_coords=np.array([0.0, 480.0, 960.0]),
...     target_coords=np.array([0.0, 0.5, 1.5]),
...     source_id="ticks",
...     target_id="seconds",
... )
>>> imap(240.0)  # 240 ticks -> 0.25 seconds
0.25

title: FlowControlRegistry
text:
timelines.FlowControlRegistry(elements=(), *, unit=None, number_type=None)
The flow control of one timeline: its elements in canonical order.
One collection holds every :class:FlowControlElement, ordered by coordinate and then by ID; jumps, jump_targets, breaks, section_breaks and barlines are views of it by class. All of them are tuples: the collection changes through :meth:add, :meth:add_all, :meth:with_belief and :meth:with_beliefs alone, and no element ever leaves it. Every element carries an ID unique within the registry and, once the registry belongs to a timeline, within that timeline’s whole manifest: an element whose ID, given or minted, is taken is refused. A manifest writes the registry as the timeline’s flow_control array.
The registry refuses what cannot be played: a second Jump at a coordinate, or, once the registry belongs to a timeline, at a position of the root’s axis that a Jump of the root’s tree holds (the coordinate plus the offsets of the timeline and its ancestors, summed exactly), a to naming neither a :class:JumpTarget of the registry nor a place of its timeline, an after that does not name exactly one destination of another Jump of the registry, and an element or a destination’s place lying outside the axis, which runs from 0 to the timeline’s length (from 0 on while that length is unknown, and for a registry that belongs to no timeline).
An element that some actor believes "false" is rejected (:attr:FlowControlElement.is_rejected, :meth:with_belief): it stays in the registry and is written, but it is out of every rule, as what is checked and as what is named. A rejected Jump and its replacement may therefore share a coordinate. An element that another element not rejected names (by to or after) is not rejected alone: the elements naming it are rejected in the same step (:meth:with_beliefs).





Name
Type
Description
Default

The elements the registry starts with, added together.
()

The unit of the axis the registry is bound to, if any.
None

The number type of that axis, if any.
None

>>> registry = FlowControlRegistry(unit=TimeUnit.quarters)
>>> registry.add(JumpTarget(Coordinate(16, "quarters"), id="segno"))
JumpTarget('segno' @ 16 quarters)
>>> registry.add(
...     Jump(
...         Coordinate(64, "quarters"),
...         [JumpDestination(to="segno", repeat_count=1, reset=False)],
...         id="ds",
...     )
... ).id
'ds'
>>> [element.role for element in registry.elements]
['jump_target', 'jump']
>>> registry.place_of(registry.jumps[0].targets[0], registry.jumps[0])
Coordinate(Fraction(16, 1), quarters)

title: measure_keys_from_flow_control

timelines.flow.measure_keys_from_flow_control(elements, measures)
Return the row keys that flow control states, one object per measure.
The reverse of :func:flow_control_from_measures for the three keys it covers, read from what the elements look like (their manifestations):

start_repeat: a :class:JumpTarget (repeat_start) lies at the measure’s start;
end_repeat: the Jump at the measure’s end has a repeat_end destination;
volta: the measure lies under a bracket, whose passes are the value (one pass as an integer, several as a list). A bracket begins where a volta destination goes on (by: 0 at its Jump, to at its jump target) and ends where the next bracket of that Jump begins.

Where the last bracket of a run ends is no fact of flow control. It stays with the rows: the last bracket is given its first measure, and the measures following it for as long as measures state these very passes as their volta.
An element lying inside a measure, a bracket stating its passes as {from: n} and a to naming no jump target among elements state no row key.

title: OutputNumberTypeError
text:
OutputNumberTypeError
maps.OutputNumberTypeError()
A float handed to a map declared to write fractions.
Such a map computes exactly, so it takes ints and Fractions only: a float result rebuilt as an exact value would state a ratio the input never stated. The input is refused as a value, like any other position a map cannot answer for.

title: MpmLoader
text:
loader.alignment.mpm.MpmLoader(seed=None)
Load an MPM-Toolbox MSM+MPM+MPR triple as one multimodal AlignmentBundle.
The loader is given the .mpr project file; it resolves the sibling .msm / .mpm by the bare filenames the project names, parses the score, the selected modelled performance’s markup, and the observed alignment, and assembles a bundle with a shared logical "score" group and a physical "perf" group — the latter also carrying the spectrogram’s graphical pixel axis (perf:dgt_…) when the project ships one — linked by one synchronous :class:MatchClaim per score note. The bundle thus spans the logical, physical, and (when a spectrogram is present) graphical domains.
Usage follows the standard loader two-phase pattern:

loader.load(mpr_path) — ingest the whole project.
loader.create_bundle() — assemble the AlignmentBundle.
loader.create_timeline(uid) / create_timelines() — retrieve individual timelines.

By default the first <performance> in the .mpm is used. Pass performance=<name> to load to select a different one.
The loader reads the modelled performance and the observed alignment; it never runs an aligner.

title: Shape
text:
Shape()
An area of an image, on one axis: a :class:BoundingBox or a :class:Quadrilateral.
The shape is in image space (origin the top-left corner, x right, y down), every member in one unit and one number type. Everything a shape answers is derived here from :attr:corners, its four corners in the canonical order top_left, top_right, bottom_right, bottom_left (the order SVG and IIIF selectors draw a polygon in).
Every number enters a shape as given, finite and never rounded: NaN and the infinities are refused on every axis; on an int axis a float is taken only when it is a whole number (100.0 is 100) and a ratio only when its denominator is 1, on a fraction axis a float only when it is a whole number, on a float axis a ratio only when it is a whole number; anything else is refused, naming the value and the axis. A constructor’s refusal is a ValueError holding its message alone.
A shape is written as a format writes it (:meth:as_media_fragment, :meth:as_svg_points, :meth:as_mei_zone) and read back from it; a value a format cannot write is refused, never rounded.

title: Region
text:
timelines.Region(
    start,
    end,
    name=None,
    meta=dict(),
    *,
    id=None,
    seed=None,
    _unknown_keys=dict[str, Any](),
    _statement_state=dict(),
    _prefixes=dict(),
)
An identified part of a timeline defined by a TimeInterval.
IMPORTANT: Regions are NOT timelines. They cannot hold events or C-maps. Use Timeline.create_child_from_region(region_id) to create a Child timeline from a Region.
A region is frozen: :meth:with_statement and its siblings return a copy holding other statements (see :mod:~timetoalign.timelines.statements), and a timeline stores a changed copy in the region’s place with :meth:Timeline.replace_region <timetoalign.timelines.Timeline.replace_region>.










Name
Type
Description




start
Coordinate
Start coordinate of the region.


end
Coordinate
End coordinate of the region.


name
str | None
Optional display name (e.g., “Chorus”); names may repeat.


meta
dict[str, Any]
Additional metadata (e.g., traversal order labels).


id
str
The region’s id. When not given, one with the prefix region is minted when the region is built: from IdMinter(seed) with seed=, else from the content minter of its complete form without the id.






>>> from timetoalign import Coordinate, TimeUnit
>>> start = Coordinate(16.0, TimeUnit.quarters)
>>> end = Coordinate(32.0, TimeUnit.quarters)
>>> region = Region(start, end, name="Chorus", seed=7)
>>> region.id
'region_1hvif5xc2r1fv'
>>> region.duration
Duration(Fraction(16, 1), quarters)
>>> region.as_interval
Interval(start=Coordinate(Fraction(16, 1), quarters), end=Coordinate(Fraction(32, 1), quarters))
A region marks part of a timeline; turning it into a Child timeline goes through the timeline that owns it:
>>> from timetoalign import ContinuousLogicalTimeline
>>> tl = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=64)
>>> tl.create_region(16, 32, id="chorus", name="Chorus")
Region('chorus', name='Chorus', 16-32 quarters)
>>> chorus_child = tl.create_child_from_region("chorus")
>>> chorus_child.length
Coordinate(Fraction(16, 1), quarters)
