The bundle read back writes the same manifest, and so does a manifest file.

bundle.to_file(FOLDER / "layerit.yaml")
(
    tta.AlignmentBundle.from_dict(manifest).to_dict() == manifest,
    tta.AlignmentBundle.from_file(FOLDER / "layerit.yaml").to_dict() == manifest,
)

(True, True)


A timeline written on its own writes a manifest of its own. The WAV file’s source names the video, which that manifest does not hold, so the pair is left out together with its entry; the bundle’s own statements stay behind, and the @context holds the format’s terms alone.

show_manifest(bundle.get_timeline("dpt_1").to_dict())

"@context": {}
timelines:
  -
    id: "#dpt_1"
    length: 1470868
    name: ClairDeLune_MariaJoaoPires_untilM6.wav
    unit: samples
timetoshare: "0.2.0"





An MEI file’s meiHead describes the work it encodes, the work’s expressions, the manifestations embodying them and the items exemplifying those. MeiHeadLoader states that description in LRMoo’s and MeLODy’s vocabulary. The header below is a short one modelled on the Carl Nielsen Edition’s header of the song Hr. Olufs Sang, CNW 133; the autograph’s address is invented.

HEADER = """<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<mei xmlns="http://www.music-encoding.org/ns/mei" meiversion="5.1">
 <meiHead>
  <fileDesc><titleStmt><title>Hr. Olufs Sang</title></titleStmt><pubStmt/></fileDesc>
  <workList>
   <work xml:id="work_1">
    <identifier xml:id="identifier_1" label="CNW">133</identifier>
    <title xml:id="title_1" type="main" xml:lang="da">Hr. Olufs Sang</title>
    <composer><persName xml:id="persName_1" role="composer">Carl Nielsen</persName></composer>
    <lyricist><persName xml:id="persName_2"
      auth.uri="https://d-nb.info/gnd/" codedval="119018934">Holger Drachmann</persName></lyricist>
    <expressionList>
     <expression xml:id="expression_1">
      <title xml:id="title_3">Version for voice and piano</title>
      <key xml:id="key_1" pname="f" accid="s" mode="minor"/>
     </expression>
    </expressionList>
   </work>
  </workList>
  <manifestationList>
   <manifestation xml:id="source_1">
    <titleStmt><title xml:id="title_4">Score, print</title></titleStmt>
    <relationList>
     <relation xml:id="relation_2" rel="isEmbodimentOf" target="#expression_1"/>
    </relationList>
   </manifestation>
   <manifestation xml:id="source_2" sameas="https://example.org/sources/autograph">
    <titleStmt><title xml:id="title_5" type="main">Score, autograph</title></titleStmt>
    <itemList>
     <item xml:id="item_1">
      <identifier xml:id="identifier_4" label="RISM">DK-Kk CNS 342e</identifier>
     </item>
    </itemList>
   </manifestation>
  </manifestationList>
 </meiHead>
</mei>
"""
(FOLDER / "cnw0133.mei").write_text(HEADER, encoding="utf-8")
song = MeiHeadLoader.from_file(FOLDER / "cnw0133.mei").create_bundle(date="2026-11-19")
song.name, [(tl_id, song.get_timeline(tl_id).name) for tl_id in song.timeline_ids]

('cnw0133',
 [('cgt_361ckq06sqrc3', 'Score, print'),
  ('cgt_1vpnau7ca8hbu', 'Score, autograph')])


The bundle takes the file’s stem as its name; its ID is minted, as are the timelines’ IDs (cgt_…), seeded from the file, so the same file gives the same IDs on every run. Each manifestation becomes a graphical timeline in millimetres of unknown length, named by its title, the axis along which pages of the print or the autograph can be laid out. The work lands as a value node under the bundle’s schema:about, its IRI the file’s address followed by # and the work’s xml:id, and the bundle points to the MEI file with rdfs:seeAlso.

show(song)

rdfs:seeAlso: {"id": "cnw0133.mei"}
schema:about: {"id": "cnw0133.mei#work_1", "type": ["melod:Work"], "melod:hasTitle": [{"type": ["melod:Title"], "rdfs:label": [{"@value": "Hr. Olufs Sang", "@language": "da"}], "melod:hasTitleType": [{"id": "melodTerms:MainTitle"}]}], "melod:hasIdentifier": [{"type": ["melod:Identifier"], "rdfs:label": ["CNW"], "owl:hasValue": ["133"]}], "rel:lyr": [{"id": "gnd:119018934", "label": "Holger Drachmann"}], "lrmoo:R3_is_realised_in": [{"id": "cnw0133.mei#expression_1"}]}
[stated] schema:about: {"id": "cnw0133.mei#work_1"}
    {"stated_by": ["https://timetoalign.github.io/"], "date": "2026-11-19", "method": "imported", "basis": ["cnw0133.mei#work_1"]}
[stated] rdfs:seeAlso: {"id": "cnw0133.mei"}
    {"stated_by": ["https://timetoalign.github.io/"], "date": "2026-11-19", "method": "imported", "basis": ["cnw0133.mei"]}


Every pair carries an entry: method imported, the agent timetoalign.timelines.LIBRARY_AGENT (the library’s address) unless stated_by= names another, and as its basis the MEI element it comes from. What the header encodes with an IRI is stated: the lyricist, whom the header names by a GND number. A name without an IRI is a candidate, for reconciliation: the composer.

WORK = ("schema:about", 0)
show(song, node=WORK)

lrmoo:R3_is_realised_in: {"id": "cnw0133.mei#expression_1"}
melod:hasIdentifier: {"type": ["melod:Identifier"], "rdfs:label": ["CNW"], "owl:hasValue": ["133"]}
melod:hasTitle: {"type": ["melod:Title"], "rdfs:label": [{"@value": "Hr. Olufs Sang", "@language": "da"}], "melod:hasTitleType": [{"id": "melodTerms:MainTitle"}]}
rel:lyr: {"id": "gnd:119018934", "label": "Holger Drachmann"}
type: "melod:Work"
[stated] rdf:type: {"id": "melod:Work"}
    {"stated_by": ["https://timetoalign.github.io/"], "date": "2026-11-19", "method": "imported", "basis": ["cnw0133.mei#work_1"]}
[stated] melod:hasTitle: {"type": ["melod:Title"], "rdfs:label": [{"@value": "Hr. Olufs Sang", "@language": "da"}], "melod:hasTitleType": [{"id": "melodTerms:MainTitle"}]}
    {"stated_by": ["https://timetoalign.github.io/"], "date": "2026-11-19", "method": "imported", "basis": ["cnw0133.mei#title_1"]}
[stated] melod:hasIdentifier: {"type": ["melod:Identifier"], "rdfs:label": ["CNW"], "owl:hasValue": ["133"]}
    {"stated_by": ["https://timetoalign.github.io/"], "date": "2026-11-19", "method": "imported", "basis": ["cnw0133.mei#identifier_1"]}
[candidate] rel:cmp: {"label": "Carl Nielsen"}
    {"stated_by": ["https://timetoalign.github.io/"], "date": "2026-11-19", "method": "imported", "note": "unreconciled", "basis": ["cnw0133.mei#persName_1"]}
[stated] rel:lyr: {"id": "gnd:119018934"}
    {"stated_by": ["https://timetoalign.github.io/"], "date": "2026-11-19", "method": "imported", "basis": ["cnw0133.mei#persName_2"]}
[stated] lrmoo:R3_is_realised_in: {"id": "cnw0133.mei#expression_1"}
    {"stated_by": ["https://timetoalign.github.io/"], "date": "2026-11-19", "method": "imported", "basis": ["cnw0133.mei#expression_1"]}


The expression is a value node too, under lrmoo:R4_embodies of the manifestation that embodies it, the print; the autograph holds its item.

print_timeline = next(
    song.get_timeline(tl_id)
    for tl_id in song.timeline_ids
    if song.get_timeline(tl_id).name == "Score, print"
)
show(print_timeline)

lrmoo:R4_embodies: {"id": "cnw0133.mei#expression_1", "type": ["melod:Expression"], "rdfs:label": ["Version for voice and piano"], "mus:U11_has_key": [{"type": ["melod:Key"], "melod:hasPitch": [{"id": "melodTerms:F"}], "melod:hasAccidental": [{"id": "melodTerms:Sharp"}], "melod:isInMode": [{"id": "melodTerms:Minor"}]}]}
melod:hasTitle: {"type": ["melod:Title"], "rdfs:label": ["Score, print"]}
type: "melod:Manifestation"
[stated] rdf:type: {"id": "melod:Manifestation"}
    {"stated_by": ["https://timetoalign.github.io/"], "date": "2026-11-19", "method": "imported", "basis": ["cnw0133.mei#source_1"]}
[stated] melod:hasTitle: {"type": ["melod:Title"], "rdfs:label": ["Score, print"]}
    {"stated_by": ["https://timetoalign.github.io/"], "date": "2026-11-19", "method": "imported", "basis": ["cnw0133.mei#title_4"]}
[stated] lrmoo:R4_embodies: {"id": "cnw0133.mei#expression_1"}
    {"stated_by": ["https://timetoalign.github.io/"], "date": "2026-11-19", "method": "imported", "basis": ["cnw0133.mei#relation_2"]}


An imported candidate is stated as any other. Here the editor states the composer’s name as the header writes it; a lookup service could instead offer the person’s IRI, as the GND entry was offered above.

song.add_statement(
    "rel:cmp", {"label": "Carl Nielsen"}, actor=EDITOR, date="2026-11-19", node=WORK
)
song.get_candidates(node=WORK), song.statements["schema:about"][0]["rel:cmp"]

([], [{'label': 'Carl Nielsen'}])


create_bundle(into=…) states the description on an existing bundle, and subjects= maps the xml:id of a manifestation or an item to one of its timelines or regions. Importing again adds nothing: a pair already stated or held as a candidate is passed over, so a decision stays. base= gives the MEI file’s published address, from which every IRI and basis built from an xml:id then begins.



A MeLODy data repository keeps one Turtle file per entity: a work, an expression, a manifestation, an item, a person. Its statements are pairs already, so MelodyLoader carries them as they are, in LRMoo, MeLODy’s own terms and schema.org. The repository below is written for this guide in the shape of MeLODy’s template.

PREFIXES = """\
@prefix melod: <https://lod.academy/melod/vocab/ontology#> .
@prefix melodTerms: <https://lod.academy/melod/vocab/terms#> .
@prefix lrmoo: <http://iflastandards.info/ns/lrm/lrmoo/> .
@prefix owl: <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#> .
@prefix rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .
@prefix schema: <https://schema.org/> .
"""
REPOSITORY = {
    "works/1.ttl": """\
<urn:uuid:works/1> a melod:Work ;
  melod:hasTitle [ a melod:Title ; rdfs:label "Clair de lune"@fr ] ;
  owl:sameAs <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q29117946> ;
  lrmoo:R3_is_realised_in <urn:uuid:expressions/2> .
""",
    "expressions/2.ttl": """\
<urn:uuid:expressions/2> a melod:Expression ;
  rdfs:label "Clair de lune, piano" ;
  melod:hasContribution [ a melod:Contribution ; melod:hasAgent <urn:uuid:persons/3> ;
    melod:hasRole melodTerms:Composer ] .
""",
    "persons/3.ttl": """\
<urn:uuid:persons/3> a melod:Person ; schema:givenName "Claude" ;
  schema:familyName "Debussy" ; owl:sameAs <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q4700> .
""",
    "manifestations/4.ttl": """\
<urn:uuid:manifestations/4> a melod:Manifestation ;
  melod:hasTitle [ a melod:Title ; rdfs:label "Suite bergamasque, first edition" ] ;
  lrmoo:R4_embodies <urn:uuid:expressions/2> .
""",
    "items/5.ttl": """\
<urn:uuid:items/5> a melod:Item ; rdfs:label "Copy 1" ; melod:hasShelfmark "TEST 1" ;
  lrmoo:R7_exemplifies <urn:uuid:manifestations/4> .
""",
}
repository = FOLDER / "melody"
for relative, turtle in REPOSITORY.items():
    path = repository / relative
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(PREFIXES + turtle, encoding="utf-8")

suite = MelodyLoader.from_file(repository).create_bundle(
    id="clair_de_lune", date="2026-11-19"
)
[(tl_id, suite.get_timeline(tl_id).name) for tl_id in suite.timeline_ids]

[('cgt_0m4opm12ew51m', 'Suite bergamasque, first edition')]


The one manifestation embodying the work’s expression became a timeline. The work is the value of the bundle’s schema:about, with the triples of its file. IRIs are compacted with the catalogue’s prefixes, which read MeLODy’s https://schema.org/ as schema:.

show(suite, node=("schema:about", 0))

lrmoo:R3_is_realised_in: {"id": "urn:uuid:expressions/2", "label": "Clair de lune, piano"}
melod:hasTitle: {"type": ["melod:Title"], "rdfs:label": [{"@value": "Clair de lune", "@language": "fr"}]}
owl:sameAs: {"id": "wd:Q29117946"}
type: "melod:Work"


The manifestation’s timeline states its own IRI as owl:sameAs, the expression it embodies as a value node and its item under lrmoo:R7i_is_exemplified_by; the item names its manifestation by the timeline’s reference. A person who is no subject is a value, labelled from the triples of its file. Each entry’s basis is the file the pair was read from. The bundle holds one graphical timeline, so a regular expression matching every cgt_ ID finds it.

show(suite.get_timeline("cgt_.*"))

lrmoo:R4_embodies: {"id": "urn:uuid:expressions/2", "type": ["melod:Expression"], "melod:hasContribution": [{"type": ["melod:Contribution"], "melod:hasAgent": [{"id": "urn:uuid:persons/3", "label": "Claude Debussy", "owl:sameAs": [{"id": "wd:Q4700"}]}], "melod:hasRole": [{"id": "melodTerms:Composer"}]}], "rdfs:label": ["Clair de lune, piano"]}
lrmoo:R7i_is_exemplified_by: {"id": "urn:uuid:items/5", "type": ["melod:Item"], "lrmoo:R7_exemplifies": [{"id": "#cgt_0m4opm12ew51m"}], "melod:hasShelfmark": ["TEST 1"], "rdfs:label": ["Copy 1"]}
melod:hasTitle: {"type": ["melod:Title"], "rdfs:label": ["Suite bergamasque, first edition"]}
owl:sameAs: {"id": "urn:uuid:manifestations/4"}
type: "melod:Manifestation"
[stated] rdf:type: {"id": "melod:Manifestation"}
    {"stated_by": ["https://timetoalign.github.io/"], "date": "2026-11-19", "method": "imported", "basis": ["manifestations/4.ttl"]}
[stated] owl:sameAs: {"id": "urn:uuid:manifestations/4"}
    {"stated_by": ["https://timetoalign.github.io/"], "date": "2026-11-19", "method": "imported", "basis": ["manifestations/4.ttl"]}
[stated] lrmoo:R4_embodies: {"id": "urn:uuid:expressions/2"}
    {"stated_by": ["https://timetoalign.github.io/"], "date": "2026-11-19", "method": "imported", "basis": ["manifestations/4.ttl", "expressions/2.ttl"]}
[stated] melod:hasTitle: {"type": ["melod:Title"], "rdfs:label": ["Suite bergamasque, first edition"]}
    {"stated_by": ["https://timetoalign.github.io/"], "date": "2026-11-19", "method": "imported", "basis": ["manifestations/4.ttl"]}
[stated] lrmoo:R7i_is_exemplified_by: {"id": "urn:uuid:items/5"}
    {"stated_by": ["https://timetoalign.github.io/"], "date": "2026-11-19", "method": "imported", "basis": ["items/5.ttl"]}


Both importers’ bundles write manifests as any other, their @context holding the prefixes of LRMoo, MeLODy and the other vocabularies used.

sorted(key for key in suite.to_dict()["@context"] if key not in FORMAT_CONTEXT)

['lrmoo', 'melod', 'melodTerms', 'owl', 'rdf', 'rdfs', 'schema', 'wd']

title: How to Describe What a Bundle and Its Timelines Stand For
text:
add_statement() states one pair on a timeline or a bundle, in place. The bundle is about the work, named here by its Wikidata item; the value is a node, a thing with an id and a label cached for display. The video’s timeline is a video: type takes a class, and the catalogue’s verb is_a states the same in Wikidata’s vocabulary, as an instance of (wdt:P31) the item for a video, wd:Q98069877. add_verb() takes the verb, the system and the value, and states the pairs the catalogue’s pattern for them gives.

bundle.add_statement("schema:about", {"id": "wd:Q29117946", "label": "Clair de lune"})
video.add_statement("type", "schema:VideoObject")
video.add_verb("is_a", "wikidata", "wd:Q98069877")
video.statements

{'type': ['schema:VideoObject'], 'wdt:P31': [{'id': 'wd:Q98069877'}]}
crumbs: How to Describe What a Bundle and Its Timelines Stand For

title: How to Describe What a Bundle and Its Timelines Stand For
text:
The pianist is named in two systems: by a Wikidata item through Wikidata’s property “performer” (wdt:P175), and by a VIAF identifier through the MARC relator “performer” (rel:prf), the fallback for a system without a property of its own. Each pair holds a node of its own.

video.add_verb("performed_by", "wikidata", "wd:Q235650", label="Maria João Pires")
video.add_verb("performed_by", "fallback", "viaf:113931950")
[(rectangle.verb, rectangle.things) for rectangle in video.get_rectangles()]

[('is_a',
  ('http://schema.org/VideoObject',
   'http://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q98069877')),
 ('performed_by', ('http://viaf.org/viaf/113931950',)),
 ('performed_by', ('http://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q235650',))]


get_rectangles() gathers the pairs the catalogue reads as one verb about one thing. So far the two performers are two things. A value node is a subject too: node= addresses it by its path, the property and the index, and schema:sameAs on the Wikidata node ties the two. The pairs then form one rectangle, labelled by the node’s label.

video.add_statement("schema:sameAs", {"id": "viaf:113931950"}, node=("wdt:P175", 0))
[
    (rectangle.verb, rectangle.label, rectangle.things)
    for rectangle in video.get_rectangles()
]

[('is_a',
  None,
  ('http://schema.org/VideoObject',
   'http://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q98069877')),
 ('performed_by',
  'Maria João Pires',
  ('http://viaf.org/viaf/113931950',
   'http://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q235650'))]

title: How to Describe What a Bundle and Its Timelines Stand For
text:
A pair without a provenance entry is stated by the manifest’s publisher. provenance= gives the pair an entry naming who stated it, when, how and why; the keys are those the file writes. actor= records the person stating the pair as believing it, with the belief "true" and the day. A loader or a service records how a pair was made and holds no belief. get_provenance() answers the entries.

video.add_statement(
    "schema:sameAs",
    {"id": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ch2mrPm1JnM"},
    provenance={
        "stated_by": [EDITOR],
        "date": DAY,
        "method": "manual",
        "note": "pasted URL",
    },
    actor=EDITOR,
    date=DAY,
)
video.get_provenance()

[{'property': 'schema:sameAs',
  'value': {'id': 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ch2mrPm1JnM'},
  'stated_by': ['https://example.org/people/editor'],
  'date': '2026-11-18',
  'method': 'manual',
  'note': 'pasted URL',
  'beliefs': [{'actor': 'https://example.org/people/editor',
    'belief': 'true',
    'date': '2026-11-18'}]}]

title: How to Describe What a Bundle and Its Timelines Stand For
text:
A candidate is a pair held only as its entry: the subject does not state it, and it waits for someone to. add_candidate() offers one. The WAV file was cut from the video’s sound, which is an inference. A value naming an element of the manifest is the node of its reference, # followed by its ID, which to_file_id() builds.

source = {"id": to_file_id(video.id)}
wav.add_candidate(
    "dcterms:source",
    source,
    stated_by=EDITOR,
    method="inferred",
    date=DAY,
    note="assumed ripped from the video's sound and cut",
)
show(wav)

[candidate] dcterms:source: {"id": "#cpt_1"}
    {"stated_by": ["https://example.org/people/editor"], "date": "2026-11-18", "method": "inferred", "note": "assumed ripped from the video's sound and cut"}


Stating the candidate with add_statement() makes it a pair of the subject; its entry keeps every key and records the person stating it as believing it.

wav.add_statement("dcterms:source", source, actor=EDITOR, date="2026-11-19")
show(wav)

dcterms:source: {"id": "#cpt_1"}
[stated] dcterms:source: {"id": "#cpt_1"}
    {"stated_by": ["https://example.org/people/editor"], "date": "2026-11-18", "method": "inferred", "note": "assumed ripped from the video's sound and cut", "beliefs": [{"actor": "https://example.org/people/editor", "belief": "true", "date": "2026-11-19"}]}


Any actor may record a belief in any pair with add_belief(): "true", "false" or "unlikely", at most one per actor, a later one replacing the earlier. A belief never changes what is stated: a reviewer who believes the source "false" leaves the pair in place, and nothing derives a truth value from the beliefs. The belief filter reads them for one actor, the believer, keeping the states listed in beliefs= ("true", "undecided" where the believer holds no belief, "unlikely", "false"); by default every state but "false".

wav.add_belief(
    "dcterms:source", source, actor=REVIEWER, belief="false", date="2026-11-20"
)
(
    wav.statements,
    len(wav.get_provenance(believer=REVIEWER)),
    len(wav.get_provenance(believer=EDITOR, beliefs=["true"])),
)

({'dcterms:source': [{'id': '#cpt_1'}]}, 0, 1)


A candidate an actor believes "false" was examined and refused; it is kept, so that it is not offered to that actor again. A lookup in the GND offers its entry “Clair de lune” as the work the encoding is an example of; it is Debussy’s song on Verlaine’s poem, not the piano piece. The entry keeps how the candidate was found beside the belief. get_candidates() answers every candidate, and with believer= those the believer does not believe "false".

score.add_statement("type", "melod:Manifestation")
score.add_candidate(
    "schema:exampleOfWork",
    {"id": "gnd:1156628156"},
    stated_by=EDITOR,
    method="reconciled",
    service="https://lobid.org/gnd/search",
    date=DAY,
)
score.add_belief(
    "schema:exampleOfWork",
    {"id": "gnd:1156628156"},
    actor=EDITOR,
    belief="false",
    date=DAY,
    note="GND 'Clair de lune' is Debussy's song L 32 on Verlaine, not the piano piece",
)
show(score)
len(score.get_candidates()), score.get_candidates(believer=EDITOR)

title: How to Describe What a Bundle and Its Timelines Stand For
text:
A region stands for the stretch of its timeline’s manifestation it marks. Regions are frozen: with_statement() returns a copy holding the pair, and replace_region() stores it in the place of the region with its ID. The region’s siblings without_statement(), with_candidate(), with_belief(), with_verb() and with_prefix() mirror the timeline’s remove_statement(), add_candidate(), add_belief(), add_verb() and add_prefix().

opening = score.create_region(0, 9, id="opening", name="mm. 1–2")
score.replace_region(
    opening.with_statement("rdfs:comment", "the opening, before the melody enters")
)
opening.statements, score.get_region("opening").statements

({}, {'rdfs:comment': ['the opening, before the melody enters']})

title: How to Save and Load Timelines, Groups and Bundles
text:
A Timeline, a TimelineGroup and an AlignmentBundle each write one TimeToShare manifest with to_dict() and read one with from_dict(). Every manifest has the same shape, whatever it holds, and every manifest is an alignment bundle:

a single timeline writes a bundle of one root timeline;
a group writes a bundle of one group;
a bundle writes any number of timelines and groups.

A manifest that carries an id or a name is a named bundle; one with neither is an anonymous bundle.
This guide writes each of the three, reads them back, checks that the rebuilt objects answer every query exactly as the originals do, selects one timeline or group out of a larger manifest, saves the manifests as files with to_file() and reads them with from_file(), and edits a file the way a reviewed change would. It ends with a timeline whose length is not known.
A manifest holds structure: timelines, their children, conversion maps, regions and flow control, the measure maps the conversion maps read, and the groups and their members, with the members’ display order. MatchClaims are not part of it, nor is a bundle’s support policy, which is a setting of the bundle. Events stay out unless you ask for them.


Install the library with pip install timetoalign; the TimeToShare package comes with it. Three small helpers keep the cells below short: answers lists what a stamp says about every timeline it reaches, show prints a manifest as the text a file would hold, in canonical YAML (see Save and load files), with its @context reduced to the prefixes beyond the format’s own terms, and outline shows a manifest with each root timeline reduced to its id and without its @context.

import difflib
import tempfile
from fractions import Fraction
from pathlib import Path

from timetoshare import FORMAT_CONTEXT, dumps

from timetoalign import (
    AlignmentBundle,
    ContinuousLogicalTimeline,
    ContinuousPhysicalTimeline,
    DiscreteGraphicalTimeline,
    DiscretePhysicalTimeline,
    Timeline,
    TimelineGroup,
    UnknownLengthError,
)

FILES = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())


def answers(stamps):
    """Map each stamp to its coordinates, one per timeline it reaches."""
    return [
        {
            timeline_id: stamp.get_coordinate_for(timeline_id)
            for timeline_id in stamp.present_timelines
        }
        for stamp in stamps
    ]


def show(data):
    """Print a manifest as canonical YAML, its context reduced to the prefixes."""
    context = data.get("@context", {})
    prefixes = {
        key: value for key, value in context.items() if key not in FORMAT_CONTEXT
    }
    print(dumps({**data, "@context": prefixes}), end="")


def outline(data):
    """Show a manifest with each root timeline reduced to its id, without its context."""
    rest = {key: value for key, value in data.items() if key != "@context"}
    return {**rest, "timelines": [timeline["id"] for timeline in data["timelines"]]}




A score of sixteen quarters with one region.

score = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=Fraction(16), name="Score")
score.create_region(0, 8, name="First half")
score

ContinuousLogicalTimeline[clt_2zjcv11ok5rjn] (1 regions)
                      0 __________________________________ 16 quarters


to_dict() writes the minimal form: every key holding its default is left out, length being the one key written in every form. The manifest carries the version marker timetoshare: "0.2.0"; its timelines array holds the score as its one root.
A value on the timeline’s own axis (its length, a region’s start and end) is written bare, in the axis’s number type: quarters count in exact fractions, so sixteen quarters are the pair [16, 1]. The library’s class is not written: the unit decides it.
Every ID in a manifest, an element’s own and every reference to one, is written # followed by the ID: the score’s minted ID clt_… is written #clt_…. The objects hold their IDs without it, so score.id reads clt_….
Every manifest written opens with an inline JSON-LD @context: the format’s own terms (timetoshare.FORMAT_CONTEXT) and the prefixes its statements use, none here, which is why show prints it empty. A file holds the whole context; the statements are the subject of How to Describe What a Bundle and Its Timelines Stand For.

show(score_data)

Timeline.from_dict() reads either form and supplies every default that is left out. It returns the class the unit decides, here a ContinuousLogicalTimeline for quarters. Both forms read to the same timeline: each writes back the minimal form of the original, and its complete form.

    from_minimal.to_dict(minimal=False) == score_complete,

Because every default may be left out, a manifest is easy to write by hand. The smallest one names the version and one timeline with its id, unit and length, the ID written with its #. In a manifest of one timeline and no group, timeline_id= and name= override that timeline’s id and name as it is read, unless a timeline of the manifest already has that id or name: such a timeline is selected instead, and an id and a name given together must then name the same timeline.

    "timetoshare": "0.2.0",
    "timelines": [{"id": "#piece", "unit": "quarters", "length": [32, 1]}],
}

piece.id, piece.name, piece.length

    Timeline.from_dict(

            "timelines": [{"id": "#piece", "unit": "quarters", "length": 32}],

A group’s members share one start and one end: every member’s 0 coincides with every other member’s 0, and every member’s length with every other member’s length. Positions in between convert linearly and exactly.
Here only the second half of a score takes part, alongside a recording and a scanned page. The second half is a child of the score, placed at its exact offset, and the child is the member. The three members carry three number types: quarters as fractions, seconds as floats, pixels as integers. They are added page first, so their display order differs from their id order.

score = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=Fraction(16), name="Score")
second_half = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=Fraction(8), name="Second half")
score.add_child(second_half, offset=Fraction(8))
recording = ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=10.0, name="Recording")
page = DiscreteGraphicalTimeline(length=1920, name="Page")

group = TimelineGroup(name="Second half", timelines=[page, second_half, recording])
group.id, group.timeline_ids

A group writes an anonymous bundle holding its group:

groups: the one group, with its id, its name and its members, the member ids sorted so that two equal groups write equal text.
graphical.order: the members in the order they were added, keyed by the group’s id. This is the display order.

A bundle holds timelines and the groups among them. This one has two groups and timelines that belong to none:

Performance: a score and a performance recording;
Facsimile: a page and an excerpt of a long recording, the excerpt being a child of that recording;
ungrouped: an annotation layer, and the long recording itself. When a child joins a group, its root joins the bundle too, ungrouped unless you group it.

as_group= names a new group; its id is minted (group_…).

bundle.add_timeline(page, as_group="Facsimile")
bundle.add_timeline(excerpt, grouped_with=page.id)

Its timelines array holds every root timeline of the bundle, so each timeline is written once; its groups, sorted by id, point into that one array; graphical.order holds each group’s display order. to_file() writes an object’s manifest to a file and returns its path; from_file() reads a file as from_dict() reads a manifest, taking the same selection arguments.
The format’s validator checks every manifest the library reads and every manifest it writes. A manifest it refuses raises a ValueError, and to_file() then writes no file.
A file is written in canonical YAML unless you ask for another serialization: the keys of every object sorted, the arrays in a canonical order, every member and every item on lines of its own, and a list of plain values, such as a Fraction pair, on one line. A manifest file has a form (minimal or complete), may hold styling (a graphical object) and has a serialization: canonical YAML ("yaml"), pretty JSON ("json") or RFC 8785 JSON ("jcs"), whose bytes suit a digest or a signature. from_file() reads all three and notes what it found: the form is minimal when no key holds its default, and the serialization is the one the text is written in. to_file() writes an object read from a file back in the same form, styling and serialization. A file in canonical YAML, pretty JSON or RFC 8785 JSON that is read and written back unchanged so keeps its bytes; any other JSON or YAML text is written back in the canonical form of the serialization it was read as. minimal=, styling= and serialization= override each; an object built in code is written in the minimal form, its styling included, in canonical YAML.
Here the bundle is saved as pretty JSON in the complete form, and a copy written from the file read back is the same file, byte for byte.

bundle_path = bundle.to_file(
    FILES / "edition.json", minimal=False, serialization="json"
)
copy_path = AlignmentBundle.from_file(bundle_path).to_file(FILES / "copy.json")
print(*bundle_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()[:12], sep="\n")
copy_path.read_bytes() == bundle_path.read_bytes()

    "@version": 1.1,

    },

Manifests are meant to be kept in a repository and changed by reviewed pull requests. The workflow is: read the file, enrich what it holds, write it back, and review the diff. Canonical YAML keeps every change to its own lines, so the diff shows what was added and nothing else.
Here a second performance joins the performance’s group in the bundle’s YAML file.

edition_path = bundle.to_file(FILES / "edition.yaml")
before_text = edition_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

edition = AlignmentBundle.from_file(edition_path)
second_take = ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=13.25, name="Second performance")
edition.add_timeline(second_take, grouped_with=performance.id)
edition.to_file(edition_path)

diff = difflib.unified_diff(
    before_text.splitlines(keepends=True),
    edition_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(keepends=True),
    "edition.yaml",
    "edition.yaml (edited)",
)
print("".join(diff), end="")

--- edition.yaml
+++ edition.yaml (edited)
@@ -55,12 +55,12 @@
   value: "http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#object"
 graphical:
   order:
-    "#group_1to9tdyc2vduc": ["#cpt_0mb1ovv8h6nu0", "#clt_0w16gtqdm1hof"]
+    "#group_1to9tdyc2vduc": ["#cpt_0mb1ovv8h6nu0", "#clt_0w16gtqdm1hof", "#cpt_0bm2e5r8e8utu"]
     "#group_2whxqvkk96nwi": ["#dgt_1zrfm79dc2qu2", "#dpt_325i5pqhkjql7"]
 groups:
   -
     id: "#group_1to9tdyc2vduc"
-    members: ["#clt_0w16gtqdm1hof", "#cpt_0mb1ovv8h6nu0"]
+    members: ["#clt_0w16gtqdm1hof", "#cpt_0bm2e5r8e8utu", "#cpt_0mb1ovv8h6nu0"]
     name: Performance
   -
     id: "#group_2whxqvkk96nwi"
@@ -78,6 +78,11 @@
     length: [12, 1]
     name: Annotations
     unit: quarters
+  -
+    id: "#cpt_0bm2e5r8e8utu"
+    length: 13.25
+    name: "Second performance"
+    unit: seconds
   -
     id: "#cpt_0mb1ovv8h6nu0"
     length: 12.5


The diff holds the lines of the new timeline, and the one line each of the group’s members and of its display order in graphical.order, which now name it. Every other line of the file is unchanged.



Some timelines have no known end: a live stream still running, a recording whose duration has not been measured. length=None states that the length is not known. It is a fact about the timeline, never inferred from its content: adding content leaves it unknown.

stream = ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=None, name="Live stream")
stream.create_region(30.0, 45.0, name="Interview")
stream.add_child(ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=20.0, name="Clip"), offset=100.0)
stream.length, stream.end, stream.is_length_known

(None, None, False)


Its positions are not bounded above, so a query far beyond all content still resolves. The reach is the farthest coordinate the content reaches, here the clip’s end at 120 seconds; the diagram is drawn to it and marks the unknown end ?.

stream.get_timestamp_at(1000.0), stream.reach

(TimeStamp(axis=1000 seconds @cpt_0qmf1es92eejz, source='cpt_0qmf1es92eejz'),
 Coordinate(120.0, seconds))



stream

ContinuousPhysicalTimeline[cpt_0qmf1es92eejz] (1 children, 1 regions)
                      0 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ ? seconds
  └─ Clip           100                               ~~~~~~ 120


A manifest writes the unknown length as null, in both forms, and reading it gives back a timeline whose length is not known.

stream_data = stream.to_dict()
show(stream_data)
Timeline.from_dict(stream_data).is_length_known

"@context": {}
timelines:
  -
    children:
      -
        id: "#cpt_2dgcya08y5my0"
        length: 20.0
        locked: true
        name: Clip
        offset: 100.0
        unit: seconds
    id: "#cpt_0qmf1es92eejz"
    length: null
    name: "Live stream"
    regions:
      -
        end: 45.0
        id: "#region_3b0pyrqpa8lof"
        name: Interview
        start: 30.0
    unit: seconds
timetoshare: "0.2.0"


False


Operations that need the end raise UnknownLengthError, a ValueError that names the operation and the timeline, before they change anything. A group converts positions in proportion to its members’ lengths, so a conversion to or from a member of unknown length is one of them; appending a child at a parent’s end is another.

programme = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=Fraction(16), name="Programme")
broadcast = TimelineGroup(name="Broadcast", timelines=[programme, stream])
for operation in (
    lambda: broadcast.get_timestamp_at(Fraction(4), programme.id),
    lambda: stream.append_child(ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=10.0)),
):
    try:
        operation()
    except UnknownLengthError as error:
        print(f"UnknownLengthError: {error}")

UnknownLengthError: Cannot convert a position from 'clt_05m23yu04a4xh' to 'cpt_0qmf1es92eejz': the length of timeline 'cpt_0qmf1es92eejz' is unknown
UnknownLengthError: Cannot append a child: the length of timeline 'cpt_0qmf1es92eejz' is unknown


Once the length is known, setting it is an ordinary edit, and every operation is available again.

stream.length = 3600.0
stream.is_length_known, answers([broadcast.get_timestamp_at(Fraction(4), programme.id)])

(True,
 [{'clt_05m23yu04a4xh': IdCoordinate(Fraction(4, 1), quarters, 'clt_05m23yu04a4xh'),
   'cpt_0qmf1es92eejz': IdCoordinate(900.0, seconds, 'cpt_0qmf1es92eejz')}])






Events: to_dict(events=True) writes every timeline’s event rows into the dict; see How to Construct Timelines Manually. A bundle’s file names no event: to_file(events=True) writes its events into the registry beside the manifest, their content into one pre-parsed table per event type; see How to Write the Registry and Share Tables in a Package.
Groups in depth: the Timeline Groups tutorial.
Alignments between groups: the Alignment Bundles and MatchClaims tutorial.

title: How to Save and Load Timelines, Groups and Bundles
text:
A score of sixteen quarters with one region.

score = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=Fraction(16), name="Score")
score.create_region(0, 8, name="First half")
score

ContinuousLogicalTimeline[clt_2zjcv11ok5rjn] (1 regions)
                      0 __________________________________ 16 quarters


to_dict() writes the minimal form: every key holding its default is left out, length being the one key written in every form. The manifest carries the version marker timetoshare: "0.2.0"; its timelines array holds the score as its one root.
A value on the timeline’s own axis (its length, a region’s start and end) is written bare, in the axis’s number type: quarters count in exact fractions, so sixteen quarters are the pair [16, 1]. The library’s class is not written: the unit decides it.
Every ID in a manifest, an element’s own and every reference to one, is written # followed by the ID: the score’s minted ID clt_… is written #clt_…. The objects hold their IDs without it, so score.id reads clt_….
Every manifest written opens with an inline JSON-LD @context: the format’s own terms (timetoshare.FORMAT_CONTEXT) and the prefixes its statements use, none here, which is why show prints it empty. A file holds the whole context; the statements are the subject of How to Describe What a Bundle and Its Timelines Stand For.

score_data = score.to_dict()
show(score_data)

"@context": {}
timelines:
  -
    id: "#clt_2zjcv11ok5rjn"
    length: [16, 1]
    name: Score
    regions:
      -
        end: [8, 1]
        id: "#region_10it1ir9e4m5e"
        name: "First half"
        start: [0, 1]
    unit: quarters
timetoshare: "0.2.0"


to_dict(minimal=False) writes the complete form: every key the format defines, each written even when it holds its default (null, {}, []).

score_complete = score.to_dict(minimal=False)
show(score_complete)

"@context": {}
groups: []
measure_maps: []
meta: {}
name: null
resources: []
timelines:
  -
    children: []
    conversion_maps: []
    flow_control: []
    id: "#clt_2zjcv11ok5rjn"
    is_segment_line: false
    length: [16, 1]
    locked: false
    meta: {}
    name: Score
    number_type: fraction
    regions:
      -
        end: [8, 1]
        id: "#region_10it1ir9e4m5e"
        meta: {}
        name: "First half"
        start: [0, 1]
    unit: quarters
timetoshare: "0.2.0"

title: How to Save and Load Timelines, Groups and Bundles
text:
Timeline.from_dict() reads either form and supplies every default that is left out. It returns the class the unit decides, here a ContinuousLogicalTimeline for quarters. Both forms read to the same timeline: each writes back the minimal form of the original, and its complete form.

from_minimal = Timeline.from_dict(score_data)
from_complete = Timeline.from_dict(score_complete)
(
    type(from_minimal).__name__,
    from_complete.to_dict() == from_minimal.to_dict() == score_data,
    from_minimal.to_dict(minimal=False) == score_complete,
)

('ContinuousLogicalTimeline', True, True)


Because every default may be left out, a manifest is easy to write by hand. The smallest one names the version and one timeline with its id, unit and length, the ID written with its #. In a manifest of one timeline and no group, timeline_id= and name= override that timeline’s id and name as it is read, unless a timeline of the manifest already has that id or name: such a timeline is selected instead, and an id and a name given together must then name the same timeline.

smallest = {
    "timetoshare": "0.2.0",
    "timelines": [{"id": "#piece", "unit": "quarters", "length": [32, 1]}],
}
piece = Timeline.from_dict(smallest, name="Full score")
piece.id, piece.name, piece.length

('piece', 'Full score', Coordinate(Fraction(32, 1), quarters))


A bare value must be written in its axis’s number type; reading never coerces it. A length of 32 on a quarters axis is an integer where the axis counts fractions. The error names the value’s place in the manifest, as a JSON pointer, and says what to write instead.

try:
    Timeline.from_dict(
        {
            "timetoshare": "0.2.0",
            "timelines": [{"id": "#piece", "unit": "quarters", "length": 32}],
        }
    )
except ValueError as error:
    print(f"ValueError: {error}")

ValueError: #/timelines/0/length: length 32 of 'piece' is an int on a fraction axis: write [32, 1]

title: How to Save and Load Timelines, Groups and Bundles
text:
A group’s members share one start and one end: every member’s 0 coincides with every other member’s 0, and every member’s length with every other member’s length. Positions in between convert linearly and exactly.
Here only the second half of a score takes part, alongside a recording and a scanned page. The second half is a child of the score, placed at its exact offset, and the child is the member. The three members carry three number types: quarters as fractions, seconds as floats, pixels as integers. They are added page first, so their display order differs from their id order.

score = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=Fraction(16), name="Score")
second_half = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=Fraction(8), name="Second half")
score.add_child(second_half, offset=Fraction(8))
recording = ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=10.0, name="Recording")
page = DiscreteGraphicalTimeline(length=1920, name="Page")

group = TimelineGroup(name="Second half", timelines=[page, second_half, recording])
group.id, group.timeline_ids

('group_2q8my9zelevxv',
 ['dgt_1orwcwwfq03tb', 'clt_2muyd6ylpzh8r', 'cpt_3pjxm0c9p6iip'])


One third of a quarter into the second half is 1/3 · 10/8 = 5/12 seconds into the recording and 1/3 · 1920/8 = 80 pixels into the page. The conversion is computed exactly, and each answer is then written in its member’s own number type: a Fraction of quarters, an integer of pixels, and for the recording the float nearest to 5/12, 0.4166666666666667.

positions = [Fraction(0), Fraction(1, 3), Fraction(3), Fraction(8)]
before = answers(group.get_timestamps_at(positions, second_half.id))
before

[{'clt_2muyd6ylpzh8r': IdCoordinate(Fraction(0, 1), quarters, 'clt_2muyd6ylpzh8r'),
  'dgt_1orwcwwfq03tb': IdCoordinate(0, pixels, 'dgt_1orwcwwfq03tb'),
  'cpt_3pjxm0c9p6iip': IdCoordinate(0.0, seconds, 'cpt_3pjxm0c9p6iip')},
 {'clt_2muyd6ylpzh8r': IdCoordinate(Fraction(1, 3), quarters, 'clt_2muyd6ylpzh8r'),
  'dgt_1orwcwwfq03tb': IdCoordinate(80, pixels, 'dgt_1orwcwwfq03tb'),
  'cpt_3pjxm0c9p6iip': IdCoordinate(0.4166666666666667, seconds, 'cpt_3pjxm0c9p6iip')},
 {'clt_2muyd6ylpzh8r': IdCoordinate(Fraction(3, 1), quarters, 'clt_2muyd6ylpzh8r'),
  'dgt_1orwcwwfq03tb': IdCoordinate(720, pixels, 'dgt_1orwcwwfq03tb'),
  'cpt_3pjxm0c9p6iip': IdCoordinate(3.75, seconds, 'cpt_3pjxm0c9p6iip')},
 {'clt_2muyd6ylpzh8r': IdCoordinate(Fraction(8, 1), quarters, 'clt_2muyd6ylpzh8r'),
  'dgt_1orwcwwfq03tb': IdCoordinate(1920, pixels, 'dgt_1orwcwwfq03tb'),
  'cpt_3pjxm0c9p6iip': IdCoordinate(10.0, seconds, 'cpt_3pjxm0c9p6iip')}]


A group writes an anonymous bundle holding its group:

timelines: the root of every member, sorted by id; a member that is a child arrives inside its root. Here the second half arrives inside the score, among the score’s children.
groups: the one group, with its id, its name and its members, the member ids sorted so that two equal groups write equal text.
graphical.order: the members in the order they were added, keyed by the group’s id. This is the display order.

The minimal form shows the structure without the defaults.

group_data = group.to_dict()
show(group_data)

"@context": {}
graphical:
  order:
    "#group_2q8my9zelevxv": ["#dgt_1orwcwwfq03tb", "#clt_2muyd6ylpzh8r", "#cpt_3pjxm0c9p6iip"]
groups:
  -
    id: "#group_2q8my9zelevxv"
    members: ["#clt_2muyd6ylpzh8r", "#cpt_3pjxm0c9p6iip", "#dgt_1orwcwwfq03tb"]
    name: "Second half"
timelines:
  -
    children:
      -
        id: "#clt_2muyd6ylpzh8r"
        length: [8, 1]
        locked: true
        name: "Second half"
        offset: [8, 1]
        unit: quarters
    id: "#clt_2vmtd2dv5nsp8"
    length: [16, 1]
    name: Score
    unit: quarters
  -
    id: "#cpt_3pjxm0c9p6iip"
    length: 10.0
    name: Recording
    unit: seconds
  -
    id: "#dgt_1orwcwwfq03tb"
    length: 1920
    name: Page
    unit: pixels
timetoshare: "0.2.0"


A child’s offset is a bare value on its parent’s axis, in its parent’s number type: the second half starts at [8, 1] quarters into the score. add_child() locks a child unless it is given locked=False, so this one writes locked: true. An unlocked child writes false, and reading keeps whichever the manifest states.

group_data["timelines"][0]["children"][0]["offset"]

[8, 1]


graphical may also carry styles, rules, timestamps and matchstamps, the TimeToShare styling. The library does not interpret them: from_dict() keeps them as the group’s styling and to_dict() writes them back. In the complete form they appear at their defaults.

group.to_dict(minimal=False)["graphical"]

{'order': {'#group_2q8my9zelevxv': ['#dgt_1orwcwwfq03tb',
   '#clt_2muyd6ylpzh8r',
   '#cpt_3pjxm0c9p6iip']},
 'styles': {},
 'rules': [],
 'timestamps': [],
 'matchstamps': [],
 'elisions': []}

title: How to Save and Load Timelines, Groups and Bundles
text:
TimelineGroup.from_dict() rebuilds the timelines, resolves each member id among the roots and their descendants, and adds the members in their display order. The rebuilt group writes the same manifest and answers the same queries with the same coordinates, in the same number types.

rebuilt = TimelineGroup.from_dict(group_data)
(
    rebuilt.timeline_ids,
    rebuilt.to_dict() == group_data,
    answers(rebuilt.get_timestamps_at(positions, second_half.id)) == before,
)

(['dgt_1orwcwwfq03tb', 'clt_2muyd6ylpzh8r', 'cpt_3pjxm0c9p6iip'], True, True)

title: How to Save and Load Timelines, Groups and Bundles
text:
A bundle holds timelines and the groups among them. This one has two groups and timelines that belong to none:

Performance: a score and a performance recording;
Facsimile: a page and an excerpt of a long recording, the excerpt being a child of that recording;
ungrouped: an annotation layer, and the long recording itself. When a child joins a group, its root joins the bundle too, ungrouped unless you group it.

as_group= names a new group; its id is minted (group_…).

score = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=Fraction(12), name="Score")
performance = ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=12.5, name="Performance")
page = DiscreteGraphicalTimeline(length=1920, name="Page")
long_recording = DiscretePhysicalTimeline(length=441000, name="Recording")
excerpt = DiscretePhysicalTimeline(length=88200, name="Excerpt")
long_recording.add_child(excerpt, offset=44100)
annotations = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=Fraction(12), name="Annotations")

bundle = AlignmentBundle(name="Edition")
bundle.add_timeline(performance, as_group="Performance")
bundle.add_timeline(score, grouped_with=performance.id)
bundle.add_timeline(page, as_group="Facsimile")
bundle.add_timeline(excerpt, grouped_with=page.id)
bundle.add_timeline(annotations)

{group_id: bundle.get_group(group_id).timeline_ids for group_id in bundle.group_ids}

{'group_1to9tdyc2vduc': ['cpt_0mb1ovv8h6nu0', 'clt_0w16gtqdm1hof'],
 'group_2whxqvkk96nwi': ['dgt_1zrfm79dc2qu2', 'dpt_325i5pqhkjql7']}


Within a group, a MatchStamp converts linearly, as the group does. A position on the excerpt also reaches its root through the child’s offset.

bundle_queries = {
    score.id: [Fraction(0), Fraction(3), Fraction(12)],
    excerpt.id: [0, 22050, 88200],
}
bundle_before = {
    timeline_id: answers(bundle.get_matchstamps_at(at, timeline_id))
    for timeline_id, at in bundle_queries.items()
}
bundle_before

{'clt_0w16gtqdm1hof': [{'clt_0w16gtqdm1hof': IdCoordinate(Fraction(0, 1), quarters, 'clt_0w16gtqdm1hof'),
   'cpt_0mb1ovv8h6nu0': IdCoordinate(0.0, seconds, 'cpt_0mb1ovv8h6nu0')},
  {'clt_0w16gtqdm1hof': IdCoordinate(Fraction(3, 1), quarters, 'clt_0w16gtqdm1hof'),
   'cpt_0mb1ovv8h6nu0': IdCoordinate(3.125, seconds, 'cpt_0mb1ovv8h6nu0')},
  {'clt_0w16gtqdm1hof': IdCoordinate(Fraction(12, 1), quarters, 'clt_0w16gtqdm1hof'),
   'cpt_0mb1ovv8h6nu0': IdCoordinate(12.5, seconds, 'cpt_0mb1ovv8h6nu0')}],
 'dpt_325i5pqhkjql7': [{'dpt_325i5pqhkjql7': IdCoordinate(0, samples, 'dpt_325i5pqhkjql7'),
   'dgt_1zrfm79dc2qu2': IdCoordinate(0, pixels, 'dgt_1zrfm79dc2qu2'),
   'dpt_3uw8nvr6a3vhp': IdCoordinate(44100, samples, 'dpt_3uw8nvr6a3vhp')},
  {'dpt_325i5pqhkjql7': IdCoordinate(22050, samples, 'dpt_325i5pqhkjql7'),
   'dgt_1zrfm79dc2qu2': IdCoordinate(480, pixels, 'dgt_1zrfm79dc2qu2'),
   'dpt_3uw8nvr6a3vhp': IdCoordinate(66150, samples, 'dpt_3uw8nvr6a3vhp')},
  {'dpt_325i5pqhkjql7': IdCoordinate(88200, samples, 'dpt_325i5pqhkjql7'),
   'dgt_1zrfm79dc2qu2': IdCoordinate(1920, pixels, 'dgt_1zrfm79dc2qu2'),
   'dpt_3uw8nvr6a3vhp': IdCoordinate(132300, samples, 'dpt_3uw8nvr6a3vhp')}]}


A bundle writes the same shape. Its timelines array holds every root timeline of the bundle, so each timeline is written once; its groups, sorted by id, point into that one array; graphical.order holds each group’s display order. The roots that no group names, here the annotation layer and the long recording, are the ungrouped timelines.
This bundle has a name, so it writes a named bundle. It has no id: the bundle was given none, and the id it minted for itself is never written. id and name are independent; a manifest may carry either, both or neither.

bundle_data = bundle.to_dict()
outline(bundle_data)

{'timetoshare': '0.2.0',
 'name': 'Edition',
 'timelines': ['#clt_0w16gtqdm1hof',
  '#clt_1ie1yiu0kg5bg',
  '#cpt_0mb1ovv8h6nu0',
  '#dgt_1zrfm79dc2qu2',
  '#dpt_3uw8nvr6a3vhp'],
 'groups': [{'id': '#group_1to9tdyc2vduc',
   'name': 'Performance',
   'members': ['#clt_0w16gtqdm1hof', '#cpt_0mb1ovv8h6nu0']},
  {'id': '#group_2whxqvkk96nwi',
   'name': 'Facsimile',
   'members': ['#dgt_1zrfm79dc2qu2', '#dpt_325i5pqhkjql7']}],
 'graphical': {'order': {'#group_1to9tdyc2vduc': ['#cpt_0mb1ovv8h6nu0',
    '#clt_0w16gtqdm1hof'],
   '#group_2whxqvkk96nwi': ['#dgt_1zrfm79dc2qu2', '#dpt_325i5pqhkjql7']}}}

title: How to Save and Load Timelines, Groups and Bundles
text:
From a manifest that holds several timelines or any group, Timeline.from_dict() reads one timeline, which timeline_id= or name= (or both) select. The selected timeline may be a root or any descendant, here the excerpt, a child of the long recording.

excerpt_read = Timeline.from_dict(bundle_data, name="Excerpt")
excerpt_read

DiscretePhysicalTimeline[dpt_325i5pqhkjql7]
                      0 ⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅⋅ 88200 samples


TimelineGroup.from_dict() selects one group the same way, by group_id= or name=, and reads it with the timelines its members need.

facsimile = TimelineGroup.from_dict(bundle_data, name="Facsimile")
facsimile.id, facsimile.timeline_ids

('group_2whxqvkk96nwi', ['dgt_1zrfm79dc2qu2', 'dpt_325i5pqhkjql7'])


A selection must match exactly one timeline. Without a selection the read is refused; a selection that matches none lists the manifest’s timelines to choose from.

for selection in ({}, {"name": "Coda"}):
    try:
        Timeline.from_dict(bundle_data, **selection)
    except ValueError as error:
        print(f"ValueError: {error}")

ValueError: the manifest holds several timelines or groups: give timeline_id or name to select one; its timelines: 'clt_0w16gtqdm1hof' (name 'Score'), 'clt_1ie1yiu0kg5bg' (name 'Annotations'), 'cpt_0mb1ovv8h6nu0' (name 'Performance'), 'dgt_1zrfm79dc2qu2' (name 'Page'), 'dpt_3uw8nvr6a3vhp' (name 'Recording'), 'dpt_325i5pqhkjql7' (name 'Excerpt')

title: How to Save and Load Timelines, Groups and Bundles
text:
to_file() writes an object’s manifest to a file and returns its path; from_file() reads a file as from_dict() reads a manifest, taking the same selection arguments.
The format’s validator checks every manifest the library reads and every manifest it writes. A manifest it refuses raises a ValueError, and to_file() then writes no file.
A file is written in canonical YAML unless you ask for another serialization: the keys of every object sorted, the arrays in a canonical order, every member and every item on lines of its own, and a list of plain values, such as a Fraction pair, on one line. Equal manifests so give equal text. Floats keep their float spelling: the recording’s 10.0 seconds stay 10.0. The file opens with the whole @context.

group_path = group.to_file(FILES / "second_half.yaml")
print(group_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), end="")

The group read from the file writes the same manifest and answers the same queries.

group_read = TimelineGroup.from_file(group_path)
(
    group_read.to_dict() == group_data,
    answers(group_read.get_timestamps_at(positions, second_half.id)) == before,
)

(True, True)


A manifest file has a form (minimal or complete), may hold styling (a graphical object) and has a serialization: canonical YAML ("yaml"), pretty JSON ("json") or RFC 8785 JSON ("jcs"), whose bytes suit a digest or a signature. from_file() reads all three and notes what it found: the form is minimal when no key holds its default, and the serialization is the one the text is written in. to_file() writes an object read from a file back in the same form, styling and serialization. A file in canonical YAML, pretty JSON or RFC 8785 JSON that is read and written back unchanged so keeps its bytes; any other JSON or YAML text is written back in the canonical form of the serialization it was read as. minimal=, styling= and serialization= override each; an object built in code is written in the minimal form, its styling included, in canonical YAML.
Here the bundle is saved as pretty JSON in the complete form, and a copy written from the file read back is the same file, byte for byte.

bundle_path = bundle.to_file(
    FILES / "edition.json", minimal=False, serialization="json"
)
copy_path = AlignmentBundle.from_file(bundle_path).to_file(FILES / "copy.json")
print(*bundle_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()[:12], sep="\n")
copy_path.read_bytes() == bundle_path.read_bytes()

title: How to Save and Load Timelines, Groups and Bundles
text:
Manifests are meant to be kept in a repository and changed by reviewed pull requests. The workflow is: read the file, enrich what it holds, write it back, and review the diff. Canonical YAML keeps every change to its own lines, so the diff shows what was added and nothing else.
Here a second performance joins the performance’s group in the bundle’s YAML file.

edition_path = bundle.to_file(FILES / "edition.yaml")
before_text = edition_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

edition = AlignmentBundle.from_file(edition_path)
second_take = ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=13.25, name="Second performance")
edition.add_timeline(second_take, grouped_with=performance.id)
edition.to_file(edition_path)

diff = difflib.unified_diff(
    before_text.splitlines(keepends=True),
    edition_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(keepends=True),
    "edition.yaml",
    "edition.yaml (edited)",
)
print("".join(diff), end="")

--- edition.yaml
+++ edition.yaml (edited)
@@ -55,12 +55,12 @@
   value: "http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#object"
 graphical:
   order:
-    "#group_1to9tdyc2vduc": ["#cpt_0mb1ovv8h6nu0", "#clt_0w16gtqdm1hof"]
+    "#group_1to9tdyc2vduc": ["#cpt_0mb1ovv8h6nu0", "#clt_0w16gtqdm1hof", "#cpt_0bm2e5r8e8utu"]
     "#group_2whxqvkk96nwi": ["#dgt_1zrfm79dc2qu2", "#dpt_325i5pqhkjql7"]
 groups:
   -
     id: "#group_1to9tdyc2vduc"
-    members: ["#clt_0w16gtqdm1hof", "#cpt_0mb1ovv8h6nu0"]
+    members: ["#clt_0w16gtqdm1hof", "#cpt_0bm2e5r8e8utu", "#cpt_0mb1ovv8h6nu0"]
     name: Performance
   -
     id: "#group_2whxqvkk96nwi"
@@ -78,6 +78,11 @@
     length: [12, 1]
     name: Annotations
     unit: quarters
+  -
+    id: "#cpt_0bm2e5r8e8utu"
+    length: 13.25
+    name: "Second performance"
+    unit: seconds
   -
     id: "#cpt_0mb1ovv8h6nu0"
     length: 12.5


The diff holds the lines of the new timeline, and the one line each of the group’s members and of its display order in graphical.order, which now name it. Every other line of the file is unchanged.

title: How to Save and Load Timelines, Groups and Bundles
text:
Some timelines have no known end: a live stream still running, a recording whose duration has not been measured. length=None states that the length is not known. It is a fact about the timeline, never inferred from its content: adding content leaves it unknown.

stream = ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=None, name="Live stream")
stream.create_region(30.0, 45.0, name="Interview")
stream.add_child(ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=20.0, name="Clip"), offset=100.0)
stream.length, stream.end, stream.is_length_known

(None, None, False)


Its positions are not bounded above, so a query far beyond all content still resolves. The reach is the farthest coordinate the content reaches, here the clip’s end at 120 seconds; the diagram is drawn to it and marks the unknown end ?.

stream.get_timestamp_at(1000.0), stream.reach

(TimeStamp(axis=1000 seconds @cpt_0qmf1es92eejz, source='cpt_0qmf1es92eejz'),
 Coordinate(120.0, seconds))



stream

ContinuousPhysicalTimeline[cpt_0qmf1es92eejz] (1 children, 1 regions)
                      0 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ ? seconds
  └─ Clip           100                               ~~~~~~ 120


A manifest writes the unknown length as null, in both forms, and reading it gives back a timeline whose length is not known.

stream_data = stream.to_dict()
show(stream_data)
Timeline.from_dict(stream_data).is_length_known

"@context": {}
timelines:
  -
    children:
      -
        id: "#cpt_2dgcya08y5my0"
        length: 20.0
        locked: true
        name: Clip
        offset: 100.0
        unit: seconds
    id: "#cpt_0qmf1es92eejz"
    length: null
    name: "Live stream"
    regions:
      -
        end: 45.0
        id: "#region_3b0pyrqpa8lof"
        name: Interview
        start: 30.0
    unit: seconds
timetoshare: "0.2.0"


False


Operations that need the end raise UnknownLengthError, a ValueError that names the operation and the timeline, before they change anything. A group converts positions in proportion to its members’ lengths, so a conversion to or from a member of unknown length is one of them; appending a child at a parent’s end is another.

programme = ContinuousLogicalTimeline(length=Fraction(16), name="Programme")
broadcast = TimelineGroup(name="Broadcast", timelines=[programme, stream])
for operation in (
    lambda: broadcast.get_timestamp_at(Fraction(4), programme.id),
    lambda: stream.append_child(ContinuousPhysicalTimeline(length=10.0)),
):
    try:
        operation()
    except UnknownLengthError as error:
        print(f"UnknownLengthError: {error}")

UnknownLengthError: Cannot convert a position from 'clt_05m23yu04a4xh' to 'cpt_0qmf1es92eejz': the length of timeline 'cpt_0qmf1es92eejz' is unknown
UnknownLengthError: Cannot append a child: the length of timeline 'cpt_0qmf1es92eejz' is unknown


Once the length is known, setting it is an ordinary edit, and every operation is available again.

stream.length = 3600.0
stream.is_length_known, answers([broadcast.get_timestamp_at(Fraction(4), programme.id)])

(True,
 [{'clt_05m23yu04a4xh': IdCoordinate(Fraction(4, 1), quarters, 'clt_05m23yu04a4xh'),
   'cpt_0qmf1es92eejz': IdCoordinate(900.0, seconds, 'cpt_0qmf1es92eejz')}])

Events: to_dict(events=True) writes every timeline’s event rows into the dict; see How to Construct Timelines Manually. A bundle’s file names no event: to_file(events=True) writes its events into the registry beside the manifest, their content into one pre-parsed table per event type; see How to Write the Registry and Share Tables in a Package.
